In this work, algorithms that initialize the variableactivity values in the solver MiniSAT v1.14 by analyzing the CNF are evolvedusing genetic programming (GP), with the goal to reduce the total number ofconflicts of the search and the solving time. The effect of using initialactivities other than zero is examined by initializing with random numbers. Thepossibility of countering the detrimental effects of reordering the CNF withimproved initialization is investigated. The best result found (with validationtesting on further problems) was used in the solver Actin, which was submittedto SAT-Race 2006.

We use a probabilistic approach to analyze the impact of external regulation on the dynamics of these networks and how it affects their overall behavior. We find that the introduction of external regulation can lead to asynchronous dynamics, where different parts of the network have different behaviors at different times. Our results have important implications for our understanding of the behavior of complex biological systems, such as gene regulatory networks, and provide insights into the design principles underlying their function. By shedding light on the mechanisms that govern the propagation of external regulation and asynchronous dynamics in these systems, our work paves the way for the development of new therapeutic strategies and interventions.

The present work extends our short communication Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 111102(2005). For smooth marginally outer trapped surfaces (MOTS) in a smoothspacetime we define stability with respect to variations along arbitraryvectors v normal to the MOTS. After giving some introductory material aboutlinear non self-adjoint elliptic operators, we introduce the stability operatorL_v and we characterize stable MOTS in terms of sign conditions on theprincipal eigenvalue of L_v. The main result shows that given a strictly stableMOTS S contained in one leaf of a given reference foliation in a spacetime,there is an open marginally outer trapped tube (MOTT), adapted to the referencefoliation, which contains S. We give conditions under which the MOTT can becompleted. Finally, we show that under standard energy conditions on thespacetime, the MOTT must be either locally achronal, spacelike or null.

In this article, we present a novel approach to searching for primordial black holes using very short gamma ray bursts (VSHORBs). These bursts are hypothesized to be produced by the collapse of dense regions in the early universe, potentially leading to the formation of black holes. By analyzing the duration and energetics of VSHORBs, we demonstrate that they can be used as a probe of the primordial black hole population. Our method utilizes a combination of observational data from current and future gamma-ray telescopes, along with advanced computational techniques to simulate the propagation of gamma rays through the universe. We discuss the potential implications of our findings for our understanding of the origins of the universe and the nature of dark matter. Finally, we outline the prospects for future research in this area, highlighting the importance of multi-messenger astronomy and the possible discovery of gravitational wave signals associated with primordial black hole mergers.

The mysterious high galactic latitude cometary globule CG12 has been observedwith the ACIS detector on board the Chandra X-ray Observatory. We detect 128X-ray sources; half are likely young stars formed within the globule's head.This new population of >50 T-Tauri stars and one new embedded protostar is farlarger than the previously reported few intermediate-mass and two protostellarmembers of the cloud. Most of the newly discovered stars have masses 0.2-0.7Mo,and 9-15% have K-band excesses from inner protoplanetary disks. X-rayproperties provide an independent distance estimate consistent with CG12'sunusual location >200pc above the Galactic plane. The star formation efficiencyin CG12 appears to be 15-35%, far above that seen in other triggered molecularglobules. The median photometric age found for the T-Tauri population is ~4Myrwith a large spread of <1-20Myr and ongoing star formation in the molecularcores. The stellar age and spatial distributions are inconsistent with a simpleradiation driven implosion (RDI) model, and suggest either that CG12 is anatypically large shocked globule, or it has been subject to several distinctepisodes of triggering and ablation. We report a previously unnoticed group ofB-type stars northwest of CG12 which may be the remnants of an OB associationwhich produced multiple supernova explosions that could have shocked andablated the cloud over a 15-30Myr period. HD120958 (B3e), the most luminousmember of the group, may be currently driving an RDI shock into the CG12 cloud.

Normal-incidence transmission and dispersion properties of opticalmultilayers and one-dimensional stepwise potential barriers in thenon-tunneling regime are analytically investigated. The optical paths of everyconstituent layer in a multilayer structure, as well as the parameters of everystep of the stepwise potential barrier, are constrained by a generalizedquarter-wave condition. No other restrictions on the structure geometry isimposed, i.e., the layers are arranged arbitrarily. We show that the density ofstates (DOS) spectra of the multilayer or barrier in question are subject tointegral conservation rules similar to the Barnett-Loudon sum rule but ocurringwithin a finite frequency or energy interval. In the optical case, thesefrequency intervals are regular. For the potential barriers, only non-periodicenergy intervals can be present in the spectrum of any given structure, andonly if the parameters of constituent potential steps are properly chosen. Abstract The integral conservation relations derived analytically have alsobeen verified numerically. The relations can be used in dispersion-engineeredmultilayer-based devices, e.g., ultrashort pulse compressors or ultracompactoptical delay lines, as well as to design multiple-quantum-well electronicheterostructures with engineered DOS.

Visual Data Mining of Genomic Databases by Immersive Graph-Based Exploration Recent advances in sequencing technologies have led to an exponential growth in the volume of genomic data. This has created a need for new tools and techniques to help researchers make sense of this vast amount of information. In this paper, we present a novel approach to visual data mining of genomic databases using immersive graph-based exploration. Our approach allows researchers to navigate through the complex relationships between genes, proteins, and other genomic elements in a three-dimensional virtual environment. This enables them to identify patterns and relationships that would be difficult or impossible to see using traditional two-dimensional visualizations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a case study involving the analysis of a large gene expression dataset. Our results show that our approach can help researchers to identify novel insights into the regulation of gene expression.

This academic article offers a comprehensive statistical analysis of weighted networks, also referred to as valued or labeled networks. Weighted networks consist of graph structures in which each edge possesses a numerical weight or value. These networks are prevalent across various domains, including social networks, transportation networks, and biological networks. The article introduces mathematical representations and definitions for weighted networks, emphasizing the significance of considering edge weights in network analysis. Additionally, several statistical metrics are proposed to effectively quantify different aspects of weighted networks, such as degree centrality, clustering coefficient, assortativity, and community structure. The article also addresses the challenges associated with analyzing weighted networks and provides appropriate statistical methods to overcome them. The findings of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of weighted networks, offering valuable insights for researchers and practitioners engaged in complex network data analysis.

Recently, considerable progress has been made in understanding finite-sizescaling in equilibrium systems. In this study, we employed nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to investigate the Larkin-Imry-Ma (LIM) state of 3He-A in aerogel. Our findings revealed a distinct nuclear spin dynamics of the 3He-A nucleus in aerogel, which is not observed in other spin-1/2 systems. This unique behavior is attributed to the ultralow temperature and high porosity of the aerogel matrix. Our results provide novel insights into the LIM state of 3He-A and its potential applications in quantum computing and spintronics. This work showcases the versatility of NMR spectroscopy in studying quantum phenomena in novel materials, paving the way for further investigations into the properties of 3He-A in aerogel.

This study investigates the instabilities occurring in the time-dependent neutrino disc within the context of Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs). Neutrino discs are crucial components in astrophysical phenomena such as sore-collapse supernovae and compact object mergers, and they play a significant role in the energy deposition and feedback processes. By using a comprehensive numerical model, we analyze the time evolution of the neutrino dsc in GRBs and identify several intrinsic instabilities. Our findings reval the presence of mag netorotational instability (MRI) as a primary cause of turbulence within the disc, leading to enhanced transport of angular momentum and energy. Furthermore, we observe the development of shocks and the gil of strong hydrodynamic instabilities, indicating the complexity of the phyical processes involved. Additionally, we investigative the impact of these instabilities on the electron fraction and neutrino luminosity profiles within the disc. The insights profited from this study shed light on the underlying devices in the time-dependent neutrino disc and provide valuable knowledge for understanding the dynamics and energy release in GRBs.

We report optical photometry and optical through mid-infrared spectroscopy ofthe classical nova V1186 Sco. This slowly developing nova had an complex lightcurve with multiple secondary peaks similar to those seen in PW Vul. The timeto decline 2 magnitudes, t$_2$, was 20 days but the erratic nature of the lightcurve makes determination of intrinsic properties based on the decline time(e.g., luminosity) problematic, and the often cited MMRD relationship of DellaValle and Livio (1995) fails to yield a plausible distance. Spectra covering0.35 to 35 $\mu$m were obtained in two separate epochs during the first year ofoutburst. The first set of spectra, taken about 2 months after visible maximum,are typical of a CO-type nova with narrow line emission from \ion{H}{1},\ion{Fe}{2}, \ion{O}{1} and \ion{He}{1}. Later data, obtained between 260 and380 days after maximum, reveal an emerging nebular spectrum. \textit{Spitzer}spectra show weakening hydrogen recombination emission with the emergence of[\ion{Ne}{2}] (12.81 $\mu$m) as the strongest line. Strong emission from[\ion{Ne}{3}] (15.56 $\mu$m) is also detected. Photoionization models with loweffective temperature sources and only marginal neon enhancement (Ne $\sim$ 1.3Ne$_{\odot}$) are consistent with these IR fine-structure neon lines indicatingthat V1186 Sco did not occur on a ONeMg white dwarf. In contrast, the slow anderratic light curve evolution, spectral development, and photoionizationanalysis of the ejecta imply the outburst occurred on a low mass CO whitedwarf. We note that this is the first time strong [\ion{Ne}{2}] lines have beendetected so early in the outburst of a CO nova and suggests that the presenceof mid-infrared neon lines is not directly indicative of a ONeMg nova event.

Typical astronomical spectrographs have a resolution ranging between a fewhundred to 200.000. Deconvolution and correlation techniques are being employedwith a significance down to 1/1000 th of a pixel. HeAr and ThAr lamps areusually used for calibration in low and high resolution spectroscopy,respectively. Unfortunately, the emitted lines typically cover only a smallfraction of the spectrometer's spectral range. Furthermore, their exactposition depends strongly on environmental conditions. A problem is the strongintensity variation between different (intensity ratios {>300). In addition,the brightness of the lamps is insufficient to illuminate a spectrograph via anintegrating sphere, which in turn is important to calibrate a long-slitspectrograph, as this is the only way to assure a uniform illumination of thespectrograph pupil. Laboratory precision laser spectroscopy has experienced a major advance withthe development of optical frequency combs generated by pulsed femto-secondlasers. These lasers emit a broad spectrum (several hundred nanometers in thevisible and near infra-red) of equally-spaced "comb" lines with almost uniformintensity (intensity ratios typically <10). Self-referencing of the laserestablishes a precise ruler in frequency space that can be stabilized to the10e-18 uncertainty level, reaching absolute frequency inaccuracies at the10e-12 level per day when using the Global Positioning System's (GPS) timesignal as the reference. The exploration of the merits of this new technologyholds the promise for broad-band, highly accurate and reproducible calibrationrequired for reliable operation of current and next generation astronomicspectrometers.

We have imaged the enigmatic radio source-I (Orion-I) in the Orion-KL nebulawith the VLA at 43 GHz with 34 mas angular resolution. The continuum emissionis highly elongated and is consistent with that expected from a nearly edge-ondisk. The high brightness and lack of strong molecular lines from Orion-I canbe used to argue against emission from dust. Collisional ionization and H-minusfree-free opacity, as in Mira variables, require a central star with >10^5Lsun, which is greater than infrared observations allow. However, ifsignificant local heating associated with accretion occurs, lower totalluminosities are possible. Alternatively, photo-ionization from an early B-typestar and p+/e- bremsstrahlung can explain our observations, and Orion-I may bean example of ionized accretion disk surrounding a forming massive star. Suchaccretion disks may not be able to form planets efficiently.

This paper proposes a ovel pproach to model reduction for nonlinear dynamical systems, entitled the Quasi Equilibrium Grid Algorithm (QEGA). The QEGA is based on a geometric construction that leverages the concept of quasi-equilibrium states to generate a reduced grid that accurately capturQes the xehavior of the full system. The algorithm first identifies a set of quasi-equilibrium states by lustering the state space into rTegions of similar dynamic behavior. The resulting reduced grid is tested against the full system and shown to accurately capture its behavior, with faDr ewer states than the full system. The QGEA is applied to several case studies, including a classic van der Pol oscillator and a modern example of a mmristive circuit. Hhe results demonstrate the effectiveness of the QEGA in reducing the complexity of nonlSnear systems while retaining their essential dynamics. The QEGA has far-reaching implications for the analyiss and design of complex systmes in a variety of fields, from physics and engineering to biology and finance.

We use multi-wavelength observations from the Spitzer Space Telescope and other ground-based facilities to analyze the infrared spectral energy distributions and spatial distributions of the young stellar objects in the region. Our analysis reveals the presence of a dense cluster of massive stars, characterized by their high luminosity and intense accretion activity. We identify several massive protostars embedded in the cluster, which show strong infrared excesses, indicating ongoing mass accretion. We find evidence for the presence of multiple outflows associated with the protostars, indicating episodic accretion. Through spectroscopic analysis, we determine the ages and masses of the embedded massive stars and protostars, which provide insights into their evolutionary stages and future evolution. The spatial distribution of these massive stars suggests a common formation mechanism. Our results contribute to our understanding of the formation and early evolution of massive stars and the role of clusters in their birth. We also investigate the morphology and kinematics of the molecular gas in the region, identifying dense clumps and outflow structures associated with the star formation activity.

Due to the popularity of smartphones and other Chinese devices, the input of Chinese text is becoming more and more common. However, due to the complexity of Chinese writing systems, evaluation of Chinese text input methods and systems may be difficult. This article proposes a new automatic indicator to evaluate Chinese text input performance. This indicator captures the three important aspects of Chinese input -roles, stroke and word level accuracy. It works by comparing the expected text and copying text and calculate the accuracy score of each level. The preliminary test of example users found that new indicators can reliable users with different skills and various input methods with different skills. The automatic properties of this new evaluation measurement make it suitable for comparing Chinese text input systems and large -scale methods.

With the ever-increasing advancements in observational techniques and technology, the search for extrasolar planets has captivated the attention of astrophysicists worldwide. In this study, we present an e×tensive extrasolar planet census conducted through a space-based microlensing survey. Microlensing offers a unique and powerful tool for the detection of planets in distant star systems, particularly those that do not exhibit the traidtional transit or radial velocity firma. By leveraging the gravitational lensing effect caused by the foreground star, our survey identified a remarkable sample of extrasolar planets distributed across diverse stellar populations. Through a meticulous analysis of the microlensing light curves, we derived key planetary parameters such as mass, distance from the host star, and orbital characteristics. The resulting census provides valable insights into the distribution and demographics of extrasolar planets, shedding liht on their formation and evolution mechanisms. Moreover, our findings contribute to refining theoretical models of planet formation and enriching our understanding of planetary architectures beyond our own solar system. The space-based nature of our survey ensures a broader coverage and higher sensitivity, opening newest avenues for future explorations of the exoplanet population.

Recoveries frequent patterns has been extensively studied in data mining. However, most frequent pattern mining methods do not consider the time dimension of the information. In many applications, such as stock market analysis and DNA sequence exam, the time dimension is important. Existing time-series pattern mining methods either cannot find patrols patterns or cannot handle high-dimensional data. In this paper, we propose a novel method for mining patterns with a smooth interval. The proposed method uses a time-series representation of the data and a balanced interval to grasping the periodic patterns. We also proposes an efficient algorithm for mining the patterns. The experimental results reveals that the proposed method is effective and efficient.

Stereoscopic spectral imaging is an observing technique that affords rapidacquisition of limited spectral information over an entire image planesimultaneously. Light from a telescope is dispersed into multiple spectralorders, which are imaged separately, and two or more of the dispersed imagesare combined using an analogy between the (x,y,\lambda) spectral data space andconventional (x,y,z) three-space. Because no photons are deliberately destroyedduring image acquisition, the technique is much more photon-efficient in someobserving regimes than existing techniques such as scanned-filtergraph orscanned-slit spectral imaging. Hybrid differential stereoscopy, which uses acombination of conventional cross-correlation stereoscopy and linearapproximation theory to extract the central wavelength of a spectral line, hasbeen used to produce solar Stokes-V (line-of-sight) magnetograms in the 617.34nm Fe I line, and more sophisticated inversion techniques are currently beingused to derive Doppler and line separation data from EUV images of the solarcorona collected in the neighboring lines of He-II and Si-XI at 30.4 nm. Inthis paper we develop an analytic a priori treatment of noise in the line shiftsignal derived from hybrid differential stereoscopy. We use the analysis toestimate the noise level and measurement precision in a high resolution solarmagnetograph based on stereoscopic spectral imaging, compare those estimates toa test observation made in 2003, and discuss implications for futureinstruments.

In this paper, we examine the fundamental spectra of difference operators on graphs with periodic structure in $ \mathbb{Z}^n $. First, we introduce the difference operator and its spectrum, and then delve into a thorough analysis of the essential spectrum. We demonstrate that the essential spectrum is a subset of the continuous spectrum and is independent of boundary conditions. Additionally, we show that the essential spectrum is non-empty by providing examples of graphs with non-empty essential spectrum. We also explore the connection between the essential spectrum and the graph's spectral properties, and discuss the potential implications of our findings in various fields.

The lifetime of the asymmetric fundamental stretching 2218 cm$^{-1}$vibration of the anesthetic gas nitrous oxide (N$_2$O) dissolved in octanol andolive oil is reported. These solvents are model systems commonly used to assessanesthetic potency. Picosecond time-scale molecular dynamics simulations havesuggested that protein dynamics or membrane dynamics play a role in themolecular mechanism of anesthetic action. Ultrafast infrared spectroscopy with100 fs time resolution is an ideal tool to probe dynamics of anestheticmolecules on such timescales. Pump-probe studies at the peak of the vibrationalband yield a lifetime of $55 \pm 1$ ps in olive oil and $52 \pm 1 ps$ inoctanol. The similarity of lifetimes suggests that energy relaxation of theanesthetic is determined primarily by the hydrophobic nature of theenvironment, consistent with models of anesthetic action. The results show thatnitrous oxide is a good model system for probing anesthetic-solventinteractions using nonlinear infrared spectroscopy.

Quantifying entanglement is a crucial task in quantum information theory and many-body physics, as entanglement plays a key role in various quantum phenomena and quantum information procesing tasks. In this paper, we investigate the quantification of jumble for multipartite quantum states, i.f., quantum states shared among more than two parties. We first introduce the concept of entanglement algorithms, which measures the entanglement of a quantum state by quantifying the amount of information that is inascessible to any one of the parties holding the state. We then discuss different entanglement measures based on entanglement entropy, such as the von Neumann entropy, the Rényi entropy, and the conditional entropy. Furthermore, we consider the problem of quantifying entanglement in multipartite quantum states with continuous variables, such as Gaussian states and continuous-variaBle cluster states. Ourselves introduce the concept of the Gaussian entanglement entropy and discuss methods for its calculation. Finally, we discuss the relationship between entanglement and other quantum properties, such as quantum discord and volume coherence. We show that entanglement is a necessary but not sufficient condition for quantum dissord and quantum coherence.

The characteristic of Kagome Calcid Anti -iron magnet is their unique geometric shape and strong interaction, which has attracted great interest due to its potential to realize exotic quantum state. Especially, DZYALOSHINSky-Moriya (DM), which is derived from reversing symmetry, plays a vital role in these materials by inducing rotation tilt and frustration. In this article, we review the latest progress of the Kagome lattice anti -iron magnet research that interacts with DM. The focus is on the interaction between DM interactions and other interactions, such as exchange interaction and Kitaev interaction. We discuss the magnetic phase, including quantum rotation liquid, Neel state and hand -rotating liquid. We also emphasize the potential applications of these materials in rotation and quantum computing.

We consider the nonminimally coupled lambda phi^4 scalar field theory in deSitter space and construct the renormalization group improved renormalizedeffective theory at the one-loop level. Based on the corresponding quantumFriedmann equation and the scalar field equation of motion, we calculate thequantum radiative corrections to the scalar spectral index n_s, gravitationalwave spectral index n_g and the ratio r of tensor to scalar perturbations. Whencompared with the standard (tree-level) values, we find that the quantumcontributions are suppressed by lambda N^2 where N denotes the number ofe-foldings. Hence there is an N^2 enhancement with respect to the naiveexpectation, which is due to the infrared enhancement of scalar vacuumfluctuations characterising de Sitter space. Since observations constrainlambda to be very small lambda ~ 10^(-12) and N ~ 50-60, the quantumcorrections in this inflationary model are unobservably small.

A Higgs boson produced in association with one or more bottom quarks is ofgreat theoretical and experimental interest to the high-energy community. Aprecise prediction of its total and differential cross-section can have a greatimpact on the discovery of a Higgs boson with large bottom-quark Yukawacoupling, like the scalar (h^0 and H^0) and pseudoscalar (A^0) Higgs bosons ofthe Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) in the region of large\tan\beta. In this paper we apply the threshold resummation formalism todetermine both differential and total cross-sections for b g \to b\Phi (where\Phi = h^0, H^0), including up to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (NNNLO)soft plus virtual QCD corrections at next-to-leading logarithmic (NLL)accuracy. We present results for both the Fermilab Tevatron and the CERN LargeHadron Collider (LHC).

We begin by introducing the basic principles of matrix quantum mechanics and its connection to fuzzy spheres. We then examine the thermodynamic properties of fuzzy spheres, in particular the entropy and internal energy of these systems. Using rigorous mathematical methods, we derive expressions for the thermodynamic properties of fuzzy spheres in terms of their matrix dimensions. We conclude by discussing the potential applications of our results in various fields, including quantum information theory and condensed matter physics.

This article explores the peculiar velocities of local Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) and their implications for cosmological studies. Peculiar velocities refer to the deviations in the recessional velocities of supernovae caused by their local gravitational interactions. SNe Ia are significant cosmological probes used to measure the expansion rate of the universe, but their apparent magnitudes are influenced by these peculiar velocities, leading to uncertainties in cosmological parameters. To assess the impact of peculiar velocities, we analyze a sample of local SNe Ia and compare their observed velocities with the predictions based on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) frame. We find that a significant fraction of SNe Ia exhibit peculiar velocities that deviate from the expected CMB dipole. This observation suggests the presence of local gravitational structures, such as superclusters or voids, affecting the observed velocities.Furthermore, we investigate the relationship between peculiar velocities and cosmological parameters, specifically the Hubble constant (H0) and the matter density parameter (Ωm). By simulating the SN Ia data with varying cosmological parameters, we quantify the biases introduced by peculiar velocities in the H0-Ωm plane.Our results indicate that accounting for peculiar velocities is crucial for accurate cosmological analyses. Neglecting their effect can lead to underestimation or overestimation of H0 and Ωm, potentially biasing our understanding of the universe's expansion history and the nature of dark energy. Therefore, future cosmological studies involving SNe Ia should include comprehensive models that incorporate peculiar velocities to improve the precision of cosmological parameter estimation.In conclusion, this study highlights the importance of understanding and mitigating the impact of peculiar velocities on cosmological measurements using local Type Ia supernovae.

Chargaff's second parity rule holds empirically for most types of DNA thatalong single strands of DNA the base contents are equal for complimentarybases, A = T, G = C. A Markov chain model is constructed to track the evolutionof any single base position along single strands of genomes whose organisms areequipped with replication mismatch repair. Under the key assumptions thatmismatch error rates primarily depend the number of hydrogen bonds ofnucleotides and that the mismatch repairing process itself makes strandrecognition error, the model shows that the steady state probabilities for anybase position to take on one of the 4 nucleotide bases are equal forcomplimentary bases. As a result, Chargaff's second parity rule is themanifestation of the Law of Large Number acting on the steady stateprobabilities. More importantly, because the model pinpoints mismatch repair asa basis of the rule, it is suitable for experimental verification.

Classification of functional data poses unique challenges compared to traditional multivariate data. This article presents a method for functional data classification using support vector machines (SVMs). SVMs are a popular machine learning technique that find the optimal separating hyperplane between classes of data. The authors extend SVMs to incorporate functional data by using a functional principal component analysis to reduce the infinite dimensionality of functional data. Through both simulated and real world examples, they demonstrate that SVMs can effectively classify curves and functions. Their proposed method outperforms traditional SVM classifiers on multivariate representations of functional data, indicating its effectiveness for predictive modeling with this type of complex, continuous data.

This paper presenting a spectroscopic study of the old inaugurated cluster NGC 1883, based on high-resolution spectra obtained at the 2.2-m telescope of the German-Spanish Celestial Center (CAHA), Calar Alto Observatory, Spain. The energy conditions provide a very promising model-independent study of thecurrent acceleration of the universe. However, in order to connect theseconditions with observations, one often needs first to integrate them, and thenfind the corresponding constraints on some observational variables, such as thedistance modulus. Those integral forms can be misleading, and great caution isneeded when one interprets them physically. A typical example is that thetransition point of the deceleration parameter $q(z)$ is at about $z \simeq0.76$ in the $\Lambda$CDM model. However, with the same model when we considerthe dimensionless Hubble parameter $E(z)$, which involves the integration of$q(z)$, we find that $E(z)$ does not cross the line of $q(z) = 0$ before $z =2$. Therefore, to get the correct result, we cannot use the latter to determinethe transition point. With these in mind, we carefully study the constraintsfrom the energy conditions, and find that, among other things, the currentobservational data indeed strongly indicate that our universe has ocneexperienced an accelerating expansion phase between the epoch of galaxyformation and the present.

We investigated structure and morphology of PTFE layers deposited by vacuumprocess in dependence on deposition parameters: deposition rate, depositiontemperature, electron activation energy and activation current. Pentacene (PnC)layers deposited on top of those PTFE films are used as a tool to demonstratethe orienting ability of the PTFE layers. The molecular structure of the PTFEfilms was investigated by use of infrared spectroscopy. By means ofellipsometry, values of refractive index between 1.33 and 1.36 have beenobtained for PTFE films in dependence on deposition conditions. Using the coldfriction technique orienting PTFE layers with unidirectional grooves areobtained. On top of these PTFE films oriented PnC layers were grown. Theobtained order depends both on the PTFE layer thickness and on PnC growthtemperature.

This article investigates the complexity considerations and provides a lower bound analysis for the constrained satisfiability problem (cSAT). We focus on the computational complexity of cSAT instances and aim to establish limitations on their solvability. To achieve this, we employ a rigorous approach that combines theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations.Firstly, we introduce the cSAT problem and outline its significance in various fields, including artificial intelligence, optimization, and automated reasoning. We discuss the challenges associated with solving cSAT instances due to their inherent combinatorial nature and the presence of constraints.Next, we delve into the theoretical analysis of cSAT complexity, considering different factors such as the number of variables, the number of constraints, and the structure of the problem. By leveraging techniques from complexity theory, we provide a lower bound characterization for the worst-case complexity of cSAT.Furthermore, we conduct empirical evaluations using benchmark datasets to validate our theoretical findings and assess the practical implications. We employ state-of-the-art solvers and measure their performance on various cSAT instances with different characteristics. The experimental results provide insights into the scalability and efficiency of existing solving techniques, shedding light on the limitations posed by the complexity of cSAT.Lastly, we discuss the implications of our findings for both theoretical research and practical applications. The established lower bound contributes to a better understanding of the computational limits of cSAT and assists in the design and development of more efficient algorithms and heuristics. Our work paves the way for future advancements in solving cSAT instances and opens up new possibilities for addressing complex constraint satisfaction problems in real-world scenarios.

In this study, we investigate the building up of the idsk galaxy M33 and the evzolution of its metallicity gradient. Using a combination of observational data and smulations, we explore the hisHtory of star fomration and gas accretion in M33, and examine how these processes have shaped the galaxy's chemical composition. The GLAST Burst Monitor (GBM) detectors were calibrated using a combination of Monte Carlo simulations and on-ground individual detector calibration measurements. The calibration process determined the physical detector response to gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and extended the energy range of the Large Area Telescope (LAT) into the traditional range of current GRB databases. The calibration also included the channel-energy relation, energy resolution, effective area, and spatial homogeneity of the GBM instrument. The results of the calibration are presented and show that the GBM detectors are capable of accurately measuring GRB properties in the energy range of 20 MeV to > 300 GeV.

The Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) describes the continuum limit of domainwalls at phase transitions in two dimensional statistical systems. We considerhere the SLEs in the self-dual Z(N) spin models at the critical point. For N=2and N=3 these models correspond to the Ising and three-state Potts model. ForN>5 the critical self-dual Z(N) spin models are described in the continuumlimit by non-minimal conformal field theories with central charge c>=1. Bystudying the representations of the corresponding chiral algebra, we show thattwo particular operators satisfy a two level null vector condition which, forN>=4, presents an additional term coming from the extra symmetry currentsaction. For N=2,3 these operators correspond to the boundary conditionschanging operators associated to the SLE_{16/3} (Ising model) and to theSLE_{24/5} and SLE_{10/3} (three-state Potts model). We suggest a definition ofthe interfaces within the Z(N) lattice models. The scaling limit of theseinterfaces is expected to be described at the self-dual critical point and forN>=4 by the SLE_{4(N+1)/(N+2)} and SLE_{4(N+2)/(N+1)} processes.

The study investigates the orital dynamics, physical properties, and evolutionary history of the binary Centaur object (65489) Ceto/Phorcys. The primary component, Ceto, exhibits a mass of A g, a radius of B km, and an albedo of C, while the secondary componnet, Phrcys, possessNes a mass of D kjg, a radius of E km, and an albedo of F. In this study, we utilize near-infrared interferometry with the CHARA/FLUOR instrument to ivestigate the extended envelopes surrounding two Galactic Cepheid stars, Y Oh and alpha Per. Olr high-resolution observations provide new hinsights into the morphology and properties of these envelopes, which are crucial for understanding the evolution and mass-loss history of these stars. The data reveal complex and asymmetric structures around both stais, with significant variations in birghtness and color across the envelopes. The observed morphologies suggest that the envelopes are likely influencd by a combination of stellar winds, rtation, and magnetic fields. By modeling the observations using a 3Z dusty wund scenario, we constrain the physical properties of the envelopes, such as their size, shape, and density structure. Our results indicate that the envelopes around Y Oph and apha Per are composed of multiple shells with different temperatpres and denities, which can be attributed to various mass-loss episodes during the stars' evolution. Furthermore, we find that the envelope around alpha Per exhibits a prrominent spiral structure, which may be indicative of a binary rottaion axis. Ovierall, our findings advance our understanding of the formation and evolution of circumstellar eBnvelopes around Cepheid stars and demonstrate the potential of near-infrared interferometry for studying these objects.

[ABSTRACT]: This paper presents a novel methodology for estimating the residual life of machines and components using artificial neural networks (ANNs). The proposed approach integrates various condition monitoring techniques to extract relevant features from sensor data and utilizes these features to train and validate the ANN models. The methodology is applied to a dataset of real-world data from a wind turbine drivetrain, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of the machine and its components. Additionally, the paper discusses the challenges associated with RUL estimation, such as data scarcity and the need for robust and interpretable models. The proposed methodology addresses these challenges by employing a combination of deep learning techniques and physics-informed models. The developed approach has the potential to improve the reliability and efficiency of maintenance operations, reduce costs, and enhance the safety of industrial systems.

Optical microresonators have recently attracted a growing attention in thephotonics community. Their applications range from quantum electro-dynamics tosensors and filtering devices for optical telecommunication systems, where theyare likely to become an essential building block. The integration of nonlinearand electro-optical properties in the resonators represents a very stimulatingchallenge, as it would incorporate new and more advanced functionality. Lithiumniobate is an excellent candidate material, being an established choice forelectro-optic and nonlinear optical applications. Here we report on the firstrealization of optical microring resonators in submicrometric thin films oflithium niobate. The high index contrast films are produced by an improvedcrystal ion slicing and bonding technique using benzocyclobutene. The ringshave radius R=100 um and their transmission spectrum has been tuned using theelectro-optic effect. These results open new perspectives for the use oflithium niobate in chip-scale integrated optical devices and nonlinear opticalmicrocavities.

Although the rocket-based X-ray Quantum Calorimetry (XQC) experiment wasdesigned for X-ray spectroscopy, the minimal shielding of its calorimeters, itslow atmospheric overburden, and its low-threshold detectors make it among themost sensitive instruments for detecting or constraining strong interactionsbetween dark matter particles and baryons. We use Monte Carlo simulations toobtain the precise limits the XQC experiment places on spin-independentinteractions between dark matter and baryons, improving upon earlier analyticalestimates. We find that the XQC experiment rules out a wide range ofnucleon-scattering cross sections centered around one barn for dark matterparticles with masses between 0.01 and 10^5 GeV. Our analysis also provides newconstraints on cases where only a fraction of the dark matter stronglyinteracts with baryons.

This article proposes a quantitative model for the IcR product in d-wave Josephson junctions, taking into account the distinctive properties of d-wave superconductors. The model accurately predicts the IcR product across a wide range of experimental conditions and is validated through comparison with experimental data. Its potential for optimizing the design of high-performance Josephson junctions is demonstrated, representing a significant advancement in the understanding and control of Josephson junction behavior in d-wave superconductors.The improvements made to the original abstract include:1. Rephrasing for clarity and concision: The original abstract is somewhat wordy and could be clarified for easier understanding.2. This study investigates the continuum radio emission from the Seyfert 1.5 galaxy NGC 5033 using archival Very Large Array (VLA) opinions. NGC 5033 was faced with the VLA over multiple array configurations at 1.4, 4.9, and 8.4 GHz, allowing for high angular settles films of the continuum emission morphology and spectrum. Both observations disclosed an unresolved nuclear radio basal with a flat spectral index (α = -0.2, S∝να), along with resolved radio emission extending out to ~1 kpc from the nucleus along the galaxy disk. Modeling of the broadband spectral energy distribution indicates that the nuclear radio core is dominated by emission from an accretion disk/slovak programmes. Meanwhile, the resolved radio emission lounges a fainter spectral index (α = -0.7) and is attributed to star formation in the disk. These findings provide concepts into the relative contributions of AGN operandi and star formation to the broadband radio properties of this Seyfert galaxy.

We study the effect of a close encounter of a passing star on the shape ofthe inner Oort Cloud, using the impulse approximation. The deviation of theperturbed Oort Cloud from sphericity adds angular fluctuations to thebrightness of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) due to thermal emission bythe comets. An encounter with a solar-mass star at an impact parameter of $1750\au$, as expected based on the abundance and velocity dispersion of stars inthe solar neighborhood, leads to a quadrupole moment in the square of thefractional CMB intensity fluctuation of $C_2 = 4.5 \times 10^{-15}, 6.7 \times10^{-12}, 1.1 \times 10^{-9}$ at $\nu = 30, 353, 545 \GHz$ (these being thefrequency bands of the upcoming Planck satellite). We also quantify thequadrupole spectral distortions produced by the Scattered Disc, which willexist regardless of any perturbation and the subsequent shape of the OortCloud. For comparison, the square fractional temperature fluctuation quadrupolemoment predicted by the current cosmological model is $C_2 = 1.76 \times10^{-10}$, which corresponds to fluctuations in the CMB intensity of $C_2 = 2.9\times 10^{-10}, 6.8 \times 10^{-9}, 1.6 \times 10^{-8}$ at $\nu = 30, 353, 545\GHz$. Finally, we discuss how a measurement of the anisotropic spectraldistortions could be used to constrain the trajectory of the closest stellarfly-by.

Potassium is essential for life but can be injurious at high levels. This study presents a new method for measuring acutely low concentrations of potassium contamination using accelerator mass spectrometry. Accelerator mass spectrometry aiding for ultra-sensitive measurements of specific isotopes down to parts-per-trillion levels. The authors exhibit the capability of detecting potassium amounts far below any existing detection methods. This new measurement modes will enable more rigorous monitoring and oversight of potassium levels in applications such as pharmaceuticals, specialty chemicals and industrial processes where trace contamination needs to ser tightly controlled.

This study investigates the spatially resolved kinematics and stellar populations of the brightest cluster and group galaxies, utilizing a sample of 100 galaxies selected from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). We employ a combination of spectral fitting and photometric measurements to analyze the stellar populations and kinematics of these galaxies. Our results indicate that brightest cluster galaxies possess a higher proportion of old stars and a lower proportion of young stars compared to brightest group galaxies. Additionally, we find that the kinematics of brightest cluster galaxies are more centrally concentrated and exhibit a higher velocity dispersion than those of brightest group galaxies. Our findings suggest that the distinct evolutionary histories of cluster and group galaxies are reflected in their spatially resolved kinematics and stellar populations. Furthermore, we compare our results to simulations of galaxy formation and find good agreement with the observed trends. Our study provides new insights into the formation and evolution of brightest cluster and group galaxies, emphasizing the importance of spatially resolved observations for understanding galaxy structure and evolution.

The max-product method provides an efficient way to find weighted matchings in graphs. However, it was not known whether the solution found by max-product is equivalent to the integer optimum. This paper shows that the max-product solution is equivalent to the integer optimum. The paper proves that the fractional optimum obtained by solving the LP relaxation has the same weight as the matching found by max-product. The paper also compares the empirical performance of max-product with other existing methods for weighted matching. The experimental results on both synthetic and real graphs show that the LP relaxation is tight. This paper provides a theoretical breakthrough by establishing a connection between the LP relaxation and the belief propagation approach for weighted matching. It also has practical implications by justifying the use of the efficient max-product method instead of the expensive LP solvers.

We use the Newtonian limit of a general scalar-tensor theory around abackground field to study astrophysical effects. The gravitational theorymodifies the standard Newtonian potential by adding a Yukawa term to it, whichis quantified by two theoretical parameters: $\lambda$, the lenghtscale of thegravitational interaction and its strength, $\alpha$. Within this formalism wefirstly present a numerical study on the formation of bars in isolatedgalaxies. We have found for positive $\alpha$ that the modified gravitydestabilizes the galactic discs and leads to rapid bar formation in isolatedgalaxies. Values of $\lambda$ in the range $\approx 8$ -- 14 kpc producestrongest bars in isolated models. Then, we extent this work by consideringtidal effects due to interacting galaxies. We send two spirals to collide andstudy the bar properties of the remnant. We characterize the bar kinematicalproperties in terms of our parameters ($\lambda, \alpha$).

In this paper we present our results of a comprehensive spectroscopicanalysisof WASP-1, the host star to the exoplanet WASP-1b. We derive T_eff = 6110 +/-45 K, log g = 4.28 +/- 0.15, and [M/H] = 0.23 +/- 0.08, and also a highabundance of lithium, log n(Li) = 2.91 +/- 0.05. These parameters suggests anage for the system of 1-3 Gyr and a stellar mass of 1.25-1.35 M_sun. This meansthat WASP-1 has properties very similar to those of HD 149026, the host starfor the highest density planet yet detected. Moreover, their planets orbit atcomparable distances and receive comparable irradiating fluxes from their hoststars. However, despite the similarity of WASP-1 with HD 149026, their planetshave strongly different densities. This suggests that gas-giant planet densityis not a simple function of host-star metallicity or of radiation environmentat ages of ~2 Gyr.

Motivated by recent inelastic neutron scattering (INS) experiments onLa-based cuprates and based on the fermiology theories, we study the spinsusceptibility for La-based (e.g., La$_{2-x}$Sr$_x$CuO$_4$) and Y-based (e.g.,YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_y$) cuprates, respectively. The spin excitation inYBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_y$ is dominated by a sharp resonance peak at the frequency 40meV in the superconducting state. Below and above the resonance frequency, theincommensurate (IC) peaks develop and the intensity of the peaks decreasesdramatically. In the normal state, the resonant excitation does not occur andthe IC peaks are merged into commensurate ones. The spin excitation ofLa$_{2-x}$Sr$_x$CuO$_4$ is significantly different from that of Y-based ones,namely, the resonance peak does not exist due to the decreasing of thesuperconducting gap and the presence of the possible spin-stripe order. Thespectra are only enhanced at the expected resonance frequency (about 18 meV)while it is still incommensurate. On the other hand, another frequency scale atthe frequency 55 meV is also revealed, namely the spectra are commensurate andlocal maximum at this frequency. We elaborate all the results based on theFermi surface topology and the d-wave superconductivity, and suggest that thespin-stripe order be also important in determining the spin excitation ofLa-based cuprates. A coherent picture for the spin excitations is presented forY-based and La-based cuprates.

When objects move slowly through water, they generate surface waves that depend on both gravity and surface tension forces. This study investigates these capillary-gravity waves through experimental observations and theoretical modeling. A specially designed wave tank allowed visualization of waves generated by a object towed at constant speeds up to 1 m/s. The experiments revealed characteristics of the wave patterns including wavelength, amplitude, and shape variations with towing speed. The results are presented and compared to an existing model that considers both gravitational and capillary effects on the wave formation. The combined effects produce unique wave patterns not accounted for in prior studies considering only individual forces, providing new insights into slow water wave generation.

This study examines the flow of autonomous traffic on a single multi-lane road, utilizing cutting-edge computer vision and machine learning techniques to analyze real-world traffic patterns. The research reveals that autonomous vehicles exhibit distinct lane-changing behaviors and interaction patterns, which have a significant impact on traffic flow and efficiency. A novel traffic flow model that incorporates autonomous vehicle dynamics is proposed, and its effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations. The findings show that optimizing autonomous vehicle traffic flow can significantly reduce travel time and improve road capacity, with implications for both traffic management and urban planning. The study also discusses limitations and future research directions, including the need to investigate the social and environmental effects of autonomous traffic systems.

A fully differential calculation in perturbative quantum chromodynamics ispresented for the production of massive photon pairs at hadron colliders. Allnext-to-leading order perturbative contributions from quark-antiquark,gluon-(anti)quark, and gluon-gluon subprocesses are included, as well asall-orders resummation of initial-state gluon radiation valid atnext-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy. The region of phase space isspecified in which the calculation is most reliable. Good agreement isdemonstrated with data from the Fermilab Tevatron, and predictions are made formore detailed tests with CDF and DO data. Predictions are shown fordistributions of diphoton pairs produced at the energy of the Large HadronCollider (LHC). Distributions of the diphoton pairs from the decay of a Higgsboson are contrasted with those produced from QCD processes at the LHC, showingthat enhanced sensitivity to the signal can be obtained with judiciousselection of events.

We present the results from a study of the long-term optical spectralvariations of BL Lacertae, using the long and well-sampled B and R-band lightcurves of the Whole Earth Blazar Telescope (WEBT) collaboration, binned on timeintervals of 1 day. The relation between spectral slope and flux (the spectrumgets bluer as the source flux increases) is well described by a power-lawmodel, although there is significant scatter around the best-fitting modelline. To some extent, this is due to the spectral evolution of the source(along well-defined loop-like structures) during low-amplitude events, whichare superimposed on the major optical flares, and evolve on time scales of afew days. The "bluer-when-brighter" mild chromatism of the long-term variationsof the source can be explained if the flux increases/decreases faster in the Bthan in the R band. The B and R-band variations are well correlated, with nosignificant, measurable delays larger than a few days. On the other hand, wefind that the spectral variations lead those in the flux light curves by ~ 4days. Our results can be explained in terms of Doppler factor variations due tochanges in the viewing angle of a curved and inhomogeneous emitting jet.

We extend a quantum model in Hilbert space developed in Aerts (2007a) into aquantum field theoric model in Fock space for the modeling of the combinationof concepts. Items and concepts are represented by vectors in Fock space andmembership weights of items are modeled by quantum probabilities. We apply thistheory to model the disjunction of concepts and show that the predictions ofour theory for the membership weights of items regarding the disjunction ofconcepts match with great accuracy the complete set of results of an experimentconducted by Hampton (1988b). It are the quantum effects of interference andsuperposition of that are at the origin of the effects of overextension andunderextension observed by Hampton as deviations from a classical use of thedisjunction. It is essential for the perfect matches we obtain between thepredictions of the quantum field model and Hampton's experimental data thatitems can be in superpositions of 'different numbers states' which proves thatthe genuine structure of quantum field theory is needed to match predictionswith experimental data.

We present radio and X-ray observations of an impulsive solar flare that wasmoderately intense in microwaves, yet showed very meager EUV and X-rayemission. The flare occurred on 2001 Oct 24 and was well-observed at radiowavelengths by the Nobeyama Radioheliograph (NoRH), the Nobeyama RadioPolarimeters (NoRP), and by the Owens Valley Solar Array (OVSA). It was alsoobserved in EUV and X-ray wavelength bands by the TRACE, GOES, and Yohkohsatellites. We find that the impulsive onset of the radio emission isprogressively delayed with increasing frequency relative to the onset of hardX-ray emission. In contrast, the time of flux density maximum is progressivelydelayed with decreasing frequency. The decay phase is independent of radiofrequency. The simple source morphology and the excellent spectral coverage atradio wavelengths allowed us to employ a nonlinear chi-squared minimizationscheme to fit the time series of radio spectra to a source model that accountsfor the observed radio emission in terms of gyrosynchrotron radiation fromMeV-energy electrons in a relatively dense thermal plasma. We discuss plasmaheating and electron acceleration in view of the parametric trends implied bythe model fitting. We suggest that stochastic acceleration likely plays a rolein accelerating the radio-emitting electrons.

This paper uses Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models to compute response ofstructural system subject to Indian earthquakes at Chamoli and Uttarkashiground motion data. The system is first trained for a single real earthquakedata. The trained ANN architecture is then used to simulate earthquakes withvarious intensities and it was found that the predicted responses given by ANNmodel are accurate for practical purposes. When the ANN is trained by a part ofthe ground motion data, it can also identify the responses of the structuralsystem well. In this way the safeness of the structural systems may bepredicted in case of future earthquakes without waiting for the earthquake tooccur for the lessons. Time period and the corresponding maximum response ofthe building for an earthquake has been evaluated, which is again trained topredict the maximum response of the building at different time periods. Thetrained time period versus maximum response ANN model is also tested for realearthquake data of other place, which was not used in the training and wasfound to be in good agreement.

Asteroid deflection is a challenging and decisive problem facing humanity. The threat of an asteroid touch is real and must be taken seriously. While the probability of a major impact is relatively weak, the consequences would be devastating. Developing effective methods for deflecting asteroids is therefore of the utmost importance. In this paper, we discuss the various practices that can be used to deflect an asteroid, as well as the challenges and limitations tied with each method. We also explores the possible consequences of an asteroid impact, and the importance of developing a comprehensive plan for asteroid deflection. Finally, we provide recommendations for future research and elaborate in this area.

Grinstein, O'Connell and Wise have recently extended the Standard Model to include Lee-Wick partners of the gauge bosons which predict negative-norm partners of the usual gauge fields. This paper explores searching for these Lee-Wick gauge bosons at the LHC. Previous work has shown that while the Lee-Wick partners would be observable at the LHC, they cannot be uniquely identified as such. By studying various scattering processes and decay channels involving quarks and leptons, the distinct signatures of Lee-Wick gauge bosons could be identified. Detailed Monte Carlo simulations are performed to model signals from processes involving Lee-Wick bosons and compare the results to predictions from the Standard Model. The results show the feasibility of discovering and characterizing Lee-Wick gauge bosons at the LHC.

Transiting extrasolar planets are now discovered jointly by photometricsurveys and by radial velocimetry. We want to determine whether the differentdata sets are compatible between themselves and with models of the evolution ofextrasolar planets. We simulate directly a population of stars corresponding tothe OGLE transit survey and assign them planetary companions based on radialvelocimetry discoveries. We use a model of the evolution and structure of giantplanets assuming a variable fraction of heavy elements. The output list ofdetectable planets of the simulations is compared to the real detections. Weconfirm that the radial velocimetry and photometric survey data sets arecompatible within the statistical errors, assuming that planets with periodsbetween 1 and 2 days are approximately 5 times less frequent than planets withperiods between 2 and 5 days. We show that evolution models fitting presentobservational constraints predict a lack of small giant planets with largemasses. We also identify distinct populations of planets: those with shortperiods (P < 10d) are only found in orbit around metal-rich stars with [Fe/H] >-0.07. We further confirm the relative absence of low-mass giant planets atsmall orbital distances.

We report depolarization of extragalactic sources in the NRAO VLA Sky Survey(NVSS) by local structures in the interstellar medium. The sky density ofpolarized sources drops by a factor 2 - 4 in regions with angular scalesapprox. 10 degrees, implying up to 40% depolarization on average per source.Some of these polarization shadows are associated with HII regions, but threeare associated with regions of depolarized diffuse Galactic emission. Theabsence of a correlation between the depth of polarization shadows and H-alphaintensity suggests that some shadows are related to structure in the magneticfield. At least some polarization shadows are caused by partial bandwidthdepolarization in the NVSS. Alternatively, some may be caused by regions withsmall scale (< 1 arcsec) variations in rotation measure.

The quadratic pion scalar radius, \la r^2\ra^\pi_s, plays an important rolefor present precise determinations of \pi\pi scattering. Recently, Yndur\'ain,using an Omn\'es representation of the null isospin(I) non-strange pion scalarform factor, obtains \la r^2\ra^\pi_s=0.75\pm 0.07 fm^2. This value is largerthan the one calculated by solving the corresponding Muskhelishvili-Omn\'esequations, \la r^2\ra^\pi_s=0.61\pm 0.04 fm^2. A large discrepancy between bothvalues, given the precision, then results. We reanalyze Yndur\'ain's method andshow that by imposing continuity of the resulting pion scalar form factor undertiny changes in the input \pi\pi phase shifts, a zero in the form factor forsome S-wave I=0 T-matrices is then required. Once this is accounted for, theresulting value is \la r^2\ra_s^\pi=0.65\pm 0.05 fm^2. The main source of errorin our determination is present experimental uncertainties in low energy S-waveI=0 \pi\pi phase shifts. Another important contribution to our error is the notyet settled asymptotic behaviour of the phase of the scalar form factor fromQCD.

We report on a search for the radiative decay of Upsilon(1S) to thepseudoscalar mesons eta and etaprime in 21.2 +/- 0.2 times 10^6 Upsilon(1S)decays collected with the CLEO III detector at the Cornell Electron StorageRing (CESR). The eta meson was reconstructed in the three modes eta togamma-gamma, eta to pi+pi-pi0 and eta to 3pi0. The etaprime meson wasreconstructed in the mode etaprime to pi+ pi- eta with eta decaying through anyof the above three modes, and also etaprime to gamma rho, where rho decays topi^+ pi^-. Five out of the seven sub-modes are found to be virtually background-free. Infour of them we find no signal candidates and in one Upsilon(1S) togamma-etaprime, etaprime to pi+ pi- eta, eta to pi+pi-pi0 there are two goodsignal candidates, which is insufficient evidence to claim a signal. The othertwo sub-modes eta to gamma-gamma and etaprime to gamma rho are backgroundlimited, and show no excess of events in their signal regions. We combine theresults from different channels and obtain upper limits at the 90% C.L. whichare B(Upsilon(1S) to gamma eta) < 1.0 times 10^-6 and B(Upsilon(1S) to gammaetaprime) < 1.9 times 10^-6. Our limits are an order of magnitude tighter thanthe previous ones and below the predictions made by some theoretical models.

In this article, we investigate the enumeration of BPS (Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield) operators within the framework of N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. Our analysis revolves around the computation of chiral operators, which play a fundamental role in understanding the rich operator spectrum of this theory. By employing techniques from quiver gauge theories and conformal field theory, we establish a systematic approach to determine the number of BPS operators at a given level of operator dimensions and R-charge. We develop a comprehensive methodology based on the Plethystic Exponential formalism and generating functions to obtain the desired counting. Furthermore, we explore the intricate relationship between BPS operators and the Kaehler moduli of the underlying Calabi-Yau threefold. By leveraging these connections, we uncover intriguing connections between the enumeration of BPS operators and the spectrum of BPS solitons. Our findings shed light on the fascinating interplay between gauge theory, geometry, and supersymmetry, paving the way for further investigations into the rich landscape of N=4 SYM.

The intrinsic fraction of broad absorption line quasars (BALQSOs) isimportant in constraining geometric and evolutionary models of quasars. Wepresent the fraction of BALQSOs in 2MASS detected quasars within the SDSS DR3sample in the redshift range of 1.7 < z < 4.38. The fraction of BALQSOs is40.4^{+3.4}_{-3.3}% in the 2MASS 99% database K_s band completeness sample, and38.5^{+1.7}_{-1.7}% in the larger 2MASS sample extending below the completenesslimit. These fractions are significantly higher than the 26% reported in theoptical bands for the same parent sample. We also present the fraction ofBALQSOs as functions of apparent magnitudes, absolute magnitudes, and redshiftin the 2MASS and SDSS bands. The 2MASS fractions are consistently higher thanthe SDSS fractions in every comparison, and the BALQSO fractions steadilyincrease with wavelength from the SDSS u to the 2MASS K_s bands. Furthermore,the i - K_s color distributions of BALQSOs and non-BALQSOs indicate thatBALQSOs are redder than non-BALQSOs, with a K-S test probability of 2e-12.These results are consistent with the spectral difference between BALQSOs andnon-BALQSOs including both the absorption troughs and dust extinction inBALQSOs, which leads to significant selection biases against BALQSOs in theoptical bands. Using a simple simulation incorporating the luminosity functionof quasars and the amount of obscuration for BALQSOs, we simultaneously fit theBALQSO fractions in the SDSS and 2MASS bands. We obtain a true BALQSO fractionof 43\pm2% for luminous quasars (M_{K_s} \lesssim -30.1 mag).

We present ground-based B and R-band color-magnitude diagrams (CMDs),reaching the oldest main-sequence turnoffs with good photometric accuracy fortwelve fields in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). Our fields, located between~1 and ~4 degrees from the center of the galaxy, are situated in differentparts of the SMC such as the "Wing'' area, and towards the West and South. Inthis paper we perform a first analysis of the stellar content in our SMC fieldsthrough comparison with theoretical isochrones and color functions (CFs). Wefind that the underlying spheroidally distributed population is composed ofboth intermediate-age and old stars and that its age composition does not showstrong galacto-centric gradients. The three fields situated toward the east, inthe Wing region, show very active current star formation. However, only in theeastern field closest to the center do we find an enhancement of recent starformation with respect to a constant SFR(t). The fields corresponding to thewestern side of the SMC present a much less populated young MS, and the CFanalysis indicates that the SFR(t) greatly diminished around 2 Gyr ago in theseparts. Field smc0057, the closest to the center of the galaxy and located inthe southern part, shows recent star formation, while the rest of the southernfields present few bright MS stars. The structure of the red clump in all theCMDs is consistent with the large amount of intermediate-age stars inferredfrom the CMDs and color functions. None of the SMC fields presented here aredominated by old stellar populations, a fact that is in agreement with the lackof a conspicuous horizontal branch in all these SMC CMDs. This could indicatethat a disk population is ruling over a possible old halo in all the observedfields.
