The proposed method uses advanced signal processing technology and machine learning algorithm to locate multiple AE sources at the same time. The proposed methods include three main stages. First, the signal pre -processing is performed to improve the quality of the AE signal obtained and extract related functions. This pre -processing step aims to reduce noise and enhance the detection of a single AE event. Secondly, a new type of cluster algorithm is used to group similar AE events according to its space and time characteristics. By gathering the AE event, the algorithm aims to determine the sources in the overall record signal. Finally, use a localized algorithm based on machine learning to estimate the space coordinates of each recognized AE source. In order to verify the proposed method, a wide range of experiments were conducted using the simulation environment with multiple AE sources. The results show that even if there is noise and overlapping signals, the proposed method can accurately locate multiple AE sources. The comparative analysis of the existing positioning technology further establishes the advantages of proposed methods, in terms of accuracy and robustness. At the same time, the intelligent location of AE sources is of great significance for structural health monitoring and damage assessment. By accurately locating multiple AE sources, the location and severity of the damage to the structure or material can be accurately determined.

This study is concerned with the diffusion of a passive scalar $\Theta(\r,t)$advected by general $n$-dimensional shear flows $\u=u(y,z,...,t)\hat{x}$ havingfinite mean-square velocity gradients. The unidirectionality of theincompressible flows conserves the stream-wise scalar gradient,$\partial_x\Theta$, allowing only the cross-stream components to be amplifiedby shearing effects. This amplification is relatively weak because an importantcontributing factor, $\partial_x\Theta$, is conserved, effectively rendering aslow diffusion process. It is found that the decay of the scalar variance$<\Theta^2>$ satisfies $d<\Theta^2>/dt\ge -C\kappa^{1/3}$, where $C>0$ is aconstant, depending on the fluid velocity gradients and initial distribution of$\Theta$, and $\kappa$ is the molecular diffusivity. This result generalizes toaxisymmetric flows on the plane and on the sphere having finite mean-squareangular velocity gradients.

The temperature and doping dependence of the upper critical field was investigated by a combination of experimental techniques, including resistivity and magnetization measurements. Our results show that the upper critical field has a distinct behavior in the underdoped and overdoped regimes, indicating significant differences in the superconducting properties of the materials. Through a comprehensive analysis, we discuss the implications of these results for the underlying mechanism of superconductivity in $La_2xSr_xCuO_4$ compounds, and shed light on the relationship between doping, critical fields, and the nature of the superconducting state in these high-T_c superconductors.

Numerous ongoing experiments aim at detecting WIMP dark matter particles fromthe galactic halo directly through WIMP-nucleon interactions. Once such adetection is established a confirmation of the galactic origin of the signal isneeded. This requires a direction-sensitive detector. We show that such adetector can measure the velocity anisotropy beta of the galactic halo.Cosmological N-body simulations predict the dark matter anisotropy to benonzero, beta~0.2. Baryonic matter has beta=0 and therefore a detection of anonzero beta would be strong proof of the fundamental difference between darkand baryonic matter. We estimate the sensitivity for various detectorconfigurations using Monte Carlo methods and we show that the strongest signalis found in the relatively few high recoil energy events. Measuring beta to theprecision of ~0.03 will require detecting more than 10^4 WIMP events withnuclear recoil energies greater than 100 keV for a WIMP mass of 100 GeV and a32S target. This number corresponds to ~10^6 events at all energies. We discussvariations with respect to input parameters and we show that our method isrobust to the presence of backgrounds and discuss the possible improvedsensitivity for an energy-sensitive detector.

We present a general numerical scheme for the practical implementation ofstatistical moment closures suitable for modeling complex, large-scale,nonlinear systems. Building on recently developed equation-free methods, thisapproach numerically integrates the closure dynamics, the equations of whichmay not even be available in closed form. Although closure dynamics introducestatistical assumptions of unknown validity, they can have significantcomputational advantages as they typically have fewer degrees of freedom andmay be much less stiff than the original detailed model. The closure method canin principle be applied to a wide class of nonlinear problems, includingstrongly-coupled systems (either deterministic or stochastic) for which theremay be no scale separation. We demonstrate the equation-free approach forimplementing entropy-based Eyink-Levermore closures on a nonlinear stochasticpartial differential equation.

We present results from a study of the distances and distribution of a sampleof intermediate-age clusters in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Using deepnear-infrared photometry obtained with ISPI on the CTIO 4m, we have measuredthe apparent K-band magnitude of the core helium burning red clump stars in 17LMC clusters. We combine cluster ages and metallicities with the work ofGrocholski & Sarajedini to predict each cluster's absolute K-band red clumpmagnitude, and thereby calculate absolute cluster distances. An analysis ofthese data shows that the cluster distribution is in good agreement with thethick, inclined disk geometry of the LMC, as defined by its field stars. Wealso find that the old globular clusters follow the same distribution,suggesting that the LMC's disk formed at about the same time as the globularclusters, ~ 13 Gyr ago. Finally, we have used our cluster distances inconjunction with the disk geometry to calculate the distance to the LMC center,for which we find (m-M)o = 18.40 +/- 0.04_{ran} +/- 0.08_{sys}, or Do = 47.9+/- 0.9 +/- 1.8 kpc.

In Chile and Uruguay,the gregarious Pteromalidae (Monoksa dorsiplana) hasbeen discovered emerging from seeds of the persistent pods of Acacia cavenattacked by the univoltin bruchid Pseudopachymeria spinipes. We investigatedthe potential for mass rearing of this gregarious ectoparasitoid on analternative bruchid host, Callosobruchus maculatus, to use it against thebruchidae of native and cultured species of Leguminosea seeds in South America.The mass rearing of M.dorsiplana was carried out in a population cage where thedensity of egg-laying females per infested seed was increased from 1:1 on thefirst day to 5:1 on the last (fifth) day. Under these experimental conditionsegg-clutch size per host increased, and at the same time the mortality of eggslaid also increased. The density of egg-laying females influenced the sex ratiowhich tended towards a balance of sons and daughters,in contrast to the sexratio of a single egg-laying female per host (1 son to 7 daughters). The meanweight of adults emerging from a parasitized host was negatively correlatedwith the egg-clutch size, i.e., as egg-clutch size increased, adult weightdecreased. All these results show that mass rearing of the gregariousectoparasitoid M.dorsiplana was possible under laboratory conditions on analternative bruchid host C.maculatus. As M.dorsiplana is a natural enemy oflarval and pupal stages of bruchidae, the next step was to investigate whetherthe biological control of bruchid C.maculatus was possible in an experimentalstructure of stored beans.

We present a study of the interacting binary systems AE Aqr, BV Cen, and V426 Oph, which comprise a cool star and a white dwarf. To characterize the cool stars, we obtained near-infrared images with adaptive optics, optical images with lucky imaging, and Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations. The relative astrometry of the components was determined using the shift-and-add technique. The near-infrared images reveal an unresolved source near the white dwarf, which is likely the cool star. The angular separations between the components are 28.4±1.3, 15.1±0.5, and 6.5±0.5 mas in AE Aqr, BV Cen, and V426 Oph, respectively. We estimated the physical parameters of the systems, including the masses, radii, and effective temperatures of the cool stars. We find that the cool stars have masses of 0.63±0.13, 0.73±0.08, and 1.10±0.05 Msun, radii of 1.03±0.26, 0.96±0.23, and 1.30±0.21 Rsun, and effective temperatures of 3890±190, 4690±150, and 5010±130 K in AE Aqr, BV Cen, and V426 Oph, respectively. Using the near-infrared color-magnitude diagram, we derived the evolutionary status of the cool stars, which are post-mass transfer stars close to the terminal-age main sequence.

We investigate the interaction between antibaryons (Dbar) and nucleon (N) using different theoretical omdels. Previous studies have largely relied on meson-exchange modQls to describe the forces between Dbar and N at hadronic scales. pIn this work, we develop a quantum chromodynamics motivated model that incorporates quark and gluon degrees of freedom to accounY for Dbar-N dynamics from a more fundamental perspective. Our model calculates csattering Lmplitudes by representing the Dbar and N as valance quarks embedded in a sea of quasi-free gluons. Preliminary results indicate that quark-gluon effects produce an Battractive Dbar-N potential comparable in strength to meson exchanges at intermediate dsitances. Precise measurements of Dbar-N scattering could help discriminate between the meson-exchaneg and quark-gluon descriptions of the interaction and provide ew insights into the role of quarks and gluons in baryoTnic systems.

Level Hilbert functions have been increasingly studied due to their applications in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. This paper explores interval conjectures formulated by Herzog and Kuhl concerning the possible values of level Hilbert functions over the integers. In particular, the conjectures state that for any s, t in N with s ≤ t, there exists a standard graded algebra A over a field K such that the level Hilbert function of A is s in degree 0 and t in degree 1. The authors introduce new families of algebras and examine their level Hilbert functions to provide evidence supporting these conjectures. Computations of level Hilbert functions are performed for the class of codimension 3 perfect ideals of points in P^3, building on previously known results. Obstructions to the existence of certain level Hilbert functions are also investigated. The presented examples and counterexamples provide further insight into the behavior of these numerical invariants. While progress is made, the full interval conjectures remain open problems. Additional families of algebras are proposed for further study to continue advancing understanding of level Hilbert functions and the conjectured bounds.

Moving gap solitons are a fascinating phenomenon that has garenred significant attention in recent years. In this article, we explore the behavior of moving gap solitons in periodic potentials, uWsing a combination of analytical and numerical methoSds. We show that the presence of a periodic potential can signifciantly affect the dynamics of gap solitons, leading to the formation of staele moing solitons that can persist for long times. These moving solitons can exhibit complex spatial and tepmoral patterns, and we demonstrate their potential for use in various applications, including the control of nonlinear waves and the creation of novel opticUal kffects. Oru results provide new insights into the ebhavior of gap solitons in periodic potentials and have important implications for the study of nonlinear waves in a varietO of physical systems.

The dynamical Casimir effect occurs when vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory produce real specks from a boundary undergoing nonuniform acceleration. Previous studies have modeled this effect using approximate methods that did not fully consider its inherently relativistic nature. This paper presents a physically sounds Hamiltonian formulation of the dynamical Casimir effect for a massless scalar field with a time-dependent boսndary condition in 1+1 dimensions. The formulation is based on standard canonical quantization of a relativistic scalar field in terms of creation and extinction operators. Equations of motion for the field operators are derived and exact solutions for particle creation are obtained in terms of Bogoliubov coefficients. It is shown that the number of created particles can be computed unambiguously from the Hamiltoinan and agrees with results from other formalisms under appropriate limits. Notably, this approach allows the backreaction of created particles on the boundary dynamics to be incorporated self-consistently. The new formulation provides a technically rigorous foundation for studying effects like particle establishment across accelerating mirrors and their applications in analog gravity systems.

The SSIPM is based on semiparametric regression and uses penalized likelihood estimation to achieve efficient model fitting. The SSIPM is designed to handle complex relationships between predictors and the response variable by introducing spline functions and a single-index structure. The use of spline functions allows for flexible modeling of nonlinear relationships, while the single-index structure reduces dimensionality and enhances interpretability. The proposed model is evaluated using simulated data and real-world data from various domains, including finance and health care. The results show that the SSIPM outperforms competing methods in terms of prediction accuracy and model interpretability. In general, the SSIPM is a flexible and powerful tool for prediction modeling, which strikes a balance between interpretability and accuracy in complex data analysis tasks.

We study a lattice realization of a Luttinger liquid interacting with a bathof quantum spins in terms of an antiferromagnetic S=1/2 Heisenberg chain, whereeach spin is also coupled to a \sigma=1/2 Kondo spin degree of freedom. Thismodel describes the low-energy spin dynamics in quasi one dimensionalmaterials, where the electronic spins of the magnetic ions interact with thoseof impurities, nuclei and possibly other spin species present in theirenvironment. For large ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo interaction J'there are two phases corresponding to an effective spin-1 Heisenberg chain anda dimerised spin-1/2 ladder, respectively. For weak Kondo interaction weestablish that the Kondo interaction drives the system to a strong couplingregime. This suggests that J'=0 is the only critical point in the system.

Characteristic scales of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in redshift-space, such as the sound horizon scale at the drag epoch \(r_d\) and the baryon acoustic scale \(r_{BAO}\) are essential standard rulers for precision cosmology. Using perturbation theory, we investigate the effects of non-linear evolution and redshift-space distortions (RSD) on these scales up to one-loop order. We find that the RSD effect causes a \(1.46\%\) enhancement to the \(r_d\) scale. At the same time, non-linear evolution induces a \(3.25\%\) enhancement to \(r_{BAO}\). Our results reveal that both effects are not negligible and should be carefully considered in future cosmic distance measurements and cosmological parameter inferences using BAO. In addition, we provide fitting formulae for the redshift-space distortion parameter \(f\) and the dilation factor \(D\), which quantify the RSD and non-linear effects, respectively. The fitting formulae with simple forms can be conveniently employed in the cosmological analyses of BAO measurements.

We compute the two-loop corrections to the world-sheet sigma model describing type IIB superstring theory on AdS5 x S5. Using the pure spinor formalism, we explicitly evaluate the determinant of the Laplacian appearing in the one-loop effective action. This determines the two-loop counterterm needed to cancel divergences in the path integral. We find additional finite contributions to the beta functions of coupling constants in the corresponding low-energy effective string action. The results agree with expectactions from integrability and match previous computations in the light-cone gauge. This high-loop world-sheet computation in a covariant formalism is an important check of the AdS/CFT correspondence beyond the leading order.

This paper introduces a new technique for building hierarchical grid spatial indexes using image processing. A grid is overlaid on the spatial data region, assigning unique color values to each cell. Data points are then located within cells and their positions recorded. The grid image recursively subdivides until cells contain zero or one point. This creates an index equivalent to traditional hierarchical space partitioning trees. Query performance is evaluated on real and synthetic point and region datasets, showing the image index matches existing hierarchical grid indexes in size and efficiency. Implementing the index through image processing simplifies creation while enabling parallelization and GPU acceleration opportunities. The approach is well-suited for large-scale spatial data requiring efficient querying on embedded or mobile devices with constrained resources. In summary, an image-based methodology forms novel hierarchical grid spatial indexes from source datasets through recursive subdivision and cell color encoding.

Cosmic shear constrains cosmology by exploiting the apparent alignments ofpairs of galaxies due to gravitational lensing by intervening mass clumps.However galaxies may become (intrinsically) aligned with each other, and withnearby mass clumps, during their formation. This effect needs to bedisentangled from the cosmic shear signal to place constraints on cosmology. Weuse the linear intrinsic alignment model as a base and compare it to analternative model and data. If intrinsic alignments are ignored then the darkenergy equation of state is biased by ~50 per cent. We examine how the numberof tomographic redshift bins affects uncertainties on cosmological parametersand find that when intrinsic alignments are included two or more times as manybins are required to obtain 80 per cent of the available information. Weinvestigate how the degradation in the dark energy figure of merit depends onthe photometric redshift scatter. Previous studies have shown that lensing doesnot place stringent requirements on the photometric redshift uncertainty, solong as the uncertainty is well known. However, if intrinsic alignments areincluded the requirements become a factor of three tighter. These results arequite insensitive to the fraction of catastrophic outliers, assuming that thisfraction is well known. We show the effect of uncertainties in photometricredshift bias and scatter. Finally we quantify how priors on the intrinsicalignment model would improve dark energy constraints.

We consider the problem of quantization of classical soliton integrablesystems, such as the KdV hierarchy, in the framework of a general formalism ofGaudin models associated to affine Kac--Moody algebras. Our experience with theGaudin models associated to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras suggeststhat the common eigenvalues of the mutually commuting quantum Hamiltonians in amodel associated to an affine algebra should be encoded by affine opersassociated to the Langlands dual affine algebra. This leads us to some concretepredictions for the spectra of the quantum Hamiltonians of the soliton systems.In particular, for the KdV system the corresponding affine opers may beexpressed as Schroedinger operators with spectral parameter, and ourpredictions in this case match those recently made by Bazhanov, Lukyanov andZamolodchikov. This suggests that this and other recently found examples of thecorrespondence between quantum integrals of motion and differential operatorsmay be viewed as special cases of the Langlands duality.

Given a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel, feedback from thereceiver can be used to specify a transmit precoding matrix, which selectivelyactivates the strongest channel modes. Here we analyze the performance ofRandom Vector Quantization (RVQ), in which the precoding matrix is selectedfrom a random codebook containing independent, isotropically distributedentries. We assume that channel elements are i.i.d. and known to the receiver,which relays the optimal (rate-maximizing) precoder codebook index to thetransmitter using B bits. We first derive the large system capacity ofbeamforming (rank-one precoding matrix) as a function of B, where large systemrefers to the limit as B and the number of transmit and receive antennas all goto infinity with fixed ratios. With beamforming RVQ is asymptotically optimal,i.e., no other quantization scheme can achieve a larger asymptotic rate. Theperformance of RVQ is also compared with that of a simpler reduced-rank scalarquantization scheme in which the beamformer is constrained to lie in a randomsubspace. We subsequently consider a precoding matrix with arbitrary rank, andapproximate the asymptotic RVQ performance with optimal and linear receivers(matched filter and Minimum Mean Squared Error (MMSE)). Numerical examples showthat these approximations accurately predict the performance of finite-sizesystems of interest. Given a target spectral efficiency, numerical examplesshow that the amount of feedback required by the linear MMSE receiver is onlyslightly more than that required by the optimal receiver, whereas the matchedfilter can require significantly more feedback.

In this study, we investigate the potential impact of non-standard neutrino interactions (NSIs) on the properties of neutrinos emitted during supernova events. We employ a comprehensive theoretical framework and analyze observational data to assess the potential existence and influence of NSIs. Through detailed simulations and statistical analyses, we demonstrate that NSIs can significantly modify the neutrino emission spectra and alter the flavor conversion patterns within the dense and complex environment of a supernova. Our findings provide crucial insights into the existence of NSIs and their implications for our understanding of neutrino physics and astrophysical phenomena.

We present a new catalog of galaxy peculiar velocities derived using the I-band Tully-Fisher relation. The catalog, tered SFI++ II, contains measurements and uncertainties for over 3000 spiral galaxies. Distances were estimated from 21 cm line widths and integrated I-band magnitudes. Peculiar velocities and unsertainties were measured with respect to a model of the cosmic microwave background dipole. Overall, our results are in agreement with the predictions of the standard cosmological model inside the measurement uncertainties. This new dataset will provide strong constraints on models of the dynamics and mass distribution in the local universe.

The simulation of the border layer between the white dwarf and its accumulation disk was given. The boundary layer is the area where the disk is accumulated to the white dwarf. It is expected to be turbulent and generate X -rays. Simulation uses two -dimensional, time -dependent fluid power code. The results show that the boundary layer is highly changed in time, and the optical light of X -ray changes accordingly. The simulation also shows that the boundary layer is the source of quality loss of white dwarves.

In this analyze, we present a user-friendly code designed to facilitate the diagnosis of chromospheric plasmas in solar observations. The chromosphere is a significance region of the solar atmosphere that plays a significant role in various proactive processes and energy transport mechanisms. However, accurately characterizing and study chromospheric plasmas has remained a challenging task due to their complex and dynamic nature. Our code dealing this challenge by providing a comprehensive and accessible tool for the diagnosis of chromospheric plasmas. It incorporates pinnacle computational algorithms that leverage multi-wavelength observations to derive considerable plasma parameters such as temperature, density, and velocity. Moreover, the encoder includes intuitive graphical interfaces and interactive features, entitles users to visualize and explore the diagnostic results in a user-friendly manner. We demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the code through a series of case studies, showcasing its potential to helps to our understands of chromospheric plasma dynamics and its claimant in solar physics research.

Latest data on charmless strange vector-pseudoscalar $B^+$ decays nowincluding $B^+\to \rho^+ K^o$ confirm a simple penguin model in which the gluon$G$ in an initial $\bar s u G$ state fragments equally into $u \bar u$, $d \bard$ and $s \bar s$ and all form factors are equal. A search for possibleadditional contributions shows only a few signals not obscured by experimentalerrors whose implications are discussed. The experimental value of $0.25 \pm0.11$ for the ratio of the branching ratios $BR(B^+ \to K^{ +}\eta)$ to$BR(B^+\to K^{ +}\eta')$ confirms the parity selection rule prediction 0.32.Large violations arise in a new sum rule for the sum of these branching ratios,analogous to the similar pseudoscalar sum rule including $K^+\eta$ and$K^+\eta'$. Indications for either an electroweak penguin contribution oradditional admixtures like instrinsic charm in the $\eta-\eta'$ system remainto be clarified. An alternative symmetry description with new predictive powerclarifies the simple penguin approximation and presents new predictions whichcan be tested experimentally. The fragmentation of the $\bar s u G$ state intotwo mesons is described by a strong interaction S-matrix dominated by nonexotichadron resonances in multiparticle intermediate states.

With an aim towards understanding the time-dependence of entanglement entropyin generic quantum field theories, we propose a covariant generalization of theholographic entanglement entropy proposal of hep-th/0603001. Apart fromproviding several examples of possible covariant generalizations, we study aparticular construction based on light-sheets, motivated in similar spirit tothe covariant entropy bound underlying the holographic principle. Inparticular, we argue that the entanglement entropy associated with a specifiedregion on the boundary in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence is given bythe area of a co-dimension two bulk surface with vanishing expansions of nullgeodesics. We demonstrate our construction with several examples to illustrateits reduction to the holographic entanglement entropy proposal in staticspacetimes. We further show how this proposal may be used to understand thetime evolution of entanglement entropy in a time varying QFT state dual to acollapsing black hole background. Finally, we use our proposal to argue thatthe Euclidean wormhole geometries with multiple boundaries should be regardedas states in a non-interacting but entangled set of QFTs, one associated toeach boundary.

The LIGO and Virgo Scientific Collaboration conducted the second locate for gravitational wave gunshot, called IGEC-2, operate data from early 2005. This scoured boost upon previous all-sky searches by utilizing data from the upgraded LIGO and Virgo detectors which had increased sensitivity. The IGEC-2 search analyzed data from approximately 100 hours of coincident observation minute between the LIGO and Virgo detectors. No colossal gravitational wave candidates were identified in the analyzed data. Upper limits were established on the rate of gravitational surges bursts as a function of assumed signal strength. These upper limits improved upon past IGEC burst scrutinize and help constrain various astrophysical source models. Additionally, strengthened in detector sensitivity and network operation were demonstrated and will be critical for improving the capabilities of future international gravitational wave burst search. Overall, the IGEC-2 search validated the international gravitational-wave network and pushed forward the quest to discover gravitational waves use interferometric detectors.

In this paper the travelling wave solutions in the adiabatic model withtwo-step chain branching reaction mechanism are investigated both numericallyand analytically in the limit of equal diffusivity of reactant, radicals andheat. The properties of these solutions and their stability are investigated indetail. The behaviour of combustion waves are demonstrated to have similaritieswith the properties of nonadiabatic one-step combustion waves in that there isa residual amount of fuel left behind the travelling waves and the solutionscan exhibit extinction. The difference between the nonadiabatic one-step andadiabatic two-step models is found in the behaviour of the combustion wavesnear the extinction condition. It is shown that the flame velocity drops downto zero and a standing combustion wave is formed as the extinction condition isreached. Prospects of further work are also discussed.

In response to the proposed high helium content stars as an explanation forthe double main sequence observed in Omega Centauri, we investigated theconsequences of such stars elsewhere on the color-magnitude diagram. Weconcentrated on the horizontal branch where the effects of high helium areexpected to show themselves more clearly. In the process, we developed aprocedure for comparing the mass loss suffered by differing stellar populationsin a physically motivated manner. High helium stars in the numbers proposedseem absent from the horizontal branch of Omega Centauri unless their mass losshistory is very different from that of the majority metal-poor stars. It ispossible to generate a double main sequence with existing Omega Centauri starsvia accretion of helium rich pollution consistent with the latest AGB ejectatheoretical yields, and such polluted stars are consistent with the observed HBmorphology of Omega Centauri. Polluted models are consistent with observedmerging of the main sequences as opposed to our models of helium rich stars.Using the (B-R)/(B+V+R) statistic, we find that the high helium bMS starsrequire an age difference compared to the rMS stars that is too great, whereasthe pollution scenario stars have no such conflict for inferred Omega Centaurimass losses.

Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods such as Gibbs sampling are commonly used to sample from complex high-dimensional distributions. However, Gibbs sampling can mix slowly on graphs with strong structural dependencies between variables. This article analyzes the mixing time of Gibbs sampling on graphs where the average node degree grows slowly as the number of nodes increases. It is shown that under certain conditions on the growth rate of the average degree, Gibbs sampling will rapidly explore the state space. These conditions allow for graphs that are sparse on average but locally dense. Numerical experiments on stochastic block models verify that Gibbs sampling can rapidly draw approximately independent samples even when the graph is not locally tree-like. The theoretical results establish rapid mixing in a setting that generalizes sparse graphs with bounded degrees. This work provides insight into when MCMC methods may effectively samplefrom distributions defined on large graphs with complex dependencies between variables.

The Chandra Comet Survey represents a comprehensive observational investigation of comets utilizing the Chandra X-ray Observatory. In this study, we present the outcomes of a spectral analysis undertaken on the data collected from the Chandra Comet Survey over a span of three years. Our main objective was to examine the X-ray spectra of comets and explore the physical processes accountable for X-ray emission in these celestial bodies.Employing sophisticated data reduction techniques, we extracted the X-ray spectra of a subset of comets from the Chandra Comet Survey dataset. Detailed spectral modeling was performed to characterize the emission lines and continuum features evident in the spectra. Our analysis revealed a diverse range of spectral properties, encompassing distinctive emission lines from highly ionized ions as well as continuum emission from thermal and non-thermal processes.Furthermore, we investigated the connection between X-ray emission and the characteristics of cometary nuclei, including size, composition, and activity level. We observed variations in X-ray emission among different comets, indicating dissimilarities in the prevailing physical conditions and processes. Additionally, a comparison was made between our findings and previous X-ray observations of comets from other missions, revealing both similarities and differences and emphasizing the significance of multi-wavelength investigations.Moreover, we examined the temporal behavior of X-ray emission from comets, striving to detect any transient events or variations. A few instances of short-duration flares and variability in X-ray flux were identified, suggesting temporal evolution in cometary X-ray emission occurring across various timescales. These findings yield valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms steering X-ray emission in comets and contribute to our comprehension of the physics governing these cometary bodies.

This article introduces a new method of encoding through a network distribution source, focusing on minimizing transmission costs. The methods we propose uses advanced compression technology and network coding strategies to achieve significantly reduced transmission costs, while maintaining high -level data quality and accuracy. Through simulation and theoretical analysis, we have proved the effectiveness of the method and showed that it is better than traditional methods in terms of cost and performance. Our discovery is of great significance for extensive applications, including multimedia streams, wireless sensor networks and distributed data storage systems. In addition, our approach aims to expand and adapt to various network configurations, so that it has made valuable contributions to the field of distributed source coding.

We propose a new spin transfer device, which has an integrated dynamic polarizer for generating a polarized rotation current. Essence The device consists of a plane multi -layer structure, which has iron magnetic and non -magnetic layers made of sputtering deposits. The transition metal layer acts as a polarizer, and its magnetization direction can be reversed by electrical chemicals. Numerical simulation indicates that exerting voltage on a multi -layer structure will generate spin polarizer current that can switch the freedom magnetized magnetization. The prototype experiments indicate that the freedom layer between the parallel state and the anti -parallel state of the low working voltage and the anti -parallel state. This dynamic reconfigured self -rotation transfer device can enable new methods for spin memory and logical applications.

Radiative transfer plays an important role in star formation as energy from young stars heats and influences the surrounding gas and dust. This study aims to implement radiative transfer using the energy equation in smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations of star formation. A new method is presented for integrating the energy equation with radiative transfer terms into the SPH formalism. Test simulations are conducted of isolated spheres undergoing gravitational collapse with heating from an embedded protostar. The results are compared to analytical solutions and previous studies. The new method captures the overall dynamical evolution and thermal structure in good agreement with previous work, demonstrating the potential of the approach for future simulations investigating feedback effects in more complex star-forming regions.

This study resolves a long-standing problem in nuclear physics by providing a novel approach that simultaneously corrects the nucleon density and momentum distributions in nuclei for center-of-mass motion. Previous studies have only separately addressed these corrections. Our method, which applies to various nuclei with different mass numbers and charge radii, is based on a modified version of the traditional nuclear fluid approach and includes a center-of-mass correction term in the momentum equation. The results show that the simultaneous center-of-mass correction notably improves the agreement between theory and experiment, particularly for the momentum distribution of neutrons in light nuclei. This study underscores the significance of accounting for nucleon center-of-mass motion in understanding nuclear structure and reactions. The approach can be widely applied, offering valuable insights into nucleon behavior in nuclei. (

In this article, we demonstrate the current-induced switching of a single-molecule magnet (SMM) with an arbitrary oriented easy axis. We show that the magnetic moment of the SMM can be controlled by the direction of the current flowing through the molecule, leading to a switchable magnetic state. Our results indicate that the switching mechanism is driven by the spin-dependent transport properties of the molecule and the conduction electrons in the leads. We demonstrate the versatility of our approach by showing that the SMM can be switched on and off repeatedly, and that the switching efficiency can be optimized by tailoring the molecular structure and the current pulse parameters.

Suprathreshold stochastic resonance (SSR) is a form of noise enhanced signaltransmission that occurs in a parallel array of independently noisy identicalthreshold nonlinearities, including model neurons. Unlike most forms ofstochastic resonance, the output response to suprathreshold random inputsignals of arbitrary magnitude is improved by the presence of even smallamounts of noise. In this paper the information transmission performance of SSRin the limit of a large array size is considered. Using a relationship betweenShannon's mutual information and Fisher information, a sufficient condition foroptimality, i.e. channel capacity, is derived. It is shown that capacity isachieved when the signal distribution is Jeffrey's prior, as formed from thenoise distribution, or when the noise distribution depends on the signaldistribution via a cosine relationship. These results provide theoreticalverification and justification for previous work in both computationalneuroscience and electronics.

The CALICE collaboration is presently constructing a test hadron calorimeter(HCAL) with 7620 scintillator tiles read out by novel photo-detectors - SiliconPhotomultipliers (SiPMs). This prototype is the first device which uses SiPMson a large scale. We present the design of the HCAL and report on measuredproperties of more than 10 thousand SiPMs. We discuss the SiPM efficiency,gain, cross-talk, and noise rate dependence on bias voltage and temperature,including the spread in these parameters. We analyze the reasons for SiPMrejection and present the results of the long term stability studies. The firstmeasurements of the SiPM radiation hardness are presented. We compareproperties of SiPM with the properties of similar devices, MRS APD and MPPC. Apossibility to make the tiles thinner and to read them out without WLS fibershas been studied.

How can a microorganism adapt to a variety of environmental conditionsdespite there exists a limited number of signal transduction machineries? Weshow that for any growing cells whose gene expression is under stochasticfluctuations, adaptive cellular state is inevitably selected by noise, evenwithout specific signal transduction network for it. In general, changes inprotein concentration in a cell are given by its synthesis minus dilution anddegradation, both of which are proportional to the rate of cell growth. In anadaptive state with a higher growth speed, both terms are large and balanced.Under the presence of noise in gene expression, the adaptive state is lessaffected by stochasticity since both the synthesis and dilution terms arelarge, while for a non-adaptive state both the terms are smaller so that cellsare easily kicked out of the original state by noise. Hence, escape time from acellular state and the cellular growth rate are negatively correlated. Thisleads to a selection of adaptive states with higher growth rates, and modelsimulations confirm this selection to take place in general. The resultssuggest a general form of adaptation that has never been brought to light - aprocess that requires no specific machineries for sensory adaptation. Thepresent scheme may help explain a wide range of cellular adaptive responsesincluding the metabolic flux optimization for maximal cell growth.

The Brjuno function \(\alpha(z)\) associated to an irrational number \(\alpha\) and introduced by A. D. Brjuno in the early 1970s is a key tool in the modern theory of Diophantine approximations. The aim of this paper is to introduce and study a natural generalization of the classical Brjuno function in the setting of so-called \(\alpha\)-continued fractions. The basic properties of the generalized Brjuno functions and their connections with Diophantine approximation are investigated in detail. In particular, it is shown that the generalized Brjuno function naturally associated with an arbitrary Pisot number coincides with the classical Brjuno function. This fact enables us to obtain a new characterization of Pisot numbers as well as some related results.

The authors apply three methods of prospective modelling to high resolutiongeoreferenced land cover data in a Mediterranean mountain area: GIS approach,non linear parametric model and neuronal network. Land cover prediction to thelatest known date is used to validate the models. In the frame ofspatial-temporal dynamics in open systems results are encouraging andcomparable. Correct prediction scores are about 73 %. The results analysisfocuses on geographic location, land cover categories and parametric distanceto reality of the residues. Crossing the three models show the high degree ofconvergence and a relative similitude of the results obtained by the twostatistic approaches compared to the GIS supervised model. Steps under work arethe application of the models to other test areas and the identification ofrespective advantages to develop an integrated model.

We explore connections between Dyson indices from random matrix theory and separability functions used to compute separability probabilities under the Hilbert-Schmidt metric. Separability functions characterize the separable states as functions of parameters in particular parameterizations of the density matrix space. We analyze separability functions for real, complex, and quaternionic qubit-qubit systems using the Bloore parameterization and find relationships between the powers of the functions that match the Dyson indices. These relationships allow using the separability functions to conjecture exact formulas for the Hilbert-Schmidt separability probabilities. The conjectured probabilities closely follow behaviors predicted by Dyson indices. Further analyses of other parameterizations and higher-dimensional systems may help establish more separability probability conjectures adhering to Dyson index behaviors.

[Abridged] The WIde-field Nearby Galaxy-cluster Survey (WINGS) is a projectaiming at the study of the galaxy populations in clusters in the local universe(0.04<z<0.07) and the influence of environment on the physical properties ofgalaxies. This survey provides a high quality set of spectroscopic data for~6000 galaxies in 48 clusters. A salient feature of this model is thepossibility of treating dust extinction as a function of age, allowing youngerstars to be more obscured than older ones. Our technique, for the first time,takes into account this feature in a spectral fitting code. A set of templatespectra spanning a wide range of star formation histories is built, withfeatures closely resembling those of typical spectra in our sample in terms ofspectral resolution, noise and wavelength coverage. Our method of analyzingthese spectra allows us to test the reliability and the uncertainties relatedto each physical parameter we are inferring. The well-known degeneracy problem,i.e. the non-uniqueness of the best fit solution (mass and extinction indifferent age bins), can be addressed by assigning adequate error bars to therecovered parameters. The values found in this way, together with their errorbars, identify the region of parameter space which contains all the possiblesolutions for a given spectrum. A comparison test was also performed on a WINGSsubsample, containing objects in common with the Sloan Digital Sky Survey,yielding excellent agreement. We find that the stellar content as a function ofage is reliably recovered in four main age bins and that the uncertainties onlymildly depend on the S/N ratio. The metallicity of the dominant stellarpopulation is not always recoverable unambiguosly, depending on the StarFormation History pattern.

The main goal of this work is to investigate the possibility of finding thesupersymmetric version of the U(1)-global string model which behaves as avortex-superfluid. To describe the superfluid phase, we introduce aLorentz-symmetry breaking background that, in an approach based onsupersymmetry, leads to a discussion on the relation between the violation ofLorentz symmetry and explicit soft supersymmetry breakings. We also study therelation between the string configuration and the vortex-superfluid phase. Inthe framework we settle down in terms of superspace and superfields, weactually establish a duality between the vortex degrees of freedom and thecomponent fields of the Kalb-Ramond superfield. We make also considerationsabout the fermionic excitations that may appear in connection with the vortexformation.

Quantum enhancement of optical pulse timing accuracy is investigated in theHeisenberg picture. Effects of optical loss, group-velocity dispersion, andKerr nonlinearity on the position and momentum of an optical pulse are studiedvia Heisenberg equations of motion. Using the developed formalism, the impactof decoherence by optical loss on the use of adiabatic soliton control forbeating the timing standard quantum limit [Tsang, Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 023902(2006)] is analyzed theoretically and numerically. The analysis shows that anappreciable enhancement can be achieved using current technology, despite anincrease in timing jitter mainly due to the Gordon-Haus effect. The decoherenceeffect of optical loss on the transmission of quantum-enhanced timinginformation is also studied, in order to identify situations in which theenhancement is able to survive.

Scanning-probe spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for investigating the electronic properties of materials at the nanoscale. In this study, we utilize scanning-probe spectroscopy to probe the electronic properties of semiconductor donor molecules, which are crucial for understanding their potential applications in electronic devices. By using a sharp probe to scan the surface of a semiconductor material, we are able to detect the presence of donor molecules and map their distribution with high spatial resolution. Our results show that the electronic properties of the donor molecules are strongly influenced by their environment, with the presence of nearby atoms and molecules significantly affecting their electronic spectra. We also observe interesting phenomena such as electron-hole pairs and excitons, which are critical for understanding the optical properties of the material. Our findings demonstrate the potential of scanning-probe spectroscopy for studying the electronic properties of semiconductor donor molecules and their role in the development of novel electronic devices.

In this paper, we explore the possibility of detecting non-trivial topologies in the universe using cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. We present a new method for analyzing CMB data that takes into account the curvature of the universe and the possible presence of topological defects. Our approach uses a combination ofbispectrum estimators and Bayesian inference to constrain the parameters of the universe and detect signs of non-trivial topologies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method using simulated CMB data and show that it can successfully detect topologies that would be missed by traditional methods. Our results have important implications for our understanding of the universe's structure and evolution, and may lead to new insights into the nature of gravity and the origins of the universe.

According to a given title, this is a summary of the request: The interaction between the interaction between chemistry and mechanics in mechanical signal transition to biochemical functions is the basic process of biology. This review focuses on the molecular mechanism that converts mechanical forces into biochemical signals, focusing on the role of cell skeleton. Cell skeleton is a dynamic network of protein filaments and small tubes, which can provide structural support for cells and play a key role in cell division, migration and adhesion. Mechanical power deforms cells, which can trigger a biochemical signal pathway. For example, the application of mechanical forces in cells will cause activation of the ERK MAP kinase pathway. ERK MAP kinase pathway participates in various cell processes, including cell growth, differentiation and apoptosis.

We derive the light-front wave function of the three-quark state and analyze its spin properties using both numerical and analytical methods. Our results reveal the intricate interplay between the spin dynamics of the quarks and the $qqq$ force, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms that govern the structure of baryons in the framework of QCD. The results of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the fundamental aspects of hadron structure and may have implications for future experimental investigations.

It has been shown that a decentralized relay selection protocol based onopportunistic feedback from the relays yields good throughput performance indense wireless networks. This selection strategy supports a hybrid-ARQtransmission approach where relays forward parity information to thedestination in the event of a decoding error. Such an approach, however,suffers a loss compared to centralized strategies that select relays with thebest channel gain to the destination. This paper closes the performance gap byadding another level of channel feedback to the decentralized relay selectionproblem. It is demonstrated that only one additional bit of feedback isnecessary for good throughput performance. The performance impact of varyingkey parameters such as the number of relays and the channel feedback thresholdis discussed. An accompanying bit error rate analysis demonstrates theimportance of relay selection.

This paper considers the propagation of shallow-water solitary and nonlinearperiodic waves over a gradual slope with bottom friction in the framework of avariable-coefficient Korteweg-de Vries equation. We use the Whitham averagingmethod, using a recent development of this theory for perturbed integrableequations. This general approach enables us not only to improve known resultson the adiabatic evolution of isolated solitary waves and periodic wave trainsin the presence of variable topography and bottom friction, modeled by theChezy law, but also importantly, to study the effects of these factors on thepropagation of undular bores, which are essentially unsteady in the systemunder consideration. In particular, it is shown that the combined action ofvariable topography and bottom friction generally imposes certain globalrestrictions on the undular bore propagation so that the evolution of theleading solitary wave can be substantially different from that of an isolatedsolitary wave with the same initial amplitude. This non-local effect is due tononlinear wave interactions within the undular bore and can lead to anadditional solitary wave amplitude growth, which cannot be predicted in theframework of the traditional adiabatic approach to the propagation of solitarywaves in slowly varying media.

This paper presents the search for direct photons from AuAu collisions at a center-of-mass energy of \(\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200 \) GeV using a new \(\pi^0\) tagging method in the PHENIX experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). Direct photons are a valuable probe of the Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP), a deconfined state of matter created in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. They are produced in the early stages of the collision and can escape the QGP without significant interactions, carrying information about the temperature and the collective flow of the medium. The new \(\pi^0\) tagging method utilizes the electromagnetic calorimeter (EMCal) in PHENIX to identify and reject \(\pi^0\)s, which are a significant background for direct photons. The analysis is performed on data collected in the 2014 RHIC beam energy scan program. The measured direct photon spectra and the nuclear modification factor are compared to theoretical model calculations and the results from other experiments. The comparison provides valuable insights into the properties of the QGP and the photon production mechanisms in heavy-ion collisions.

In this paper we analyse the effect produced by the temperature in the vacuumpolarization associated with charged massless scalar field in the presence ofmagnetic flux tube in the cosmic string spacetime. Three differentconfigurations of magnetic fields are taken into account: $(i)$ a homogeneousfield inside the tube, $(ii)$ a field proportional to $1/r$ and $(iii)$ acylindrical shell with $\delta$-function. In these three cases, the axis of theinfinitely long tube of radius $R$ coincides with the cosmic string. Becausethe complexity of this analysis in the region inside the tube, we consider thethermal effect in the region outside. In order to develop this analysis, weconstruct the thermal Green function associated with this system for the threeabove mentioned situations considering points in the region outside the tube.We explicitly calculate in the high-temperature limit, the thermal average ofthe field square and the energy-momentum tensor.

This article examines the concept of projective Hilbert space structures in the context of exceptional points, which are singular locations in parameter space where non-Hermitian quantum systems display unique behavior. By utilizing the projective Hilbert space formalism, an extension of the standard Hilbert space framework, we investigate the geometric and topological characteristics of exceptional points. Our analysis provides a comprehensive examination of the projective Hilbert space structures associated with various types of exceptional points, including diabolic points, exceptional rings, and exceptional surfaces. We illustrate how these projective Hilbert space structures serve as effective mathematical tools for describing and comprehending the behavior of quantum systems in proximity to exceptional points. Additionally, we discuss the implications of these findings across multiple disciplines, such as wave physics, optics, and quantum information processing, underscoring the potential applications of projective Hilbert space structures in these domains. This research significantly contributes to the theoretical framework of non-Hermitian physics and enhances our understanding of the fundamental properties exhibited by exceptional points in quantum systems.

In this article, we investigate the action of the absolute Galois group on the moduli space of surfaces of general type. We show that the Galois group operates faithfully on the set of connected components of this moduli space, and that for each element of the Galois group, there exists a surface with a non-isomorphic fundamental group. Our result is a generalization of a previous theorem by Belyi, who showed that the Galois group acts faithfully on the set of smooth projective curves over an algebraic closure of the rational numbers. We demonstrate the faithfulness of the Galois action by constructing explicit examples of surfaces with non-isomorphic fundamental groups that are Galois conjugate. Our work provides a new perspective on the study of the moduli space of surfaces and its relationship to the absolute Galois group.

This article investigates the simultaneous occurrence of superconductivity and magnetic order in CeRhIn$_{5}$, with a focus on the characterization of their spectral properties. By employing various experimental techniques, including neutron scattering and specific heat measurements, we delve into the interplay between these two intriguing phenomena within a single material. Our findings unveil the existence of a distinct energy gap in the superconducting state, serving as evidence for the formation of Cooper pairs. Additionally, the magnetic spectrum exhibits notable features associated with spin fluctuations, which shed light on the origin and nature of the magnetic order in CeRhIn$_{5}$. Through a meticulous analysis of the coexisting spectral signatures, we elucidate the intricate relationship between superconductivity and magnetic order in this unique compound, thus contributing to a profound comprehension of their interconnected behavior in strongly correlated electron systems.

First principles calculations were performed to study the ground stateelectronic properties of BaFeO3 (BFO) within the density functional theory(DFT). Adopting generalized gradient approximation (GGA) exchange andcorrelation functional and Vosko-Wilk-Nusair correlation energy functionalinterpolation, we have systematically conducted the band structure, density ofstates and electronic distribution along different crystalline planes.Calculating results show that band gap in the majority spin band structure andband gap in the minority spin band structure were found to be 2.7012 eV and0.6867 eV respectively. Up-spin Fe t2g were fully occupied and down-spin Fe egwere empty. Moreover, the up-spin Fe eg and down-spin Fe t2g were partiallyoccupied near the Fermi energy, leading to a finite density of states. TheFe4+-O-Fe4+ plane superexchange coupling should rearrange the magnetic order tomake the ferromagnetic characteristic being possible, moreover the tetragonaldisplacement along the c axis could induce the perovskites materials to acquireferroelectric property. These reasons could lead to the fact that thetetragonal phase BFO could be a potential multiferroics while it was producedunder the very experimental conditions. The charge density along differentcrystalline planes were illustrated to show that strong covalent bondingbetween O and Fe can be used to investigate the exchange coupling, and thisstrong hybridization may further increase the superexchange coupling to enhancethe magnetic ordering.

In this paper, we consider the teleparallel version of the stationary axisymmetric replies in the context of Einstein's general theory of relativity. By considering the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity, known as teleparallel severity, we scrutinized the implications of this alternative framework on the solutions that describe stationary axisymmetric spacetimes. Fundamentally, using the energy-momentum complex, we calculate the energy densities and angular momenta of the teleparallel stationary axisymmetric solutions. Our analysis reveals intriguing differences between the two mode, shedding light on the underlying nature of gravity and the role of teleparallelism in describing stationary axisymmetric arrangement. Through detailed mathematical derivations and numerical computations, we demonstrate the validity and significance of our visualizing. Our results contribute to the ongoing discussions in gravitation teachings and provide a greater understanding of the teleparallel framework as an alternative to general relativity. Finally, we discuss the broader implications of our research, including the potential observational signe or experimental review that could distinguish between the predicts of teleparallel gravity and those of general relativity. This work opens up new avenues for exploring the nature of greatness and encourages further investigations into the intriguing objects of teleparallel spacetimes.

Using scaled-particle theory for binary mixtures of two-dimensional hardparticles with rotational freedom, we analyse the stability of nematic phasesand the demixing phase behaviour of a variety of mixtures, focussing on caseswhere at least one of the components consists of hard rectangles or hardsquares. A pure fluid of hard rectangles may exhibit, aside from the usualuniaxial nematic phase, an additional (tetratic) oriented phase, possessing twodirectors, which is the analogue of the biaxial or cubatic phases in three-dimensional fluids. There is computer simulation evidence that the tetraticphase might be stable with respect to phases with spatial order for rectangleswith low aspect ratios. As hard rectangles are mixed with other particles notpossessing stable tetratic order by themselves, the tetratic phase isdestabilised, via a first- or second-order phase transition, to uniaxialnematic or isotropic phases; for hard rectangles of low aspect ratio tetraticorder persists in a relatively large range of volume fractions. The order ofthese transitions depends on the particle geometry, dimensions andthermodynamic conditions of the mixture. The second component of the mixturehas been chosen to be hard discs or disco-rectangles, the geometry of which isdifferent from that of rectangles, leading to packing frustration and demixingbehaviour, or simply rectangles of different aspect ratio. These mixtures maybe good candidates for observing thermodynamically stable tetratic phases inmonolayers of hard particles. Finally, demixing between fluid(isotropic--tetratic or tetratic--tetratic) phases is seen to occur in mixturesof hard squares of different sizes when the size ratio is sufficiently large.

This paper presents an experimental gravimetric result supporting the revival of corpuscular theory. The result is based on a novel measurement of the gravitational force between objects of differing mass. The measurement demonstrates that the gravitational force is proportional to an object's mass, aligning with corpuscular theory. This result contrasts with the classical theory of gravity, predicting a proportionality between gravitational force and the square of an object's mass. The study's findings have implications for understanding gravity's nature and the structure of matter.

Gibbs sampling is a commonly used technique for sampling distributions on graphs. Previous work has shown that Gibbs sampling mixes rapidly for coloring on the Erdös-Rényi random graph G(n,d/n) when the number of colors is large enough depending on the average degree d. However, the behavior of Gibbs sampling for coloring on other families of graphs that are sparse on average was not well understood. In this article, we study the mixing time of Gibbs sampling for coloring on more general classes of graphs that have average degree d but may have diverse degree distributions. We prove that Gibbs sampling mixes rapidly in polynomial time on such graphs as long as the number of colors is sufficiently large, extending previous results on Erdös-Rényi graphs. Our analysis techniques allow for very general graph families and interactions beyond just coloring. As examples, we show our results also imply rapid mixing for the hard-core model at low fugacity and other models with soft constraints at high temperatures on these graph families. To our knowledge, this provides the first analysis of Gibbs sampling for the coloring model on general classes of sparse average graphs beyond just Erdös-Rényi random graphs.

Unparticles as suggested recently by Georgi have surprising phenomenologicalimplications, distinctive from any other new physics that we know of. But theymust interact very feebly with ordinary matter to have avoided detection thusfar. We determine how feebly they can interact with the electron, using theprecisely measured quantities in QED: the electron g-2 and the bounds oninvisible and exotic positronium decays. The most stringent bound comes frominvisible ortho-positronium decays: the effective energy scale entering thevector unparticle-electron interaction must exceed 4 x 10^5 TeV for a scalingdimension 3/2 of the vector unparticle. The lower bounds on scales for otherunparticles range from a few tens to a few hundreds TeV. This makes thedetection of unparticles challenging in low energy electron systems.
