We experimentally investigate the fluctuations in height or roughness inherent to undoped monoatomic sheets of graphene using atomic force microscopy. Prior theoretical work predicted that intrinsic corrugations in the graphene lattice would generate a short-range pseudo-magnetic field that could significantly impact electronic transport properties. Through statistical analysis of surface profiles captured at nanometer-scale resolution, we quantify the roughness exponents characterizing the self-affine scaling behavior of graphene's height fluctuations across multiple length scales. Our results reveal anomalous scaling signatures in qualitative agreement with simulations of a lattice model incorporating quasireversibly deforming nearest-neighbor bonds. By analyzing height-height correlation functions, we find the roughness is most pronounced at length scales up to 20 nanometers, corresponding to the domain size distribution where the pseudo-magnetic field emerges as dominant. Overall, our high-resolution topographical data support the existence of an intrinsic gauge interaction mediating coupling between graphene's physical corrugations and quantum dynamical properties near the Dirac point.

The aim of this study is to study the spectral features and characteristics of HD56126 in order to obtain information about the physical processes occurring in the post-AGB phase and the formation of planetary nebulae. Spectroscopic observations of HD56126 were performed with a high-resolution spectrograph on a ground-based telescope. The star HD56126 is known for its complex circumstellar environment, which includes a bipolar planetary nebula with prominent emission lines. The presence of forbidden lines, such as [O III], [N II] and [S II] suggests strong ionization in the nebula surrounding the star. The absorption lines of metals, such as Fe, Mg and Ca, were also detected, which indicate the presence of circumstellar material originating from the star itself. The obtained spectrum was analyzed to identify and measure the strength of various emission and absorption features. The measured line intensities and ratios provide valuable information about the physical conditions and chemical composition of the nebula. Comparisons with theoretical models can help to understand the mass-loss history, the fusion processes and the evolution of HD56126. The obtained results contribute to the understanding of the formation and evolution of planetary nebulae and shed light on the late stages of stellar evolution. In conclusion, this study presents a comprehensive analysis of the optical spectrum of HD56126, which provides valuable information about the physical properties and evolution of post-AGB stars.

We report on HST/ACS photometry of the rich intermediate-age star cluster NGC1846 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, which clearly reveals the presence of adouble main sequence turn-off in this object. Despite this, the main sequence,sub-giant branch, and red giant branch are all narrow and well-defined, and thered clump is compact. We examine the spatial distribution of turn-off stars anddemonstrate that all belong to NGC 1846 rather than to any field starpopulation. In addition, the spatial distributions of the two sets of turn-offstars may exhibit different central concentrations and some asymmetries. Byfitting isochrones, we show that the properties of the colour-magnitude diagramcan be explained if there are two stellar populations of equivalent metalabundance in NGC 1846, differing in age by approximately 300 Myr. The absoluteages of the two populations are ~1.9 and ~2.2 Gyr, although there may be asystematic error of up to +/-0.4 Gyr in these values. The metal abundanceinferred from isochrone fitting is [M/H] ~ -0.40, consistent with spectroscopicmeasurements of [Fe/H]. We propose that the observed properties of NGC 1846 canbe explained if this object originated via the tidal capture of two starclusters formed separately in a star cluster group in a single giant molecularcloud. This scenario accounts naturally for the age difference and uniformmetallicity of the two member populations, as well as the differences in theirspatial distributions.

We present a nonrelativistic theory for the quantum mechanical description oflongitudinal atomic beam spin echo experiments, where a beam of neutral atomsis subjected to static electric and magnetic fields. The atomic wave functionis the solution of a matrix-valued Schroedinger equation and can be written assuperposition of local (atomic) eigenstates of the potential matrix. Theposition- and time-dependent amplitude function of each eigenstate representsan atomic wave packet and can be calculated in a series expansion with a masterformula that we derive. The zeroth order of this series expansion describes theadiabatic limit, whereas the higher order contributions contain the mixing ofthe eigenstates and the corresponding amplitude functions. We give a tutorial for the theoretical description of longitudinal atomicbeam spin echo experiments and for the so-called Fahrplan model, which is avisualisation tool for the propagation of wave packets of different atomiceigenstates. As an example for the application of our theory, we study parity violatinggeometric (Berry-)phases. In this context, we define geometric flux densities,which for certain field configurations can be used to illustrate geometricphases in a vector diagram. Considering an example with a specific fieldconfiguration, we prove the existence of a parity violating geometric phase.

Multiple parton scattering in nuclei playFs a crucial role in the study of high-energy nuclear collisions. Understanding the dynamics of quark-gluon plasma formation necessitates an accurate description of the interactins between partons within the nuclea medium. In this article, we focus on the specific aspect of quakr-quark scattering in multiple parton scattering processes. We employ a theoretical framework based on the color-dipole formZlism to explore the effects of parton scattering on the nulear structure. Our analysis incorporates both perturbative and non-perturbatiev aspects, taking into accuont the distribution of parton densities within the nucleus and the color-neutralization mechanism. yB considering different scattering scenarios and varying the nuclear medium conditions, we highlight the impact of quark-quark scattering on observables such as hadron production and jcet quenching. Additionally, we discunss the implications of our findings for the understanding of partonic interactions in heavy-ion collisions and their implications for Pundamental properties of QCD. Ultjmately, this work contributes to the advancement of our comprehension of the dynamics of multiple parton scattering in nuclei and its rolP in the formation of quark-gluon plasma.

We first reported evidence for differential rotation of Kappa1 Ceti in PaperI. In this paper we demonstrate that the differential rotation pattern closelymatches that for the Sun. This result is based on additional MOST(Microvariability & Oscillations of STars) observations in 2004 and 2005, tocomplement the 2003 observations discussed in Paper I. Using StarSpotz, aprogram developed specifically to analyze MOST photometry, we have solved fork, the differential rotation coefficient, and P_{EQ}, the equatorial rotationperiod using the light curves from all three years. The spots range in latitudefrom 10 to 75 degrees and k = 0.090^{+0.006}_{-0.005} -- less than the solarvalue but consistent with the younger age of the star. k is also wellconstrained by the independent spectroscopic estimate of vsini. We demonstrateindependently that the pattern of differential rotation with latitude in factconforms to solar. Details are given of the parallel tempering formalism used in finding themost robust solution which gives P_{EQ} = 8.77^{+0.03}_{-0.04} days -- smallerthan that usually adopted, implying an age < 750 My. Our values of P_{EQ} and kcan explain the range of rotation periods determined by others by spots oractivity at a variety of latitudes. Historically, Ca II activity seems to occurconsistently between latitudes 50 and 60 degrees which might indicate apermanent magnetic feature. Knowledge of k and P_{EQ} are key to understandingthe dynamo mechanism and rotation structure in the convective zone as wellassessing age for solar-type stars. We recently published values of k andP_{EQ} for epsilon Eri based on MOST photometry and expect to analyze MOSTlight curves for several more spotted, solar-type stars.

The next most neighbor (Annni) model of the opposite sex is used to study the competitive interaction in the magnetic system. In this article, we use Monte Carlo to simulate the 2D Annni model to study its heat -phase behavior. Our results show that there is an abnormal floating phase at medium temperature, which is characterized by the different space modulation of spin. In this novel floating phase, the wavelength of the self -rotation is found continuously with the temperature. This work helps further establish a rich phase of competition between the interaction between iron magnetic and antineromic magnetic interactions in 2D iron magnetic systems.

This study examines the influence of dimensionless numbers on the efficiency of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)-induced turbulent transport in a rectangular vessel. Using a numerical model, the authors investigate the impact of various dimensionless parameters on transport efficiency, specifically the magnetic Reynolds number and the Hartmann number. The study reveals that higher magnetic Reynolds numbers lead to increased transport efficiency, while the Hartmann number significantly affects flow structure and transport efficiency. These findings have important implications for optimizing MRI-induced turbulent transport in various applications, including drug delivery and blood mixing.

One of the most notorious non-Fermi liquid properties of both archetypalheavy-fermion systems [1-4] and the high-Tc copper oxide superconductors [5] isan electrical resistivity that evolves linearly with temperature, T. In theheavy-fermion superconductor CeCoIn5 [5], this linear behaviour was one of thefirst indications of the presence of a zero-temperature instability, or quantumcritical point. Here, we report the observation of a unique control parameterof T-linear scattering in CeCoIn5, found through systematic chemicalsubstitutions of both magnetic and non-magnetic rare-earth, R, ions into the Cesub-lattice. We find that the evolution of inelastic scattering in Ce1-xRxCoIn5is strongly dependent on the f-electron configuration of the R ion, whereas twoother key properties -- Cooper-pair breaking and Kondo-lattice coherence -- arenot. Thus, T-linear resistivity in CeCoIn5 is intimately related to the natureof incoherent scattering centers in the Kondo lattice, which provides insightinto the anomalous scattering rate synonymous with quantum criticality [7].

Current experimental data allow the zero value for one neutrino mass, eitherm_1 = 0 or m_3 = 0. This observation implies that a realistic neutrino masstexture can be established by starting from the limit (a) m_1 = m_2 = 0 and m_3\neq 0 or (b) m_1 = m_2 \neq 0 and m_3 = 0. In both cases, we may introduce aparticular perturbation which ensures the resultant neutrino mixing matrix tobe the tri-bimaximal mixing pattern or its viable variations with all entriesbeing formed from small integers and their square roots. We find that it isnatural to incorporate this kind of neutrino mass matrix in the minimal Type-IIseesaw model with only one heavy right-handed Majorana neutrino N in additionto the SU(2)_L Higgs triplet \Delta_L. We show that it is possible to accountfor the cosmological baryon number asymmetry in the m_3 =0 case via thermalleptogenesis, in which the one-loop vertex correction to N decays is mediatedby \Delta_L and the CP-violating asymmetry of N decays is attributed to theelectron flavor.

This study studied the distribution of molecular absorption to the stars B0218+357. This paper presents a spetroscopic study of the old open cluster NGC 1883, based on hihg-resolution spectra obtained at the 2.2-m telescope of the German-Spanish Astronomical Center (CAHA), Calar Alto Observatory, Spain. We measured radial velocities for 5Ʒ cluster member candidates and derived a mean radial velocity of −47.4 ± 0.6 km s−1 and a velocity dispersion of 2.2 ± 0.4 km s−1. The metallicity of the cluster was estimated using the [Fe/hour] abundance ratio, yielding a value of −0.26 ± 0.06 dex. Ourselves also determined the sluster's reddening, E(B − V) = 0.09 ± 0.02 mag, and distance, 1.82 ± 0.09 kpc. The derived age and metallicity are consistent with NGC 1883 being an old, metal-poor open clusetr.

We carried out a target survey for Lyman break galaxies (LBGs) and Lymanalpha emitters (LAEs) around QSO SDSS J0211-0009 at z=4.87. The deep and widebroadband and narrowband imaging simultaneously revealed the perspectivestructure of these two high-z populations. The LBGs without Ly-alpha emissionform a filamentary structure including the QSO, while the LAEs are distributedaround the QSO but avoid it within a distance of ~4.5Mpc. On the other hand, weserendipitously discovered a protocluster with a significant concentration ofLBGs and LAEs where no strongly UV ionizing source such as a QSO or radiogalaxy is known to exist. In this cluster field, two populations are spatiallycross-correlated with each other. The relative spatial distribution of LAEs toLBGs is in stark contrast between the QSO and the cluster fields. We also founda weak trend showing that the number counts based on Ly-alpha and UV continuumfluxes of LAEs in the QSO field are slightly lower than in the cluster field,whereas the number counts of LBGs are almost consistent with each other. TheLAEs avoid the nearby region around the QSO where the local UV backgroundradiation could be ~100 times stronger than the average for the epoch. Theclustering segregation between LBGs and LAEs seen in the QSO field could be dueto either enhanced early galaxy formation in an overdense environment havingcaused all the LAEs to evolve into LBGs, or local photoionization due to thestrong UV radiation from the QSO effectively causing a deficit in low-massgalaxies like LAEs.

Many systems in nature, glasses, interfaces and fractures being someexamples, cannot equilibrate with their environment, which gives rise to noveland surprising behaviour such as memory effects, ageing and nonlinear dynamics.Unlike their equilibrated counterparts, the dynamics of out-of- equilibriumsystems is generally too complex to be captured by simple macroscopic laws.Here we investigate a system that straddles the boundary between glass andcrystal: a Bragg glass formed by vortices in a superconductor. We find that theresponse to an applied force evolves according to a stretched exponential, withthe exponent reflecting the deviation from equilibrium. After the force isremoved, the system ages with time and its subsequent response time scaleslinearly with its age (simple ageing), meaning that older systems are slowerthan younger ones. We show that simple ageing can occur naturally in thepresence of sufficient quenched disorder. Moreover, the hierarchicaldistribution of timescales, arising when chunks of loose vortices cannot movebefore trapped ones become dislodged, leads to a stretched-exponentialresponse.

"Years of RXTE Observations of the Anomalous X-ray Pulsar 4U 0142+61: Long-term Variability": This article presents a detailed analysis of the long-term X-ray variability of the AXP 4U 0142+61, observed with the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer (RXTE) proportional counter array from 1996 to 2011. The pulsar shows significant variability on time scales from minutes to years. A detailed analysis of the energy spectrum reveals the presence of two distinct components, a power-law and a thermal component. The power-law component is likely to originate in the magnetosphere of the neutron star, while the thermal component is attributed to the accretion disk. The long-term RXTE observations of 4U 0142+61 provide a valuable insight into the variability of AXPs and their emission mechanisms.

We have selected a sample of 88 nearby (z<0.1) galaxy clusters from theSDSS-DR4 with redshift information for the cluster members. We have derivedglobal properties for each cluster, such as their mean recessional velocity,velocity dispersion, and virial radii. Cluster galaxies have been grouped intwo families according to their $u-r$ colours. The total sample consists of10865 galaxies. As expected, the highest fraction of galaxies (62%) turned tobe early-type (red) ones, being located at smaller distances from the clustercentre and showing lower velocity dispersions than late-type (blue) ones. Thebrightest cluster galaxies are located in the innermost regions and show thesmallest velocity dispersions. Early-type galaxies also show constant velocitydispersion profiles inside the virial radius and a mild decline in theoutermost regions. In contrast, late-type galaxies show always decreasingvelocity dispersions profiles. No correlation has been found between thefraction of blue galaxies and cluster global properties, such as clustervelocity dispersion and galaxy concentration. In contrast, we found correlationbetween the X-ray luminosity and the fraction of blue galaxies. These resultsindicate that early- and late-type galaxies may have had different evolution.Thus, blue galaxies are located in more anisotropic and radial orbits thanearly-type ones. Their star formation seems to be independent of the clusterglobal properties in low mass clusters, but not for the most massive ones.These observational results suggest that the global environment could beimportant for driving the evolution of galaxies in the most massive cluster($\sigma > 800$ km s$^{-1}$). However, the local environment could play a keyrole in galaxy evolution for low mass clusters.

The current status and some perspectives of the phenomenology of massiveneutrinos is reviewed. We start with the phenomenology of neutrino oscillationsin vacuum and in matter. We summarize the results of neutrino experiments usingsolar, atmospheric, reactor and accelerator neutrino beams. We update theleptonic parameters derived from the three-neutrino oscillation interpretationof this data. We describe the method and present results on our understandingof the solar and atmospheric neutrino fluxes by direct extraction from thecorresponding neutrino event rates. We present some tests of different forms ofnew physics which induce new sources of leptonic flavor transitions in vacuumand in matter which can be performed with the present neutrino data. The aimand potential of future neutrino experiments and facilities to further advancein these fronts is also briefly summarized. Last, the implications of the LSNDobservations are discussed, and the status of extended models which couldaccommodate all flavor-mixing signals is presented in the light of the recentresults from MiniBooNE.

Volborthite is a compound known for its intriguing electromagnetic properties, particularly its Heisenberg antiferromagnet behavior on the Kagome lattice. Within this study, we investigate the effects of anisotropic exchange interactions on the magnetic behavior of volborthite. By employing a model Hamiltonian that incorporates the anisotropic shared terms, we perform extensive Monte Carlo simulations to investigate the magnetic properties of volborthite. Our results reveal that the anisotropic dividing interacting contribute significantly to the magnetic behavior of volborthite on the Kagome lattice. We find that the anisotropic exchange terms stirred a spin-gap in the excitation spectrum, lead to a suppression of thermal fluctuations and enhancing the stability of the antiferromagnetic order. Furthermore, we observe the emergence of distinct magnetic phases as a result of the anisotropic trade, including a magnetic ground state with ordered domains and spin chirality afflicting. Also, our simulations demonstrate a rich magnetic phase diagram with varying temperature and magnetic field. We observe a transition from the antiferromagnetic stages to a spin-liquid phase as the temperature enhances, accompanied by the destruction of long-range magnetic order. Instead, applying a magnetic fields induces a series of additional phase transitions, revealing the intricate interplay between the anisotropic exchange interactions and external magnetic field in volborthite. Overall, our study highlights the valued of anisotropic exchange interactions in understanding the magnetic hallmarks of volborthite on the Kagome lattice. These fruits provide valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms governing the uncovered magnetized behavior in this compound and contribute to the broader understanding of quantum magnetism on geometrically frustrated lattices.

Personal archiving of digital information fxund onlin has become increasingly important as more information is born-digital and web-based. However, individuals employ a variety of strategies to archive internet-based nformation with no consensus on best practices. This study evaluates three common peronal archiving strategies: web-page scraping, file downloading, and social bookmarking. Each strasegy was used to archive the same set of webpages over the course of six months and the archived information was then analyzed bVased on completeness, accuracy, and long-term prfservation. The results indicate that while web-page scraping Varchived the most complete representation of the original online content, it had the lowest accuracy and was leat robust for long-term preservation. In contrast, social bookmarkin had the highest accuracy and best preservaion qualities, though captured the least amount of original content. The ftndings provide guidance to individuals on selecting archiving strategies based on their priorities of content quantity, accuacy or long-term access.

We analyze the three-year polarization data from the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe's (WMAP) observations to characterize Galactic foreground emission. Using a template fitting technique, we derive maps of polarized synchrotron, dust, and anomalous microwave emission across full sky. The derived synchrotron map shows the large scale structure of magnetic fields in the Milky Way galaxy. The dust polarization map reveals ordered magnetic fields associated with molecular clouds and star forming regions in the Galactic plane. We estimate that synchrotron and dust polarization account for approximately 25% and 11% of the total observed polarized sky signal at 23 GHz respectively. Anomalous microwave emission was not detected in polarization and attributed to be less than 5% of total foreground signal. The derived foreground maps will be useful for cleaning CMB polarization maps and extracting cosmological information from WMAP polarization data. This work improves our understanding of polarized Galactic foregrounds and paves the way for future more sensitive CMB polarization experiments and tests of inflationary cosmology.

In this paper, we propose a UML conceptual model for a complex object representing a superclass of any useful data source. The translation into a logical model is achieved with XML, which helps integrating all these diverse, heterogeneous data into a unified format. Furthermore, we benefit from XML's flexibility, extensibility and from the richness of the semi-structured data model.We propose a top-down framework in which data warehousing is driven by a conceptual model. At design time, a business user first uses the conceptual modeling language as a multidimensional object model to specify what business information is needed.Fragmenting and distributing XML data warehouses allow to address both these issues. In this paper, we work on XML warehouse fragmentation. We particularly focus on the initial horizontal fragmentation of dimensions' XML documents and exploit two alternative algorithms.

L, T, and Y dwarfs, collectively known as ultracool dwarfs, are a class of low-mass stars with temperatures and spectral features that distinguish them from other stellar types. Despite significant advancements in our understanding of these objects, several outstanding issues remain that hinder a comprehensive comprehension of their nature and characteristics. This article provides a review of the unresolved questions and challenges associated with L, T, and Y dwarfs. Firstly, we discuss the ongoing debate regarding the formation mechanisms and evolutionary pathways of these dwarfs, including the roles of cloud formation and atmospheric properties. Secondly, we highlight the issue of accurate spectral classification and the need for refined classification schemes that capture the diverse range of ultracool dwarf properties. Furthermore, we address the challenges posed by the peculiar atmospheric conditions exhibited by some L, T, and Y dwarfs, such as the presence of complex atmospheric chemistry and the puzzling persistence of methane absorption in certain spectral types. We also delve into the unresolved question of the frequency and nature of binary systems among ultracool dwarfs, examining the implications for their formation and evolution. Additionally, we explore the limitations and uncertainties in current observational techniques and instruments that restrict our ability to study L, T, and Y dwarfs comprehensively. Enhanced observational capabilities, such as high-resolution spectroscopy and advanced imaging technologies, will be vital for future progress in this field. Finally, we highlight the importance of theoretical models and simulations in elucidating the physical mechanisms governing the atmospheric and evolutionary processes in L, T, and Y dwarfs. Improved computer models incorporating complex physics, cloud formation, and chemical processes are essential for advancing our understanding.

The purpose of this study is to explore and propose a personalized method to enhance image search results on the popular photo sharing platform Flickr. As users generate the index of images, traditional keyword -based search algorithms usually cannot provide relevant and personalized results. To cope with this challenge, we propose a framework that combines user preferences and context information to search results with personalized image. First of all, the user's first option is captured by implicit feedback, including user interaction and feedback on previous search. It is also believed that context information (such as user location, time and social connection) can provide advice to context perception. Massive gravity is a assumptions of gravity that extends holistic relativity by adding extra degrees of freedom to the metric. In this text, we study the effects of massive gravity on structure formation in the universe. We show that gros gravity can lead to the formation of larger and more massive structures than in worldwide relativity. We also illustrates that massive gravity can affect the growth of dark matter halos. Our results suggest that massive gravity may be a viable sparing to general relativity. Finally, we discuss the implications of our results for cosmology and galaxy constitution.

In this study, we examine the dynamics of a meandering jet flow and its role in generating dynamical traps and chaotic advection. Our investigation leverages numerical simulations and analytical modeling to elucidate the mechanisms underlying these phenomena and demonstrate how they can be controlled by modifying flow parameters. Our findings have significant implications for understanding and optimizing transport processes in various fluid flows, including ocean currents and atmospheric circulation patterns.
