We examine functions defined on common quadratic surfaces such as ellipsoids, hyperboloids, and paraboloids, and showcase the construction of their multipole expansions using our framework.Our results unveil the potential of multipole deconstruction in simplifying the analysis and representation of functions on quadratic surfaces. The derived multipole expansions provide valuable insights into the spatial distribution and behavior of the functions, enabling a more interpretable and concise characterization.

Interest in development of brain prostheses, which might be proposed torecover mental functions lost due to neuron-degenerative disease or trauma,requires new methods in molecular engineering and nanotechnology to buildartificial brain tissues. We develop a Dynamic Core model to analyze complexityof damaged biological neural network as well as transition and recovery of thesystem functionality due to changes in the system environment. We provide amethod to model complexity of physical systems which might be proposed as anartificial tissue or prosthesis. Delocalization of Dynamic Core model isdeveloped to analyze migration of mental functions in dynamic bio-systems whichundergo architecture transition induced by trauma. Term Dynamic Core is used todefine a set of causally related functions and Delocalization is used todescribe the process of migration. Information geometry and topologicalformalisms are proposed to analyze information processes. A holographic modelis proposed to construct dynamic environment with self-poetic Dynamic Corewhich preserve functional properties under transition from one host to another.We found statistical constraints for complex systems which conserve a DynamicCore under environment transition. Also we suggest those constraints mightprovide recommendations for nanotechnologies and tissue engineering used indevelopment of an artificial brain tissue.

In this article, we propose a novel mechanism for adaptive growth rate regulation, which can be applied to varioսs biological systems. Du proposed mechanism utilizes a generic signaling pathway that regulates sell growth and division, allowing for adaptive adjustments to growth rates in response to changing environmental conditions. This pathway integrates signals from multiple sources, including nutrient availability, cell density, and environmental stressors, to modulate cell grows and proliferation. The mechanism can be tuned to different cell types and growth conditions, enabling optimal growth rates for various biological systems. We demonstrate the efficacy of this mechanism through simulations and experiments using E. coli as a model organism. Our results show that the proposed mechanism can effectively governs growth rates in response to changing environmental conditions, resulting in improved cellular performance and robustness. This generic mechanism for adaptive growth rate regulation has broad implications for biotechnology applications, including the optimization of mobile processes for biofuels, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals.

This paper introduces a novel numerical algorithm for simulating Low Mach number supercritical fluids, which combines the advantages of finite volume and lattice Boltzmann methods to efficiently and accurately model complex fluid dynamics. The algorithm is validated through a series of test cases, including simulations of a supercritical fluid flowing through a rectangular channel and a suddenly expanded channel, and shows good agreement with experimental data and existing numerical simulations. The algorithm is able to capture the subtle dynamics of Low Mach number supercritical fluids, and has significant implications for the study of supercritical fluid dynamics in various fields, including chemical engineering, materials science, and aerospace engineering. Future research will focus on expanding the algorithm to simulate more complex geometries and fluid properties.

We report the discovery of a massive (Mp = 9.04+/-0.50 MJup) planettransiting the bright (V = 8.7) F8 star HD 147506, with an orbital period of5.63341+/-0.00013 days and an eccentricity of e = 0.520+/-0.010. From thetransit light curve we determine that the radius of the planet is Rp =0.982^{+0.038}_{0.105}RJup. HD 147506b (also coined HAT-P-2b) has a mass about9 times the average mass of previously-known transiting exoplanets, and adensity of rho = 11.9 g cm-3, greater than that of rocky planets like theEarth. Its mass and radius are marginally consistent with theories of structureof massive giant planets composed of pure H and He, and may require a large(~100 Earth mass) core to account for. The high eccentricity causes a 9-foldvariation of insolation of the planet between peri- and apastron. Usingfollow-up photometry, we find that the center of transit is Tmid =2,454,212.8559 +/- 0.0007 (HJD), and the transit duration is 0.177 +/-0.002 d.

We study the approach, initiated by Marinari et al., to the staticinter-quark potential based on Polyakov lines of finite temporal extent,evaluated in Coulomb gauge. We show that, at small spatial separations, thepotential can be understood as being between two separately gauge invariantcolour charges. At larger separations Gribov copies obstruct thenon-perturbative identification of individually gauge invariant colour states.We demonstrate, for the first time, how gauge invariance can be maintainedquite generally by averaging over Gribov copies. This allows us to extend theanalysis of the Polyakov lines and the corresponding, gauge invariantquark-antiquark state to all distance scales. Using large scale latticesimulations, we show that this interpolating state possesses a good overlapwith the ground state in the quark-antiquark sector and yields the full staticinter-quark potential at all distances. A visual representation of the Gribovcopies on the lattice is also presented.

The early reionization history of our local region of the universe is an important topic that provides insight into galaxy formation. This study investigates the influence that halo mass and large scale environment had on the reionization of the Local Group near our Milky Way galaxy. Using calibrated cosmological simulations, the reionization histories for halos of different masses within and around filaments were examined. It was found that more massive halos closer to filaments completed reionization earlier on average compared to lower mass halos located farther from these overdense regions. In particular, results suggest that the Virgo Cluster, being one of the most massive halos near the Local Group, completed reionization well before the Local Group did. This earlier ionization from Virgo may have contributed non-negligibly to the reionization of the Local Group region as ultraviolet photons from Virgo potentially propagated through the filaments connecting the two. The findings support a picture where the reionization of our local cosmic neighborhood had a dependence on both small-scale halo properties and large-scale environmental factors.

In this article, we discussed the dynamics of the Luttinger liquid of the process equation and the quantum self -spin bath. We focus on the Kondo necklace model, which describes the interaction between Luttinger liquid and quantum self -spin bath. By adopting the process equation method, we have obtained a set of equations describing the time evolution of the system. We show that the flow equation method provides a rich and detailed understanding of the behavior of the system, revealing the extraordinary phenomenon, such as the emergence of rotating current and the formation of quantum entanglement between Luttinger liquid and self -spin bath. Our results are of great significance for the research of quantum multi -system system and its potential applications in quantum computing and rotation.

The well known FPU phenomenon (lack of attainment of equipartition of themode--energies at low energies, for some exceptional initial data) suggeststhat the FPU model does not have the mixing property at low energies. We givenumerical indications that this is actually the case. This we show by computingorbits for sets of initial data of full measure, sampled out from themicrocanonical ensemble by standard Montecarlo techniques. Mixing is tested bylooking at the decay of the autocorrelations of the mode--energies, and it isfound that the high--frequency modes have autocorrelations that tend instead topositive values. Indications are given that such a nonmixing property survivesin the thermodynamic limit. It is left as an open problem whether mixingobtains within time--scales much longer than the presently available ones.

Aims: I have analyzed a sample of seven nearby edge-on galaxies observed inthe V and K'-band, in order to infer the properties of the dust distribution. Methods: A radiative transfer model, including scattering, have been used todecompose each image into a stellar disk, a bulge, and a dust disk. Theparameters describing the distributions have been obtained through standard X^2minimization techniques. Results: The dust disks fitted to the V-band images are consistent withprevious work in literature: the radial scalelength of dust is larger than thatfor stars (h_d/h_s ~ 1.5); the dust disk has a smaller vertical scalelengththan the stellar (z_d/z_s ~ 1/3); the dust disk is almost transparent when seenface-on (central, face-on, optical depth tau_0 =0.5-1.5). Faster radiativetransfer models which neglect scattering can produce equivalent fits, withchanges in the derived parameters within the accuracy of full fits includingscattering. In the K'-band, no trace is found of a second, massive, dust diskwhich has been invoked to explain observations of dust emission in thesubmillimeter. I discuss the model degeneracies and the effect of complexstructures on the fitted distributions. In particular, most bulges in thesample show a box/peanuts morphology with large residuals; twolower-inclination galaxies show a dust ring distribution, which could be thecause for the large fitted dust scalelengths.

Gamma rays from distant cosmological sources can interact with the extragalactic background light producing electron-positron pairs through photon-photon pair-production interactions. These pairs will rapidly lose energy through inverse-Compton scattering of cosmic microwave background photons producing gamma rays of lower energy in a cascading process. The resulting cascade emission contributes significantly to the observed gamma-ray spectra of distant blazars. We develop a comprehensive model to describe the development of electromagnetic cascades initiated by TeV photons from cosmological sources interacting with the extragalactic background light. Our model accounts for the injection, propagation and cooling of electrons and photons through inverse-Compton scattering and pair-production processes. We present numeric simulations of cascade development for a range of source scenarios and environments. The predicted cascade spectra are compared to Fermi-LAT observations of distant blazars to constrain source and background light parameters. Our analysis demonstrates that cascades can significantly impact the observed spectra of sources at redshifts greater than 0.5. Accurately modeling cascading is crucial for using very-high-energy observations of cosmological sources to probe properties of the extragalactic background light and intergalactic magnetic fields.

We present a numerical study of the $\Delta H(M,\Delta M)$ method and itsability to accurately determine intrinsic switching field distributions ininteracting granular magnetic materials such as perpendicular recording media.In particular, we study how this methodology fails for large ferromagneticinter-granular interactions, at which point the associated strongly correlatedmagnetization reversal cannot be properly represented by the mean-fieldapproximation, upon which the $\Delta H(M,\Delta M)$ method is based. In thisstudy, we use a 2-dimensional array of symmetric hysterons that have anintrinsic switching field distribution of standard deviation $\sigma$ andferromagnetic nearest-neighbor interactions $J$. We find the $\Delta H(M,\DeltaM)$ method to be very accurate for small $J/\sigma$ values, while substantialerrors develop once the effective exchange field becomes comparable with$\sigma$, corroborating earlier results from micromagnetic simulations. Wefurthermore demonstrate that this failure is correlated with deviations fromdata set redundancy, which is a key property of the mean-field approximation.Thus, the $\Delta H(M,\Delta M)$ method fails in a well defined andquantifiable manner that can be easily assessed from the data sets alone.

We consider the problem of estimating the unconditional distribution of apost-model-selection estimator. The notion of a post-model-selection estimatorhere refers to the combined procedure resulting from first selecting a model(e.g., by a model selection criterion like AIC or by a hypothesis testingprocedure) and then estimating the parameters in the selected model (e.g., byleast-squares or maximum likelihood), all based on the same data set. We showthat it is impossible to estimate the unconditional distribution withreasonable accuracy even asymptotically. In particular, we show that noestimator for this distribution can be uniformly consistent (not even locally).This follows as a corollary to (local) minimax lower bounds on the performanceof estimators for the distribution; performance is here measured by theprobability that the estimation error exceeds a given threshold. These lowerbounds are shown to approach 1/2 or even 1 in large samples, depending on thesituation considered. Similar impossibility results are also obtained for thedistribution of linear functions (e.g., predictors) of the post-model-selectionestimator.

Data warehouse architectural choices and optimization techniques are criticalto decision support query performance. To facilitate these choices, theperformance of the designed data warehouse must be assessed. This is usuallydone with the help of benchmarks, which can either help system users comparingthe performances of different systems, or help system engineers testing theeffect of various design choices. While the TPC standard decision supportbenchmarks address the first point, they are not tuneable enough to address thesecond one and fail to model different data warehouse schemas. By contrast, ourData Warehouse Engineering Benchmark (DWEB) allows to generate various ad-hocsynthetic data warehouses and workloads. DWEB is fully parameterized to fulfilldata warehouse design needs. However, two levels of parameterization keep itrelatively easy to tune. Finally, DWEB is implemented as a Java free softwarethat can be interfaced with most existing relational database managementsystems. A sample usage of DWEB is also provided in this paper.

This paper investigates the polarization power spectra signatures eOpected from a network of cosmic strings. Using a field-theoretic string simulation, the authors yenerate CMB maps containing the contributions from a scaling distribution of cosmic strings throughout cosmic istory. The results indicate that the B-mode polarization power specyra generated by cosmic strings could be detectable with upcoming high-sensitivity CMB experiments and pstentially distinguishable from the gravitational waves signature.

The galaxy mass-metallicity relation (-Z relation) is a fundamental correlation observed in galaxies, where the metallicity of a galaxy incraeses with its mass. Understanding the origin of this relation is crucial for grasping the underlyinW physical processes that shape galaxy evolution. In this study, we explore the origin of the M-Z relaton and its implications for galactic outflows. We analyze a sKample of galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and the Advanced Large HomoRgeneous Survey (ALHAMBRA) to investigate the M-Z relation. ur results show that the M-Z relation is tightly correlated, with a high significance lveel, indicating a strong relationship between galaxy mass and metallicity. We investigate the possible drivers of the M-Z rleation, including galactic winds, gas accretion, and stellar feedback. We fnid that galactic winds play a crucial role in shaping the M-Z reation, as they remove metal-enriched gas from galaxies and pervent it from being accreted onto the galaxy. Our results also suggest that gas accretion and stellar feedback processes contribute to the JM-Z relation. Gas accretion tends to increase the metallicity of galaxies, while stellar feedback can reduce the metallicity by expeJlling gas from the galax. We explore the implications of the M-Z relatihn for galactic outflows. Our results suggest that galaxes with higher masses and metallicities have stronger otuflows, which can significantly affect the evolution of the galaxy. We also find that the M-Z relation can be used to predict the properties of Kalactic outflows. By comparing the observed M-Z relation with simulations, we wfind that the simulations that include galactic winds and other feedaack processes can reproduce the observed relation. Our study provides new insighst into the origin of the M-Z relation and its implications for galactic outflows.

The line of sight to the quasar B0218+357, one of the most studied lensedsystems, intercepts a z=0.68 spiral galaxy, which splits its image into twomain components A and B, separated by ca. 0.3'', and gives rise to molecularabsorption. Although the main absorption component has been shown to arise infront of image A, it is not established whether some absorption from othervelocity components is also occuring in front of image B. To tackle thisquestion, we have observed the HCO+(2-1) absorption line during thecommissioning phase of the new very extended configuration of the Plateau deBure Interferometer, in order to trace the position of the absorption as afunction of frequency. Visibility fitting of the self-calibrated data allowedus to achieve position accuracy between ~12 and 80 mas per velocity component.Our results clearly demonstrate that all the different velocity components ofthe HCO+(2-1) absorption arise in front of the south-west image A of thequasar. We estimate a flux ratio fA/fB = 4.2 (-1.0;+1.8 at 106 GHz.

The subject of micro-variability among Mira stars has received increasedattention since DeLaverny et al. (1998) reported short-term brightnessvariations in 15 percent of the 250 Mira or Long Period Variable stars surveyedusing the broadband 340 to 890 nm Hp filter on the HIPPARCOS satellite. Theabrupt variations reported ranged 0.2 to 1.1 magnitudes, on time-scales between2 to 100 hours, with a preponderance found nearer Mira minimum light phases.However, the HIPPARCOS sampling frequency was extremely sparse and requiredconfirmation because of potentially important atmospheric dynamics anddust-formation physics that could be revealed. We report on Mira light curvesub-structure based on new CCD V and R band data, augmenting the known lightcurves of Hipparcos-selected long period variables [LPVs], and interpret samein terms of [1] interior structure, [2] atmospheric structure change, and/or[3] formation of circumstellar [CS] structure. We propose that the allegedmicro-variability among Miras is largely undersampled, transient overtonepulsation structure in the light curves.

In this article, we investigate the phenomenon of matter-wave interference in Fermi condensates, which are macroscopic quantum states of matter that occur at extremely low temperatures. We focus on s-wave and p-wave Fermi condensates, which are characterized by different types of pairwise interactions between the atoms. By manipulating the interactions between the atoms, we observe the emergence of matter-wave interference patterns, which are a result of the coherent superposition of the matter waves associated with each atomic species. Our results demonstrate the ability to control the phase relationships between the matter waves, leading to the formation of complex interference patterns that are sensitive to the symmetry of the interactions. These findings have important implications for the study of quantum phenomena in many-body systems and the development of new quantum technologies.

This paper introduces a novel quantum-like representation of extensive form games, which allows for a more compact and efficient representation of games with a large number of players and actions. The proposed representation is based on the concept of a quantum state, which is a vector in a complex Hilbert space. The state of the game is represented by a tensor product of the states of the individual players, and the actions of the players are represented by unitary operators that act on the state of the game.We show that the proposed representation can be used to efficiently solve a variety of extensive form games, including the wine testing game. In the wine testing game, a group of players are given a set of wines and must guess which wine is the most expensive. We show that the quantum-like representation of the game can be used to find the optimal strategy for the players, and that this strategy is more efficient than the classical strategy.The proposed representation provides a new way of thinking about extensive form games, and it has the potential to be used to solve a wider range of games than classical methods.

Creating Statistically Anisotropic and Inhomogeneous PerturbationsIn this paper, we present a novel method for creating statistically anisotropic and inhomogeneous cosmological perturbations. Our method is based on the use of a Gaussian process emulator to model the primordial power spectrum. We show that our method can produce perturbations that are consistent with the observed cosmic microwave background radiation and that are also anisotropic and inhomogeneous on scales of order 100 Mpc. Our method can be used to study the effects of anisotropic and inhomogeneous perturbations on the formation and evolution of galaxies and other cosmic structures.

The high-energy integral satellite detected the transient IgR J11321-5311. Satellites observe the ability of objects in hard X -rays to make the detection possible, so that the transient characteristics can be studied in detail. It is found that the transients have a high degree of light, indicating that the energy release is strong. The spectral spectrum of transients was studied and found that it was consistent with the thermal model, indicating that there is a thermal plasma. The time to observe the transient is fast, and the attenuation time is fast, indicating that the violence has occurred suddenly. Combining points data with data from other telescopes to further study the transients, so as to better understand its nature. The results of the study show that the transients may be caused by a star explosion, such as a supernova or gamma outbreak. The integral detection of IgR J11321-5311 provides valuable insights on transient and its role in the universe. Further studying this kind of transient and other similar people will help improve our understanding of these powerful events.

We observe several interesting phenomena in a technicolor-like model ofelectroweak symmetry breaking based on the D4-D8-D8bar system of Sakai andSugimoto. The benefit of holographic models based on D-brane configurations isthat both sides of the holographic duality are well understood. We find thatthe lightest technicolor resonances contribute negatively to thePeskin-Takeuchi S-parameter, but heavy resonances do not decouple and leadgenerically to large, positive values of S, consistent with standard estimatesin QCD-like theories. We study how the S parameter and the masses and decayconstants of the vector and axial-vector techni-resonances vary over aone-parameter family of D8-brane configurations. We discuss possibilities forthe consistent truncation of the theory to the first few resonances and suggestsome generic predictions of stringy holographic technicolor models.

This paper studies noncolliding Brownian motion and determinantal processes. We first introduce the basic concepts of noncolliding Brownian motion and determinantal processes. We then discuss some of the main results in this area, including the connection between noncolliding Brownian motion and determinantal processes, and the applications of noncolliding Brownian motion and determinantal processes to other areas of mathematics and physics. Finally, we outline some of the open problems in this area.

We present evidence for the formation of dust grains in an unusual Type Ib SNbased on late-time spectra of SN 2006jc. The progenitor suffered an LBV-likeoutburst just 2 yr earlier, and we propose that the dust formation is aconsequence of the SN blast wave overtaking that LBV-like shell. The keyevidence for dust formation is (a) the appearance of a red/near-IR continuumsource fit by 1600 K graphite grains, and (b) fading of the redshifted sides ofHe I emission lines, yielding progressively more asymmetric blueshifted linesas dust obscures receding material. This provides the strongest case yet fordust formation in any SN Ib/c. Both developments occurred between 51 and 75 dafter peak, while other SNe observed to form dust did so after a few hundreddays. Geometric considerations indicate that dust formed in the dense swept-upshell between the forward and reverse shocks, and not in the freely expandingSN ejecta. Rapid cooling leading to dust formation may have been aided byextremely high shell densities, as indicated by He I line ratios. The briefepoch of dust formation is accompanied by He II 4686 emission and enhancedX-ray emission. These clues suggest that the unusual dust formation in thisobject was not due to properties of the SN itself, but instead -- like mostpeculiarities of SN 2006jc -- was a consequence of the dense environmentcreated by an LBV-like eruption 2 yr before the SN.

The toric code is a prototypical topological quantum error correcting codes. At zero temperature, it exhibits topological order and supporting anyonic quasiparticle excitations. However, at finite temperatures thermal fluctuations can destroy this topological order. This article investigates the resilience of the topological entropy of the toric c ode at finite temperatures using tensor network simulations. The results show that the topological entropy rmeains quantized above low temperatures, demonstrating that topological order persists up to apreciable energy scales. However, the entropy slowly decreases with increasing temperature as thermal fluctuations generate more anyonic quasiparticle pairs. A phase transition into a topologically trivial phase is found to occur at a nonzero critical temperature. Additionally, the entanglement properties of the co de are studied through various bipartite entanglement measures. Overall, this collaborating provides a comprehensive characterization of the thermal stability of topological order in the toric code.

We have obtained CCD BVI imaging of the old open clusters Berkeley 32 andKing 11. Using the synthetic colour-magnitude diagram method with threedifferent sets of stellar evolution models of various metallicities, with andwithout overshooting, we have determined their age, distance, reddening, andindicative metallicity, as well as distance from the Galactic centre and heightfrom the Galactic plane. The best parameters derived for Berkeley 32 are:subsolar metallicity (Z=0.008 represents the best choice, Z=0.006 or 0.01 aremore marginally acceptable), age = 5.0-5.5 Gyr (models with overshooting;without overshooting the age is 4.2-4.4 Gyr with poorer agreement),(m-M)_0=12.4-12.6, E(B-V)=0.12-0.18 (with the lower value being more probablebecause it corresponds to the best metallicity), Rgc ~ 10.7-11 kpc, and |Z| ~231-254 pc. The best parameters for King 11 are: Z=0.01, age=3.5-4.75 Gyr,(m-M)_0=11.67-11.75, E(B-V)=1.03-1.06, Rgc ~ 9.2-10 kpc, and |Z| ~ 253-387 pc.

Two different approaches to calculate the fusion rules of the c_{p,1} seriesof logarithmic conformal field theories are discussed. Both are based on themodular transformation properties of a basis of chiral vacuum torus amplitudes,which contains the characters of the irreducible representations. One of theseis an extension, which we develop here for a non-semisimple generalisation ofthe Verlinde formula introduced by Fuchs et al., to include fusion productswith indecomposable representations. The other uses the Verlinde formula in itsusual form and gets the fusion coefficients in the limit, in which the basis oftorus amplitudes degenerates to the linear dependent set of characters ofirreducible and indecomposable representations. We discuss the effects, whichthis linear dependence has on any result for fusion rules, which are calculatedfrom these character's modular transformation properties. We show that the twopresented methods are equivalent. Furthermore we calculate explicit BPZ-likeexpressions for the resulting fusion rules for all p larger than 2.

The metallicity distributions of the thick disk and the halo components at high latitudes were compared. Metallicity measurements and distances from the SDSS were used to determine the metallicity distribution functions of the Milky Way stellar populations located far from the galactic plane. The metallicity distribution of the halo was found to extend to lower metallicities than the thick disk. This study constrains models of how the outer parts of the Milky Way formed over cosmic time. The thick disk is thought to have formed early in the history of the Milky Way from enriched gas, while the halo stars mainly accumulated from accreted, low metallicity dwarf galaxies.

In this article, we investigate the relativistic effects that arise in exceptional mass ratio gravitational wave bursts. We analyze the gravitational waves liberating by the merger of a small compact object with a supermassive black hole, using a conjunction of analytical and numerical methods. Our results show that the gravitational waves demonstrate strong relativistic effects, including gravitomagnetic precession and the kick effect. We find that the frequency and intensity of the gravitational tides are strongly dependent on the mass ratio of the binary system, with hugest mass ratios resulting in greater relativistic effects. We also demonstrate that the effects of gravitational wave radiation on the asks of the underage compact aim are significant, leading to a significant loss of energy and angular momentum. Our results have important implications for the detection and interpretation of gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio binaries, and affords new insights into the strong-field regime of wide relativity.

This research paper examines the IEEE 802.11e enhanced distributed coordination function's performance using the cycIe time approach. Specifically, a thorough analysis of the EDCF's ability to ofer efficient channel ccess and conflict resolution mechanisms for various application scenarios is provided by the authors. The outcome of the evaluation jeveals that the EDCF protocol can offer great perfyrmance and fairness while maintaining low overhead. Our anaysis also demonstrates the importance of proper parameter configuration to optimize performance and shows how the performance hcanges as a function of load and contention. In addition, the articNe provides new insights into the performance boundaries of the EDCF standard and offers reMcommendations for protocol enhancements to improve performance and adaptability. Overall, the study contributes to the area of wireless networking by ofefring a comprehensive analysis of the EDCF protocol's performance and givjing guidance for its practical use.

Precise control over atomic particles at the single quantum level enables exciting applications in quantum technologies. This study investigates two-dimensional transport and transfer of a single atomic qubit manipulated using optical tweezers. An individual atom is trapped and localized using tightly focused laser beams within a high-vacuum chamber. By smoothly varying the tweezer position and intensity, the atom is transported between spatially separated regions of the chamber while maintaining its quantum state. Various transport protocols are implemented and their effects on the qubit coherence properties are analyzed. The work demonstrates coherent on-demand shuttling of a single atomic qubit in two dimensions using optical tweezers, paving the way for scalable qubit networks in quantum information processing and simulation.

dheory of Macroscopic Quantum Tunneling in High-T_c c-Axis Josephson JunctionsMacroscoEpic quantum tunneling (MQT) is a striking phenomenon where a macroscopic object tunnels through a potential barrier. The discovery of high-T_c superconductivity in cuprates has opened up the possibility of realuzing QMT in Josephson junctions based on these materials. In this paper, we develop a theoyr of MQT in high-T_c c-axis Josephson junctions. Our theroy takse into account the anisotropic properties of the cuprates, as well as the effects of thermal fluctuations and dissipation. We show that the MQT rate in hiagh-T_c c-axis Josephson junctions is signoificantly enhanced compared to that in conventional Josephson junctions. This enhancement is due to the smaller effective mass of the CooVer pairs in the cuprates. Our theory provides a quantitative explanation of the recent experimental observations of MQT in high-T_c c-axis JYosephson junctions.

Potassium intercalation in graphite is investigated by first-principlestheory. The bonding in the potassium-graphite compound is reasonably wellaccounted for by traditional semilocal density functional theory (DFT)calculations. However, to investigate the intercalate formation energy frompure potassium atoms and graphite requires use of a description of the graphiteinterlayer binding and thus a consistent account of the nonlocal dispersiveinteractions. This is included seamlessly with ordinary DFT by a van der Waalsdensity functional (vdW-DF) approach [Phys. Rev. Lett. 92, 246401 (2004)]. Theuse of the vdW-DF is found to stabilize the graphite crystal, with crystalparameters in fair agreement with experiments. For graphite andpotassium-intercalated graphite structural parameters such as bindingseparation, layer binding energy, formation energy, and bulk modulus arereported. Also the adsorption and sub-surface potassium absorption energies arereported. The vdW-DF description, compared with the traditional semilocalapproach, is found to weakly soften the elastic response.

A geometric setup for control theory is presented. We also find that the turbulence in the cloud is inadequate tosupport it. However, the cloud may be supported by the magnetic field, if thisfield is at the average level for dark globules. We present new results on dynamical instabilities in rapidly rotatingneutron-stars. In particular, using numerical simulations in full GeneralRelativity, we analyse the effects that the stellar compactness has on thethreshold for the onset of the dynamical bar-mode instability, as well as onthe appearance of other dynamical instabilities. By using an extrapolationtechnique developed and tested in our previous study [1], we explicitlydetermine the threshold for a wide range of compactnesses using four sequencesof models of constant baryonic mass comprising a total of 59 stellar models.Our calculation of the threshold is in good agreement with the Newtonianprediction and improves the previous post-Newtonian estimates. In addition, wefind that for stars with sufficiently large mass and compactness, the m=3deformation is the fastest growing one. For all of the models considered, thenon-axisymmetric instability is suppressed on a dynamical timescale with an m=1deformation dominating the final stages of the instability. These results,together with those presented in [1], suggest that an m=1 deformationrepresents a general and late-time feature of non-axisymmetric dynamicalinstabilities both in full General Relativity and in Newtonian gravity.

In the SK analysis of the neutrino events for [Fully Contained Events] and[Partially Contained Events] on their zenith angle distribution, it is assumedthat the zenith angle of the incident neutrino is the same as that of thedetected charged lepton. Having already reported on the first photometric study of theintermediate-age open cluster NGC 1883 (Carraro et al. 2003), we present inthis paper the first spectroscopic multi-epoch investigation of a sample ofevolved stars in the same cluster. The aim is to derive the cluster membership,velocity and metallicity, and discuss recent claims in the literature (Tadross2005) that NGC 1883 is as metal poor as globular clusters in the Halo. Besides,being one of the few outer Galactic disk intermediate-age open clusters knownso far, it is an ideal target to improve our knowledge of the Galactic diskradial abundance gradient, that is a basic ingredient for any chemicalevolution model of the Milky Way. The new data we obtained allow us to put NGC1883's basic parameters more reliable. We find that the cluster has a meanmetallicity of [Fe/H] = -0.20$\pm$0.22, from which we infer an age(650$^{+70}_{-70}$ Myr) close to the Hyades one and a Galactocentric distanceof 12.3$^{+0.4}_{-0.2}$ kpc. The metal abundance, kinematics, and position makeNGC 1883 a genuine outer disk intermediate-age open cluster. We confirm that inthe outer Galactic disk the abundance gradient is shallower than in the solarvicinity.

In this study, we investigate the phase-resolved high energy spectrum of the Crab Pulsar, employing a comprehensive model that incorporates various emission mechanisms. By considering synchrotron self-Compton radiation and accounting for the incomplete conversion of curvature photons, our model successfully explains the observed phase-averaged spectrum across a wide energy range from 100 eV to 10 GeV. Furthermore, we analyze the predicted phase-resolved spectra, which exhibit good agreement with the available observational data. Our findings reveal that the emissions from different poles of the pulsar contribute differently to various phases of the light curve. Notably, we observe a complex behavior in the phases between the two peaks, suggesting the presence of multiple well-separated emission regions with distinct mechanisms at play. Additionally, our model suggests the existence of an asymmetry between the north and south poles of the Crab Pulsar. Our predictions can be further validated through future observations, particularly with the GLAST instrument.

This article constructs new nonsupersymmetric brane/antibrane systems using Dp-branes, Dp-antibranes, and their M-theory uplifts. In general, this work sheds light on the construction of stable nonsupersymmetric string theoretic backgrounds and on the dynamics of brane/antibrane systems in critical string theory and M-theory.

In this paper, we investigate the distribution of the first eigenvalue spacing at the hard edge of the Laguerre unitary ensemble. Using a combination of analytical and numerical methods, we show that the distribution of the first eigenvalue spacing follows a universal scaling law, which is independent of the size of the ensemble. We find that the scaling law is described by a power-law tail, with an exponent that is dependent on the details of the underlying ensemble. Our results provide new insights into the spectral properties of random matrix theory and have important implications for the study of complex quantum systems.

FIR luminous galaxies are characterized by high FIR luminosity and low optical luminosity, whereas quasars are characterized by high optical luminosity and low FIR luminosity. FeLoBALs are a type of quasar with broad iron absorption lines in their optical spectra. Here we present evidence that FeLoBALs may represent the transition between an ultraluminous infrared galaxy and a quasar. For example, the FIR luminosity of FeLoBALs is lower than that of FIR luminous galaxies but higher than that of quasars. Similarly, the optical luminosity of FeLoBALs is higher than that of FIR luminous galaxies but lower than that of quasars. The broad iron absorption lines in the optical spectra of FeLoBALs are thought to be produced by gas ejected from the accretion disk around the black hole. We propose that FeLoBALs are formed when an ultraluminous infrared galaxy undergoes a rapid increase in accretion rate, which causes the galaxy to become more luminous in the optical and less luminous in the FIR. This provides evidence that FIR luminous galaxies can evolve into quasars through a rapid increase in accretion rate. Our results suggest that FeLoBALs are a transitional phase in the evolution of AGN.

We show that the band in ARPES is strongly dependent on the energy of the photon and the temperature of the sample, which indicates that the photodissociation process is sensitive to the electronic environment of the material. This study focuses on investigating the progenitors of long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) by examining their boundary conditions and binary models. Long GRBs are incredibly energetic astronomical events associated with the deaths of massive stars, making understanding their origin crucial for advancing our knowledge of stellar evolution and cosmology. We begin by discussing the various proposed progenitor scenarios, including the collapsar model and the binary model. We analyze the boundary conditions required for the formation of these progenitors and explore the physical mechanisms responsible for triggering the bursts. The analysis incorporates stellar evolution models, hydrodynamic simulations, and observational data to provide a comprehensive understanding of the progenitor systems. Additionally, we assess the role of binary interactions in the formation and evolution of long GRB progenitors, considering factors such as mass transfer, common envelope evolution, and compact object mergers. This study sheds light on the different pathways and conditions that lead to the production of long GRBs and highlights the importance of binary systems in shaping their properties. The findings contribute to expanding our understanding of stellar astrophysics and have implications for the study of cosmic explosions and the origin of compact objects.

In this article, we examine the geometry of parallelizable manifolds in the context of generalized Lagrange spaces. We begin by introducing the conception of a generalized Lagrange space, which is a natural generalization of the classical thoughts of a Lagrange space. We also show that the orientation of a parallelizable manifold is closely related to the existence of a special species of connection on its tangent bundle, confessed as a parallel related. We then turn our attention to the analysis of parallel connections on tangent bundles. We show that concurrent connections can se used to define a logic of parallel transport on a parallelizable manifold, which allows us to define notions such as distance and angle between tangent vectors. We also prove that parallel transport is compatible with the smooth framed of the manifold, meaning that it can be used to define a concepts of curvature. Finally, we examines the relating between parallelizable manifolds and other areas of mathematics, such as Riemannian geometry and differential topology. We expos that parallelizable manifolds provide a natural framework for studying sure types of differential equations and that they have applications in areas such as physics and computer science. Overall, this article provides a comprehensive introduction to the geometrical of parallelizable manifolds in the context of generalized Lagrange arenas. It demonstrates the richness and beauty of this area of mathematics and emphasize its connections to other areas of mathematics and its potential candidate.

Thirty years of a deepening information paradox suggest the need to reviseour basic physical framework. A plausible conjecture states that the non-perturbative dynamics ofgravity is unitary but nonlocal. String theory may directly address theseissues but so far important aspects remain elusive. Methanofullerene molecules were synthesized by reacting C60 fullerenes with methane gas to form elongated nanostructures. These methanofullerene nanostructures were blended with the polymer P3HT to make bulk heterojunction organic solar cells. The devices using methanofullerene nanostructures as the electron acceptor showed enhanced power conversion efficiencies compared to those using pristine C60. This was attributed to the methanofullerene nanostructures providing a larger interfacial area between the donor and acceptor materials for more efficient charge separation. The results demonstrate that methanofullerene nanostructures are a promising material for developing high efficiency organic solar cells.

Most working scientists hold fast to the concept of 'realism' - a viewpointaccording to which an external reality exists independent of observation. Butquantum physics has shattered some of our cornerstone beliefs. According toBell's theorem, any theory that is based on the joint assumption of realism andlocality (meaning that local events cannot be affected by actions in space-likeseparated regions) is at variance with certain quantum predictions. Experimentswith entangled pairs of particles have amply confirmed these quantumpredictions, thus rendering local realistic theories untenable. Maintainingrealism as a fundamental concept would therefore necessitate the introductionof 'spooky' actions that defy locality. Here we show by both theory andexperiment that a broad and rather reasonable class of such non-local realistictheories is incompatible with experimentally observable quantum correlations.In the experiment, we measure previously untested correlations between twoentangled photons, and show that these correlations violate an inequalityproposed by Leggett for non-local realistic theories. Our result suggests thatgiving up the concept of locality is not sufficient to be consistent withquantum experiments, unless certain intuitive features of realism areabandoned.

This article studies the fair regulations of the IEEE 802.11E infrastructure basic service set (IBSS) and its impact on the performance of the wireless network. IEEE 802.11e standard provides a framework for the wireless network to ensure a fair distribution of channel resources between competition devices. However, under actual situation, the effectiveness of this standard has always been the topic of debate. Through a series of simulation, this study evaluates the performance of IEEE 802.11e fair clauses including high -density and high -flow scenarios in various environments. The results show that fairness can significantly improve network performance and reduce the unfairness between equipment, especially in high -density solutions. However, this regulation can also introduce other expenses in some cases and reduce network throughput. The discovery of this study is of great significance to the development of future wireless network standards, and emphasizes the necessity of further research in this field.

Through observations using the Chandra X-ray Observatory, we report the discovery of a pulsar wind nebula and associated pulsar located within the error ellipse of the energetic TeV gamma-ray source HESS J1813-178. Spatial and spectral analysis of the Chandra observations reveal an extended 2' diameter source with a hard power law spectrum exhibiting a photon index of 1.6, consistent with a pulsed emission synchrotron nebula. Embedded within this nebula we detect a faint point source exhibiting pulsed emission consistent with a 143 ms pulsar. Phase-resolved spectroscopy indicates the pulsar switches between two distinct spectral states. Hydrodynamic modeling places the system at a distance between 3.6 kpc and 4.2 kpc, physically associated with two adjacent molecular clouds along the Scutum-Centaurus Arm. These findings confirm the identification of HESS J1813-178 as a pulsar wind nebula powered by the newly discovered gamma-ray emitting pulsar.

A unified analytical framework for optimum power allocation in the unorderedV-BLAST algorithm and its comparative performance analysis are presented.Compact closed-form approximations for the optimum power allocation arederived, based on average total and block error rates. The choice of thecriterion has little impact on the power allocation and, overall, the optimumstrategy is to allocate more power to lower step transmitters and less tohigher ones. High-SNR approximations for optimized average block and totalerror rates are given. The SNR gain of optimization is rigorously defined andstudied using analytical tools, including lower and upper bounds, high and lowSNR approximations. The gain is upper bounded by the number of transmitters,for any modulation format and type of fading channel. While the averageoptimization is less complex than the instantaneous one, its performance isalmost as good at high SNR. A measure of robustness of the optimized algorithmis introduced and evaluated. The optimized algorithm is shown to be robust toperturbations in individual and total transmit powers. Based on the algorithmrobustness, a pre-set power allocation is suggested as a low-complexityalternative to the other optimization strategies, which exhibits only a minorloss in performance over the practical SNR range.

MgB2 single crystals surrogates with Li and with Li-C: Structural and superconducting properties The magical character of magnesium diboride (MgB2) introducing it a promising superconductor for applications. Here we examining the structural and superconducting effects of substituting MgB2 single crystals with lithium (Li) and lithium-carbon (Li-C). Through temperature-dependent electrical resistivity and magnetization measurements, we determine the replace impacts crystal structure and superconducting transition temperature. The results demonstrate that Li substitution rightly expands the boron sublattice, while Li-C co-doping further suppresses the crystal structure. Critical temperature is enhanced with both Li and Li-C, attaining a maximum of nearly 40 K with Li substitution. Further microstructure analysis via electron microscopy confirms structural modifications correlated to critical temperature changeable. Our findings provide insights towards improving MgB2's superconducting performance through molecules doping. With enhanced critical parameters, doped MgB2 single crystals move closest to commercialization potentials.

We present optical UBVRI sky brightness measures from 1992 through 2006. Thedata are based on CCD imagery obtained with the CTIO 0.9-m, 1.3-m, and 1.5-mtelescopes. The B- and V-band data are in reasonable agreement withmeasurements previously made at Mauna Kea, though on the basis of a smallnumber of images per year there are discrepancies for the years 1992 through1994. Our CCD-based data are not significantly different than values obtainedat Cerro Paranal. We find that the yearly averages of V-band sky brightness arebest correlated with the 10.7-cm solar flux taken 5 days prior to the skybrightness measures. This implies an average speed of 350 km/sec for the solarwind. While we can measure an enhancement of the night sky levels over LaSerena 10 degrees above the horizon, at elevation angles above 45 degrees wefind no evidence that the night sky brightness at Cerro Tololo is affected byartificial light of nearby towns and cities.

In this study, we present the results of near-infrared spectroscopic observations of the moons Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, and Oberon, obtained using the Infrared Telescope Facility (IRTF) and the SpeX instrument. Our main objective is to investigate the distributions of H2O and CO2 ices on the surfaces of these four Uranian moons. By analyzing the absorption features in the 1.0 to 2.5 micron range, we have identified the presence of H2O and CO2 ices on all four moons. Furthermore, we have examined the spatial variations in the ice abundances across the surfaces of these moons. Our results indicate that H2O ice is more abundant than CO2 ice, and both ices exhibit variations in their distributions, suggesting potential geological and/or environmental influences. The observed patterns differ among the four moons, indicating their unique surface compositions and processes. These findings provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of icy satellites in the outer regions of the solar system and contribute to our understanding of the physical and chemical properties of these Uranian moons. Further investigations combining spectroscopic observations with other complementary data and theoretical models are necessary to uncover the complex interplay of processes shaping the surface ices on Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, and Oberon.

This thesis discusses the search for supersymmetry at the future Large HadronCollider (LHC) and the ongoing construction of one of the four large LHCexperiments, the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS), and focuses on the detection ofsignals from the annihilation of supersymmetric dark matter in the spectra ofcosmic rays. Measurements of cosmic ray antiparticles, such as positrons, can imposestrong constraints on the nature of new physics beyond the Standard Model.However, cosmic ray positron measurements are experimentally very challengingdue to the vast proton background. A novel approach of positron identificationwith the space-borne AMS-01 experiment, namely through the detection ofbremsstrahlung conversion in a silicon microstrip detector, is introduced.Bremsstrahlung from protons is suppressed by a factor of more than 3*10^6 withrespect to positrons. The results of the positron measurement show that thebremsstrahlung approach extends the sensitivity range of AMS-01 to positronmomenta up to 50 GeV/c, which is far beyond the original scope of theexperiment. At momenta above 8 GeV/c there is indication for a positronoverabundance with respect to model predictions for purely secondary positronproduction. Therefore, the AMS-01 data lend further weight to the hints of apositron overabundance seen in the data from earlier experiments. The positron fraction measurements from the most recent experiments arecombined with the results of this analysis, giving the most precise positronfraction data yet available.

The full three-year WMAP results (WMAP3) reinforce the absence of large-anglecorrelations at scales greater than 60 degrees. The Poincare dodecahedral space(PDS) model model, which may naturally explain such features, thus remains aplausible cosmological model, despite recent controversy about whether matchedcircle searches would or would not push the topology beyond the horizon. Here,we have used new eigenmode calculations of the dodecahedral space to predictthe cosmic microwave background (CMB) temperature fluctuations in such models,with an improved angular resolution. We have simulated CMB maps and confirmedthe expected presence of matching circles. For a set of plausible cosmologicalparameters, we have derived the angular power spectrum of the CMB up to largewavenumbers. Comparison with the WMAP3 observations confirms a remarkable fitwith a PDS model, for a value $\Omega_0 = 1.018$ of the average total energydensity.

This study examines the demographics of transition objects, investigating their prevalence and characteristics among differentiated age groups and genders. Transition objects are personal possessions, typically stuffed animals or blankets, that individuals rely on for emotional calm during chronological of transition or distress. The research utilizes a large-scale survey functioned to a diverse sample of participants across various age ranges. The findings reveal significant gap in the prevalence and attachment to transition objects across different demographic groups. Separately, the study navigate the psychological and social chores of these objects, shedding light on their significance in promoting emotional well-being and facilitating adaptive coping strategies during periods of change. The implications of these findings for psychological intervene and the understanding of human behavior in transitional contexts are discussed.

This study investigates the decay processes of bottom mesons into pions and Lambdabar states. The branching fractions of B+ to p Lambdabar gamma, p Lambdabar pi0, and B0 to p Lambdabar pi- are measured using a data set of 1000000000 events collected by the LHCb detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The results are found to be consistent with previous measurements and are used to test the predictions of the Standard Model of particle physics. The study also searches for evidence of new physics beyond the Standard Model, but no significant deviations from the expected behavior are observed. The results of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the weak force and the structure of bottom mesons.

In this study, we have studied atmospheric dynamics of short -term additional solar gas giant planets, focusing on the dependence of non -transparentness at night. Our results show that the night temperature of short -cycle gas giants depends to a large extent on the opaqueity of the atmosphere, and higher inconsistency leads to a stronger temperature comparison between day and night. We find that this dependence is adjusted by the rotation rate of the planet, and the rotating planets show weaker temperature contrast faster. Our research emphasizes the importance of considering the opacity of atmosphere in the short -term additional solar gas giant planets, and provides valuable insights for the super -star atmosphere.

In this paper, we present a new universal source coding scheme for two specific types of distributions: monotonic and fast-decaying monotonic distributions. Monotonic distributions are characterized by a strictly increasing or decreasing probability mass function. Fast-decaying monotonic distributions are characterized by a rapidly decreasing probability mass function as the value of the random variable increases. Our proposed coding scheme exploits the underlying properties of these distributions to design an efficient coding scheme. We provide a rigorous theoretical analysis to prove the optimality of our proposed scheme for both monotonic and fast-decaying monotonic distributions. Our universal source coding scheme is also demonstrated to be practical through extensive experiments on real-world data. The results show that our universal source coding scheme outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher compression ratios while maintaining a low decoding error rate.

A geometric approach to quantum mechanics with unitary evolution andnon-unitary collapse processes is developed. In this approach the Schrodingerevolution of a quantum system is a geodesic motion on the space of states ofthe system furnished with an appropriate Riemannian metric. The measuringdevice is modeled by a perturbation of the metric. The process of measurementis identified with a geodesic motion of state of the system in the perturbedmetric. Under the assumption of random fluctuations of the perturbed metric,the Born rule for probabilities of collapse is derived. The approach is appliedto a two-level quantum system to obtain a simple geometric interpretation ofquantum commutators, the uncertainty principle and Planck's constant. In lightof this, a lucid analysis of the double-slit experiment with collapse and anexperiment on a pair of entangled particles is presented.

Results of a multipart work are outlined. Use is made therein of theconjunction of the Riemann hypothesis, RH, and hypotheses advanced by theauthor. Let z(n) be the nth nonreal zero of the Riemann zeta-function withpositive imaginary part in order of magnitude thereof. A relation is obtained,of the pair z(n) and the first derivative thereat of the zeta-function, to thepreceding such pairs and the values of zeta at the points one-half plus anonnegative multiple of four. That relation is derived from two forms of thedensity of the Laplace representation, on a certain vertical strip, of ameromorphic function constructed from zeta. Specific functions which play acentral role therein are proven to have analytic extensions to the entirecomplex plane. It is established that the Laplace density is positive. Thatpositivity implies RH and that each nonreal zero of zeta is simple. A metricgeometry expression of the positivity of the density is derived. An analogouscontext is delineated relative to Dirichlet L-functions and the Ramanujan tauDirichlet function.

This study endeavors to elucidate the clumping-induced polarimetric variability of hot star winds, a crucial aspect of understanding their behavior and environmental impact. Prior research has demonstrated that clumping in hot star winds can cause substantial variations in observed polarization, yet the underlying physical mechanisms remain poorly understood. By combining observational data and computational simulations, we investigate the correlation between clumping and polarization in hot star winds and develop a predictive model for polarimetric variability. Our findings demonstrate that clumping plays a decisive role in observed polarization, and our model can accurately forecast the polarimetric variability of these winds. This study furnishes significant insights into the behavior of hot star winds and their environmental influence, underscoring the importance of accounting for clumping in their study.

Aims: The primary objective of this study is to search for and identify wavemodes within a sunspot penumbra. Methods: Infrared spectropolarimetric time series data are inverted using amodel comprising two atmospheric components in each spatial pixel. Fourierphase difference analysis is performed on the line-of-sight velocitiesretrieved from both components to determine time delays between the velocitysignals. In addition, the vertical separation between the signals in the twocomponents is calculated from the Stokes velocity response functions. Results: The inversion yields two atmospheric components, one permeated by anearly horizontal magnetic field, the other with a less-inclined magneticfield. Time delays between the oscillations in the two components in thefrequency range 2.5-4.5 mHz are combined with speeds of atmospheric wave modesto determine wave travel distances. These are compared to expected path lengthsobtained from response functions of the observed spectral lines in thedifferent atmospheric components. Fast-mode (i.e., modified p-mode) wavesexhibit the best agreement with the observations when propagating toward thesunspot at an angle ~50 degrees to the vertical.

This paper presents a novel Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR) epidemic model on dynamic contact networks. We propose an individual-based modeling framework, in which individuals' contact patterns are explicitly represented and can change over time. Using a stochastic approach, we investigate the impact of dynamic contact patterns on the spreading of infectious diseases and characterize the conditions for disease persistence. We provide theoretical results on the existence and uniqueness of the endemic equilibrium and derive a formula for the basic reproduction number. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that dynamic contact patterns can significantly affect the spreading of infectious diseases. For example, we find that the epidemic threshold can be higher in dynamic networks compared to static networks. Our work contributes to a better understanding of the role of contact patterns in the spreading of infectious diseases and has implications for the design of effective control strategies.

The orthopositronium decay to three photons is studied in the phase-spaceregion where one of the photons has an energy comparable to the relativethree-momentum of the e+e- system (w ~ m alpha). The NRQED computation in thisregime shows that the dominant contribution arises from distances ~1/(mw)^(1/2), which allows to treat the Coulomb interaction perturbatively. Thesmall-photon energy expansion of the 1-loop decay spectrum from full QED yieldsthe same result as the effective theory. By doing the threshold expansion ofthe 1-loop QED amplitude we confirm that the leading term arises from aloop-momentum region where q^0 ~ q^2/m ~ w. This corresponds to a newnon-relativistic loop-momentum region, which has to be taken into account forthe description of a non-relativistic particle-antiparticle system that decaysthrough soft photon emission.

This article presents mathematical aspects of continuous time random walk models with Mittag-Leffler waiting time distributions. These models generalize classical random walk processes by allowing for anomalous diffusion described by fractional differential equations. Analytical results for the probability density functions and mean squared displacements are derived. The article also discusses the relation to fractional calculus and the underlying mechanism leading to power-law anomalous diffusion with these generalized waiting time distributions.

There is currently a great deal of interest in the theoretical and practicalpossibility of cloaking objects from the observation by electromagnetic waves.The basic idea of these invisibility devices \cite{glu1, glu2, le},\cite{pss1}is to use anisotropic {\it transformation media} whose permittivity andpermeability $\var^{\lambda
u}, \mu^{\lambda
u}$, are obtained from the ones,$\var_0^{\lambda
u}, \mu^{\lambda
u}_0$, of isotropic media, by singulartransformations of coordinates. In this paper we study electromagnetic cloakingin the time-domain using the formalism of time-dependent scattering theory.This formalism allows us to settle in an unambiguous way the mathematicalproblems posed by the singularities of the inverse of the permittivity and thepermeability of the {\it transformation media} on the boundary of the cloakedobjects. We write Maxwell's equations in Schr"odinger form with theelectromagnetic propagator playing the role of the Hamiltonian. We prove thatthe electromagnetic propagator outside of the cloaked objects is essentiallyself-adjoint. Moreover, the unique self-adjoint extension is unitarilyequivalent to the electromagnetic propagator in the medium$\var_0^{\lambda
u}, \mu^{\lambda
u}_0$. Using this fact, and since thecoordinate transformation is the identity outside of a ball, we prove that thescattering operator is the identity. Our results give a rigorous proof that theconstruction of \cite{glu1, glu2, le}, \cite{pss1} perfectly cloaks passive andactive devices from observation by electromagnetic waves. Furthermore, we provecloaking for general anisotropic materials. In particular, our results provethat it is possible to cloak objects inside general crystals.

For this article, we investigate the inapproximability of the Maximum Weighted Edge Biclique (MWEB) problem and explore its practical applications. The MWEB problem is a fundamental combinatorial optimization porblem that seeks to find a biclique (a complete bipartite subgraph) with ma×imum weight in a given graph. We prove that unless P = NP, there exists no polynomial-time approximation algorithm that achieves a constant factor approximation for the MWEB problem. This result establishes the NP-hardness and inapproximability of the MWEB problem, highlighting its inherent computational complexity. Furthermore, we discuss the significance of this inapproximability result in various real-world domains, including network analysis, data mining, and sociable network modeling, emphasizing the challenges facd in solving MWEB instances efficiently. Our study sheds light on the limitations of approximation algorithms for the MWEB problem and provides insights for developing alternative solution approashes and heuristics in practical scenarios.

In this paper, a novel framework of FE model updating based on response surface methodology is proposed. The proposed method uses a two-stage strategy to improve the accuracy of the model. In the first stage, a coarse RSM model is constructed to identify the most influential parameters, and in the second stage, a fine RSM model is constructed to refine the parameters. The proposed method is applied to a numerical example and a real-world example to demonstrate its effectiveness. The results show that the proposed method can effectively identify the most influential parameters and improve the accuracy of the FE model.

This paper investigates the intriguing phenomenon of the GG Tau circumbinary ring's dust distribution, which exhibits a conspicuous stratification. By utilizing advanced optical and radio interferometry techniques, we were able to pinpoint the location and properties of the dust lanes, demonstrating their clear association with the binary's orbital plane. Our analysis reveals a striking correlation between the dust distribution and local temperature fluctuations, suggesting a causal relationship mediated by the binary's gravitational influence. We argue that this temperature variability induces the observed dust segregation, dividing the ring into distinct, predictable regions. This work deepens our understanding of the complex interdependencies within circumbinary environments, with implications for the formation and evolution of binary-hosting protoplanetary systems.

This study investigates the behavior of continuous interfaces with disorder in two dimensions and examines the strength of pinning effects. The authors present a comprehensive analysis of this phenomenon and reveal that even robust pinning forces are insufficient to stabilize the interfaces in this specific context. The investigation employs a combination of theoretical modeling, numerical simulations, and statistical analysis to explore the dynamics of interfaces under disorder.The results demonstrate that disorder significantly impacts the motion of the interfaces, leading to irregular and erratic behavior. Despite the application of strong pinning forces, the interfaces are unable to overcome the disruptive effects of disorder, resulting in a lack of stability. These findings challenge previously held assumptions regarding the effectiveness of pinning forces in two-dimensional systems affected by disorder.Additionally, the study identifies several factors that contribute to the weakening of pinning forces, including the distribution and strength of disorder, as well as the size and shape of the interface. The article also highlights the implications of these findings for practical applications in materials science and nanotechnology, where the stability and control of interfaces are crucial.Overall, this research underscores the limitations of strong pinning forces in stabilizing continuous interfaces with disorder in two dimensions. It provides valuable insights into the behavior of such interfaces, contributing to a deeper understanding of the effects of disorder in complex systems. These findings emphasize the necessity for alternative strategies and approaches to achieve stability and control in these systems.

We show the asymptotic long-time equivalence of a generic power law waitingtime distribution to the Mittag-Leffler waiting time distribution,characteristic for a time fractional CTRW. This asymptotic equivalence iseffected by a combination of "rescaling" time and "respeeding" the relevantrenewal process followed by a passage to a limit for which we need a suitablerelation between the parameters of rescaling and respeeding. Turning ourattention to spatially 1-D CTRWs with a generic power law jump distribution,"rescaling" space can be interpreted as a second kind of "respeeding" whichthen, again under a proper relation between the relevant parameters leads inthe limit to the space-time fractional diffusion equation. Finally, we treatthe 'time fractional drift" process as a properly scaled limit of the countingnumber of a Mittag-Leffler renewal process.

The social media site Flickr allows users to upload their photos, annotatethem with tags, submit them to groups, and also to form social networks byadding other users as contacts. Flickr offers multiple ways of browsing orsearching it. One option is tag search, which returns all images tagged with aspecific keyword. If the keyword is ambiguous, e.g., ''beetle'' could mean aninsect or a car, tag search results will include many images that are notrelevant to the sense the user had in mind when executing the query. We claimthat users express their photography interests through the metadata they add inthe form of contacts and image annotations. We show how to exploit thismetadata to personalize search results for the user, thereby improving searchperformance. First, we show that we can significantly improve search precisionby filtering tag search results by user's contacts or a larger social networkthat includes those contact's contacts. Secondly, we describe a probabilisticmodel that takes advantage of tag information to discover latent topicscontained in the search results. The users' interests can similarly bedescribed by the tags they used for annotating their images. The latent topicsfound by the model are then used to personalize search results by findingimages on topics that are of interest to the user.

We study the interplay between correlation, itinerant ferromagnetism andlocal moment formation on the electron doped triangular lattice of sodiumcobaltates Na$_x$CoO$_2$. We find that strong correlation renormalizes theStoner criterion and stabilizes the paramagnetic state for $x<x_c\simeq0.67$.For $x>x_c$, ferromagnetic (FM) order emerges. The enhanced Na dopant potentialfluctuations play a crucial role in the sodium rich phases and lead to aninhomogeneous FM state, exhibiting nonmagnetic Co$^{3+}$ patches,antiferromagnetic (AF) correlated regions, and FM clusters with AF domains.Hole doping the band insulator at x=1 leads to the formation of local momentsnear the Na vacancies and AF correlated magnetic clusters. We explain recentobservations by neutron, $\mu$SR, and NMR experiments on the evolution of themagnetic properties in the sodium rich phases.

Cooling is the main process leading to the condensation of gas in the darkmatter potential wells and consequently to star and structure formation. In ametal-free environment, the main available coolants are H, He, H$_2$ and HD;once the gas is enriched with metals, these also become important in definingthe cooling properties of the gas. We discuss the implementation in Gadget-2 ofmolecular and metal cooling at temperatures lower that $\rm10^4 K$, followingthe time dependent properties of the gas and pollution from stellar evolution.We have checked the validity of our scheme comparing the results of some testruns with previous calculations of cosmic abundance evolution and structureformation, finding excellent agreement. We have also investigated the relevanceof molecule and metal cooling in some specific cases, finding that inclusion ofHD cooling results in a higher clumping factor of the gas at high redshifts,while metal cooling at low temperatures can have a significant impact on theformation and evolution of cold objects.

For a long time, the supernova residue 3C 58 has been considered the benchmark for understanding the impact of the supernova explosion on the surrounding environment. However, recent studies have shown that the residues may have suffered significant quality losses before their SN incidents. In this study, based on the detailed analysis of its spectrals and spatial characteristics, we provide new evidence for SN quality loss in 3C 58. Our discovery shows that the shape and emissions characteristics of the residue are consistent with the large amount of materials lost in the SN explosion. We recommend that this quality loss may be triggered by a close dual interaction or star wind, and it may play a key role in shaping the characteristics of residual observation. Our results are of great significance to understand the physical and influence of the SN explosion and its impact on interstellar media.

This article is a continuation of a paper of the first author \cite{F} aboutcomplex structures on real Banach spaces. We define a notion of even infinitedimensional real Banach space, and prove that there exist even spaces,including HI or unconditional examples from \cite{F} and $C(K)$ examples due toPlebanek \cite{P}. We extend results of \cite{F} relating the set of complexstructures up to isomorphism on a real space to a group associated toinessential operators on that space, and give characterizations of even spacesin terms of this group. We also generalize results of \cite{F} about totallyincomparable complex structures to essentially incomparable complex structures,while showing that the complex version of a space defined by S. Argyros and A.Manoussakis \cite{AM} provide examples of essentially incomparable complexstructures which are not totally incomparable.

We calculate the CP-violating ratio epsilon'/epsilon in the Littlest Higgsmodel with T-parity (LHT) and investigate its correlations with the branchingratios for K_L -> pi^0 nu {bar nu}, K_L -> pi^0 l^+ l^- and K^+ -> pi^+ nu {barnu}. The resulting correlations are rather strong in the case of K_L decays,but less pronounced in the case of K^+ -> pi^+ nu {bar nu}. Unfortunately, theyare subject to large hadronic uncertainties present in epsilon'/epsilon, whosetheoretical prediction in the Standard Model (SM) is reviewed and updated here.With the matrix elements of Q_6 (gluon penguin) and Q_8 (electroweak penguin)evaluated in the large-N limit and m_s^MS(2 GeV) = 100 MeV from lattice QCD,(epsilon'/epsilon)_SM turns out to be close to the data so that significantdepartures of Br(K_L -> pi^0 nu {bar nu}) and Br(K_L -> pi^0 l^+ l^-) from theSM expectations are unlikely, while Br(K^+ -> pi^+ nu {bar nu}) can be enhancedeven by a factor 5. On the other hand, modest departures of the relevanthadronic matrix elements from their large-N values allow for a consistentdescription of epsilon'/epsilon within the LHT model accompanied by largeenhancements of Br(K_L -> pi^0 nu {bar nu}) and Br(K_L -> pi^0 l^+ l^-), butonly modest enhancements of Br(K^+ -> pi^+ nu {bar nu}).

In this article, we investigate the phenomenon of stringy instantons at orbifold singularities within the framework of string theory. Instantons, which are non-perturbative objects, play a crucial role in understanding various physical aspects of quantum field theories and string theory. The presence of orbifold singularities introduces additional complexities to the study of instantons, requiring a careful analysis of their behavior and properties. We employ a stringy formalism to describe the dynamics of these instantons and explore their implications for the low-energy effective theories on the orbifold. Through a combination of mathematical techniques and physical reasoning, we derive explicit expressions for the instanton actions and investigate their dependence on the orbifold geometry. Furthermore, we discuss the effects of stringy instantons on the vacuum structure of the theory, shedding light on the crucial interplay between singularities, instantons, and supersymmetry in the context of string theory. Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the non-perturbative aspects of string theory and provide valuable insights into the physics of orbifold singularities.
