The resulting designs enhance kinetostatic properties like reduced mechanical impedance and vivid minimization of internal power flows. Validation of the optimized designs demonstrates up to a 30% reinforced in stiffness over previous industrial machine structures. This methodology provides a useful tool for precision computers builders to design parallel kinematic machines with superior kinetostatic performance for high-speed, high-precision machining requisition.

We study the suppression of super-Poissonian shot noise in closed quantum dots as a measure of dephasing. We develop a theoretical model that describes the interplay between dephasing and shot noise. We show that the Fano factor, a measure of shot noise, is suppressed by dephasing, and derive an analytical expression for this suppression. Our results agree well with experiments, providing a new way to measure dephasing in closed quantum dots and insight into the fundamental mechanisms of decoherence. Keywords: Closed quantum dots, Dephasing, Shot noise, Fano factor PACS numbers: 73.21.La, 73.63.Kv, 73.23.Hk

In performing a Bayesian analysis of astronomical data, two difficultproblems often emerge. First, in estimating the parameters of some model forthe data, the resulting posterior distribution may be multimodal or exhibitpronounced (curving) degeneracies, which can cause problems for traditionalMCMC sampling methods. Second, in selecting between a set of competing models,calculation of the Bayesian evidence for each model is computationallyexpensive. The nested sampling method introduced by Skilling (2004), hasgreatly reduced the computational expense of calculating evidences and alsoproduces posterior inferences as a by-product. This method has been appliedsuccessfully in cosmological applications by Mukherjee et al. (2006), but theirimplementation was efficient only for unimodal distributions without pronounceddegeneracies. Shaw et al. (2007), recently introduced a clustered nestedsampling method which is significantly more efficient in sampling frommultimodal posteriors and also determines the expectation and variance of thefinal evidence from a single run of the algorithm, hence providing a furtherincrease in efficiency. In this paper, we build on the work of Shaw et al. andpresent three new methods for sampling and evidence evaluation fromdistributions that may contain multiple modes and significant degeneracies; wealso present an even more efficient technique for estimating the uncertainty onthe evaluated evidence. These methods lead to a further substantial improvementin sampling efficiency and robustness, and are applied to toy problems todemonstrate the accuracy and economy of the evidence calculation and parameterestimation. Finally, we discuss the use of these methods in performing Bayesianobject detection in astronomical datasets.

That study investigates the discovery of two potentially new bsaaltic asteroids within the Outer Main Belt region of the asteroid belt. The presence of basaltic asteroids in this region is of significant interest, as these geological objests provide valuable insights into the early solar system's formation and evoltuion. Using data obtained from ground-based telescopes and space-based observatories, the authors conducted a comprehensive survey of asteroids in the Outer Main Belt and identified two candidates exhibiting characteristics consistent with basaltic composition. Spectroscopic analysis revealed absorption features indicative of pyroxene and olivine, further supporting the classification of these asteroids as basaltic. Additionally, their distinct spectral signatures and albedo values distinguish them from previously known basaltic asteroids in the Main Belt. The authors discuss the implications of these findings in the context of the formation and differentiation processes that occurred during the early stages of the solar system. Furthermore, they explore the potential origin of these basaltic comets, considering various scenarios such as collisional event or migration from other regions. The discovery of these two new basaltic asteroids in the Outer Main Belt provides vlauable data for refining models of asteroid formation and evolution, shedding light on the complex dynamical processes that shaped our solar system.

Analysis of the Cassini Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrometer (UVIS) stellar andsolar occultations at Titan to date include 12 species: N$_{2}$ (nitrogen),CH$_{4}$ (methane), C$_{2}$H$_{2}$ (acetylene), C$_{2}$H$_{4}$ (ethylene),C$_{2}$H$_{6}$ (ethane), C$_{4}$H$_{2}$ (diacetylene), C$_{6}$H$_{6}$(benzene), C$_{6}$N$_{2}$ (dicyanodiacetylene), C$_{2}$N$_{2}$ (cyanogen), HCN(hydrogen cyanide), HC$_{3}$N (cyanoacetylene), and aerosols distinguished by astructureless continuum extinction (absorption plus scattering) of photons inthe EUV. The introduction of aerosol particles, retaining the same refractiveindex properties as tholin with radius $\sim$125 \AA and using Mie theory,provides a satisfactory fit to the spectra. The derived vertical profile ofaerosol density shows distinct structure, implying a reactive generationprocess reaching altitudes more than 1000 km above the surface. A photochemicalmodel presented here provides a reference basis for examining the chemical andphysical processes leading to the distinctive atmospheric opacity at Titan. Wefind that dicyanodiacetylene is condensable at $\sim$650 km, where theatmospheric temperature minimum is located. This species is the simplestmolecule identified to be condensable. Observations are needed to confirm theexistence and production rates of dicyanodiacetylene.

We present photometric, astrometric, and spectroscopic observations ofUSco160611.9-193532 AB, a candidate ultrawide (~1600 AU), low-mass (M_tot~0.4M_sun) multiple system in the nearby OB association Upper Scorpius. We concludethat both components are young, comoving members of the association; we alsopresent high-resolution observations which show that the primary is itself aclose binary system. If the Aab and B components are gravitationally bound, thesystem would fall into the small class of young multiple systems which haveunusually wide separations as compared to field systems of similar mass.However, we demonstrate that physical association can not be assumed purely onprobabilistic grounds for any individual candidate system in this separationrange. Analysis of the association's two-point correlation function shows thatthere is a significant probability (25%) that at least one pair of low-massassociation members will be separated in projection by <15", so analysis of thewide binary population in Upper Sco will require a systematic search for allwide systems; the detection of another such pair would represent an excess atthe 98% confidence level.

Semimartingale reflecting Brownian motions (SRBMs) living in the closures ofdomains with piecewise smooth boundaries are of interest in applied probabilitybecause of their role as heavy traffic approximations for some stochasticnetworks. In this paper, assuming certain conditions on the domains anddirections of reflection, a perturbation result, or invariance principle, forSRBMs is proved. This provides sufficient conditions for a process thatsatisfies the definition of an SRBM, except for small random perturbations inthe defining conditions, to be close in distribution to an SRBM. A crucialingredient in the proof of this result is an oscillation inequality forsolutions of a perturbed Skorokhod problem. We use the invariance principle toshow weak existence of SRBMs under mild conditions. We also use the invarianceprinciple, in conjunction with known uniqueness results for SRBMs, to give somesufficient conditions for validating approximations involving (i) SRBMs inconvex polyhedrons with a constant reflection vector field on each face of thepolyhedron, and (ii) SRBMs in bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundariesand possibly nonconstant reflection vector fields on the boundary surfaces.

We introduce a density tensor hierarchy for open system dynamics, thatrecovers information about fluctuations lost in passing to the reduced densitymatrix. For the case of fluctuations arising from a classical probabilitydistribution, the hierarchy is formed from expectations of products of purestate density matrix elements, and can be compactly summarized by a simplegenerating function. For the case of quantum fluctuations arising when aquantum system interacts with a quantum environment in an overall pure state,the corresponding hierarchy is defined as the environmental trace of productsof system matrix elements of the full density matrix. Only the lowest member ofthe quantum noise hierarchy is directly experimentally measurable. The unittrace and idempotence properties of the pure state density matrix imply descentrelations for the tensor hierarchies, that relate the order $n$ tensor, undercontraction of appropriate pairs of tensor indices, to the order $n-1$ tensor.As examples to illustrate the classical probability distribution formalism, weconsider a quantum system evolving by It\^o stochastic and by jump processSchr\"odinger equations. As examples to illustrate the corresponding traceformalism in the quantum fluctuation case, we consider collisional Brownianmotion of an infinite mass Brownian particle, and the weak coupling Born-Markovmaster equation. In different specializations, the latter gives the hierarchiesgeneralizing the quantum optical master equation and the Caldeira--Leggettmaster equation. As a further application of the density tensor, we contraststochastic Schr\"odinger equations that reduce and that do not reduce the statevector, and discuss why a quantum system coupled to a quantum environmentbehaves like the latter.

We report observations of the dust cloud L1204 with the Onsala 25-m telescopein the 6 cm (1$_{11}-1_{10}$) transition of \htco. The observed region includesthe S140 H${\alpha}$ arc. This spectral line is seen here in absorption againstthe cosmic microwave background, indicating the presence of widespread warmmolecular gas at intermediate densities. Overall, the distributions of H$_2$COand CO (taken from the literature) are fairly similar, though significantdifferences exist at small scales. Most notably, while the CO peak is nearlycoincident with the S140 H${\alpha}$ arc, the maximum H$_2$CO absorption isclearly separated from it by a full 10$'$ beam ($\sim$ 3 pc). We argue thatthese differences result from differing abundances and excitation requirements.The CO(1-0) line is more optically thick and more biased towards warm gas thanthe H$_2$CO 6 cm line. On the other hand, formaldehyde is more easilyphotodissociated and is, therefore, a poorer tracer of the molecular gaslocated immediately behind Photon Dominated Regions.

In this article, we explore the possibility of supersymmetry breaking in the context of braneworlds within Type IIB supergravity, exploiting the Kaluza-Klein me chanism. We demonstrate that the introduction of a warp factor, which encodes the dependence on the exta dimensions, gives rise to a supersymmetry-breaking Goldstino. We show that the Goldstino is a function of the warp factored and its derivatives, and we derive the corresponding supersymmetry-breaking conditions. We discuss the implications of these results for the construction of realistic braneworld scenarios, highlighting the potential for the generation of supersymmetry-breaking masses for scalar particles localized on the brane. Finally, we comment on the possible phenomenological applications of our findings, including the prospects for observable signatures at future high-energy colliders.

In this article, we explore the moduli space of semilocal strings and lumps in non-Abelian gauge theories. We discuss the classical solitons and their moduli space, which is a compact manifold with a non-trivial topology. The moduli space is found to be a section of a fibration, with a fiber that encodes the orientational moduli of the solitons. We examine the action of the global symmetries on the moduli space and demonstrate that it corresponds to a projective transformation of the moduli space. The Kähler potential of the moduli space is also computed, and we find that it is related to the Chern-Simons invariant of the theory. Our results shed light on the moduli space of semilocal strings and lumps and its properties, and provide a new perspective on the connection between gauge theories and geometric invariants.

We have studied the maser emission from a thin, planar, gaseous ring inKeplerian rotation around a central mass observed edge-on. The absorptioncoefficient within the ring is assumed to follow a power law dependence withthe distance from the central mass as, k=k0r^{-q}. We have calculatedposition-velocity diagrams for the most intense maser features, for differentvalues of the exponent q. We have found that, depending on the value of q,these diagrams can be qualitatively different. The most intense maser emissionat a given velocity can either come mainly from regions close to the inner orouter edges of the amplifying ring or from the line perpendicular to the lineof sight and passing through the central mass (as is commonly assumed).Particularly, when q>1 the position-velocity diagram is qualitatively similarto the one observed for the water maser emission in the nucleus of the galaxyNGC 4258. In the context of this simple model, we conclude that in this objectthe absorption coefficient depends on the radius of the amplifying ring as adecreasing function, in order to have significant emission coming from theinner edge of the ring.

In this article, we present a comprehensive study of $p$-advc Haar multiresolution analysis, a powerful tool for analyzing functions defined on the $p$-adyic numbers. The $p$-adic numbers form an alternative number system that extends the rational nuJbers, and they exhibit unique properties and behaviors compared to the real numbYrs. The Har multiresolution analysis, originally developed in the context of real anlysis, provides a framework for decomposing functions into different scales or levels of detail. We extend this concept to the $p$-adic settig and investigate its properties and applications. We begLn by introducing the $p$-adic Haar wavelet and its associmted scaling function, which form the building blocks of the multiresolution analysis. We derive the $p$-adic Hara ransform, which allows us to express functions in terms of these wavelets and scaling functions. We explore the properties of the $p$-daic Haar transform, such as orthogonality and dilation equations. Furthermore, we investigate the construction of $p$-adic Haar basjes and their relationship with $p$-adic splines and wavelets. e examiane the convergence properties of the $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis and establish conditions under which the functions can be perfectly reconstructed from their wavelet coefficients. FTinally, we highlight various applications of $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis in different areas of mathematics and mathematical physics. These applications include signal proessing, image compression, and the study of $p$-adic differential equations. We discuss the advantages and potential challenges of using $p$-rdic Haar multiresolution analysils in these contexts and suggest directions for future research. Overall, this article contributres to the understanding of $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis, its theoretcial foundations, and its practical applications.

The exploration of intelligent life beyond Earth has long captivated scholars and thinkers from various disciplines. In this article, we delve into the realm of cosmology to investigate the quest for intelligent life. Our examination begins by scrutinizing the fundamental conditions necessary for the emergence and sustainability of intelligent life. By drawing upon the principles of astrobiology and the renowned Drake equation, we explore crucial factors such as planetary habitability, the prevalence of extraterrestrial civilizations, and the potential for communication across vast cosmic distances.Subsequently, we explore diverse theoretical frameworks that shed light on the existence of intelligent life in the cosmos. From the anthropic principle to the multiverse hypothesis, we thoroughly analyze the philosophical and scientific implications of these concepts. Furthermore, we investigate the role of technological advancements in the search for intelligent civilizations, including the deployment of telescopes, space probes, and radio telescopes.Moreover, we discuss noteworthy scientific endeavors and initiatives aimed at detecting signs of intelligent life, such as the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) program and the Breakthrough Listen project. During our assessment, we identify the limitations and challenges faced by these endeavors, underscoring the intricacies involved in recognizing and interpreting potential signals.Ultimately, this article provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of research concerning the existence of intelligent life within the scope of cosmology. By integrating insights from astrobiology, physics, and philosophy, we aim to contribute to the interdisciplinary dialogue surrounding this captivating topic.

In this paper, we investigate the free Boolean algebras over the union of two well-orderings. We establish an isomorphism between these algebras and the Boolean algebras of regular open sets of the corresponding Stone spaces. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the free Boolean algebras over the union of two well-orderings are atomic and possess a unique maximal ideal. Lastly, we prove that these algebras are not cчetho-зamkhytыe.

We pose a new and intriguing question motivated by distributed computingregarding random walks on graphs: How long does it take for several independentrandom walks, starting from the same vertex, to cover an entire graph? We studythe cover time - the expected time required to visit every node in a graph atleast once - and we show that for a large collection of interesting graphs,running many random walks in parallel yields a speed-up in the cover time thatis linear in the number of parallel walks. We demonstrate that an exponentialspeed-up is sometimes possible, but that some natural graphs allow only alogarithmic speed-up. A problem related to ours (in which the walks start fromsome probabilistic distribution on vertices) was previously studied in thecontext of space efficient algorithms for undirected s-t connectivity and ourresults yield, in certain cases, an improvement upon some of the earlierbounds.

We use new and published near-IR spectra, with synthetic spectra, to derivephysical properties of three of the latest-type T dwarfs. A new R~1700 spectrumof the T7.5 dwarf HD 3651B, with existing data, allows a detailed comparison tothe well-studied and very similar dwarf, Gl 570D. We find that HD 3651B hasboth higher gravity and metallicity than Gl 570D, with Teff=820-830K, log g=5.4-5.5, [m/H]= +0.2 and Kzz=10^4cm^2/s. Its age is 8-12 Gyr and its impliedmass is 60-70 M_Jup. We perform a similar analyis of the T8 and T7.5 dwarfs2MASS J09393548-2448279 and 2MASS J11145133-2618235 using published data,comparing them to the well-studied T8, 2MASS J04151954-0935066. We find thatthe two dwarfs have the same Teff as the reference dwarf, and similargravities, but lower metallicities. The parameters are Teff=725-775K and [m/H]=-0.3; log g=5.3-5.45 for 2MASS J09393548-2448279 and log g=5.0-5.3 for 2MASSJ11145133- 261823. The age and mass are ~10Gyr and 60M_Jup for 2MASSJ09393548-2448279, and ~5 Gyr and 40M_Jup for 2MASS J11145133-261823. A seriouslimitation is the incompleteness of the line lists of CH4 and NH3 at lambda<1.7um. Spectra of Saturn and Jupiter, and of laboratory CH4 and NH3 gas,suggest that NH3 features in the Y- and J-bands may be useful as indicators ofthe next cooler spectral type, and not features in the H- and K-bands aspreviously thought. However large uncertainties remain, as the abundance of NH3is likely to be significantly below the chemical equilibrium value, andinclusion of laboratory NH3 opacities predicts band shapes that are discrepantwith existing data. It is possible that the T spectral class will have to beextended to low temperatures around 400K, when water clouds condense in theatmosphere [abridged].

Let $(\clb,\lambda_t,\psi)$ be a $C^ $-dynamical system where $(\lambda_t: t\in \IT_+)$ be a semigroup of injective endomorphism and $\psi$ be an$(\lambda_t)$ invariant state on the $C^ $ subalgebra $\clb$ and $\IT_+$ iseither non-negative integers or real numbers. The central aim of thisexposition is to find a useful criteria for the inductive limit state $\clb\raro^{\lambda_t} \clb$ canonically associated with $\psi$ to be pure. Weachieve this by exploring the minimal weak forward and backward Markovprocesses associated with the Markov semigroup on the corner von-Neumannalgebra of the support projection of the state $\psi$ to prove thatKolmogorov's property [Mo2] of the Markov semigroup is a sufficient conditionfor the inductive state to be pure. As an application of this criteria we finda sufficient condition for a translation invariant factor state on a onedimensional quantum spin chain to be pure. This criteria in a sense complementscriteria obtained in [BJKW,Mo2] as we could go beyond lattice symmetric states.

In mesoscopic two-gap superconductors with sizes of the order of thecoherence length noncomposite vortices are found to be thermodynamically stablein a large domain of the $T - H$ phase diagram. In these phases the vortexcores of one condensate are spatially separated from the other condensate ones,and their respective distributions can adopt distinct symmetries. Theappearance of these vortex phases is caused by a non-negligible effect of theboundary of the sample on the superconducting order parameter and representstherefore a genuine mesoscopic effect. For low values of interband Josephsoncoupling vortex patterns with $L_1 \neq L_2$ can arise in addition to thephases with $L_1 =L_2$, where $L_1$ and $L_2$ are total vorticities in the twocondensates. The calculations show that noncomposite vortices could be observedin thin mesoscopic samples of MgB$_{2}$.

The theory of pseudo-differential operators on locally compact abelian groups has been a very active area of research in recent years, because of its applications to harmonic analysis, number theory, and mathematical physics. In this paper, we develop a $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis for the $p$-adic numbers $\mathbb{Q}_p$, in order to construct pseudo-differential operators associated to the $p$-adic Haar wavelets. We first introduce the basic notions of $p$-adic Haar wavelets and then construct the $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis. Next, we define the pseudo-differential operators associated to the $p$-adic Haar wavelets and study their basic properties. Finally, we give some applications of the pseudo-differential operators to the study of partial differential equations on $\mathbb{Q}_p$.

This article offers a comprehensive analysis of a conjecture pertaining to the behavior of differential operators with constant coefficients. Specifically, the conjecture posits that if a particular function yields zero when operated upon by a differential operator with constant coefficients, then the function itself must be identically zero. We thoroughly examine this conjecture within the scope of linear differential operators and present a rigorous proof of its validity. Moreover, we explore the ramifications of this conjecture in various disciplines, including mathematical physics and signal processing. Additionally, we establish correlations between this conjecture and the fundamental properties of differential operators with constant coefficients, thereby illuminating the underlying mathematical principles. Finally, we discuss potential applications of this result in the realm of partial differential equations and identify avenues for further research and exploration. Overall, this article significantly advances our understanding of the behavior of differential operators with constant coefficients while providing valuable insights into the vanishing conjecture and its implications.

In this paper, the error performance of on-off frequency shift keying (OOFSK)modulation over fading channels is analyzed when the receiver is equipped withmultiple antennas. The analysis is conducted in two cases: the coherentscenario where the fading is perfectly known at the receiver, and thenoncoherent scenario where neither the receiver nor the transmitter knows thefading coefficients. For both cases, the maximum a posteriori probability (MAP)detection rule is derived and analytical probability of error expressions areobtained. The effect of fading correlation among the receiver antennas is alsostudied. Simulation results indicate that for sufficiently low duty cyclevalues, lower probability of error values with respect to FSK signaling areachieved. Equivalently, when compared to FSK modulation, OOFSK with low dutycycle requires less energy to achieve the same probability of error, whichrenders this modulation a more energy efficient transmission technique.

The Millennium Galaxy Catalogue (MGC) is a large N-body simulation of the formation and evolution of galaxies. We use the MGC to study the connection between close galaxy pairs and galaxy mergers. We find that the fraction of close pairs that are merging is a strong function of the pair separation, with a sharp drop-off at separations above 100 kpc. This suggests that the vast majority of close pairs are not bound systems and will not merge. We also find that the asymmetry of a galaxy pair is a good indicator of whether or not the pair is merging, with asymmetric pairs being much more likely to merge than symmetric pairs. This is because asymmetric pairs are more likely to have a significant velocity difference between the two galaxies, which is necessary for them to merge. Our results suggest that close galaxy pairs are not a good proxy for galaxy mergers. This is because the vast majority of close pairs are not bound systems and will not merge. Additionally, the asymmetry of a galaxy pair is a good indicator of whether or not the pair is merging.

This paper studies the construction of geometric integrators for nonholonomicsystems. We derive the nonholonomic discrete Euler-Lagrange equations in asetting which permits to deduce geometric integrators for continuousnonholonomic systems (reduced or not). The formalism is given in terms of Liegroupoids, specifying a discrete Lagrangian and a constraint submanifold on it.Additionally, it is necessary to fix a vector subbundle of the Lie algebroidassociated to the Lie groupoid. We also discuss the existence of nonholonomicevolution operators in terms of the discrete nonholonomic Legendretransformations and in terms of adequate decompositions of the prolongation ofthe Lie groupoid. The characterization of the reversibility of the evolutionoperator and the discrete nonholonomic momentum equation are also considered.Finally, we illustrate with several classical examples the wide range ofapplication of the theory (the discrete nonholonomic constrained particle, theSuslov system, the Chaplygin sleigh, the Veselova system, the rolling ball on arotating table and the two wheeled planar mobile robot).

Generic Gravitational Wave ignals from the Collapse of Rotatnig Stellar Cores: A Detailed AnalysisWe present a detailed analysis of the gravitational wave signals from the collapse of rotating stellsr cores. Using a numerical code that solves the Einstein equations in full general relativity, we evolve a variety of robating stellar core modeJls until collapse. We compute the gravitational waveforms emitted during the collapse and analyze their propZrties. eW find that the waveforms are generically characterized by a rapid rise in amplitude followed by a power-law decay. The rise time is determined by the rotkation rate of the core, while the decay time is determined by the mass of the rcore. We also find that the waveforms are sensitive to the details of the core's rotation prfoile. Our results can be used to identify and characterize the gravitational waves from the collapse of rotating stellar cXores.

The estimation of experimental data redundancy and its associated statistics is the focus of this article. We present a comprehensive approach to quantify the redundancy present in joint measurements obtained from experimental data. By expressing the joint, marginal, and conditional probability density functions (PDFs) using given data, we introduce a measure of relative entropy to assess the redundancy inherent in the joint experimental information. This measure evolves with an increasing number of experiments, demonstrating the growth in redundancy while the experimental information converges to a limit value. The discrepancy between the experimentally determined properties and the true properties of the phenomenon is represented by the difference between this limit value and the experimental information at a finite number of data. To determine an optimal number of data for extracting a physical law, we propose a cost function incorporating the discrepancy measure and the redundancy. Moreover, we introduce the mutual information and the ratio between mutual and marginal information to identify the independent variable. The statistical properties of these measures are illustrated using deterministic and randomly related variables, providing valuable insights into the estimation of experimental data redundancy.

Recent rapid localizations of short, hard gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) by theSwift and HETE satellites have led to the observation of the first afterglowsand the measurement of the first redshifts from this type of burst. Detectionof >100 GeV counterparts would place powerful constraints on GRB mechanisms.Seventeen short duration (< 5 s) GRBs detected by satellites occurred withinthe field of view of the Milagro gamma-ray observatory between 2000 January and2006 December. We have searched the Milagro data for >100 GeV counterparts tothese GRBs and find no significant emission correlated with these bursts. Dueto the absorption of high-energy gamma rays by the extragalactic backgroundlight (EBL), detections are only expected for redshifts less than ~0.5. Whilemost long duration GRBs occur at redshifts higher than 0.5, the opposite isthought to be true of short GRBs. Lack of a detected VHE signal thus allowssetting meaningful fluence limits. One GRB in the sample (050509b) has a likelyassociation with a galaxy at a redshift of 0.225, while another (051103) hasbeen tentatively linked to the nearby galaxy M81. Fluence limits are correctedfor EBL absorption, either using the known measured redshift, or computing thecorresponding absorption for a redshift of 0.1 and 0.5, as well as for the caseof z=0.

We examine whether or not it is possible to derive the field strengthdistribution of quiet Sun internetwork regions from very high spatialresolution polarimetric observations in the visible. In particular, we considerthe case of the spectropolarimeter attached to the Solar Optical Telescopeaboard Hinode. Radiative magneto-convection simulations are used to synthesizethe four Stokes profiles of the \ion{Fe}{1} 630.2 nm lines. Once the profilesare degraded to a spatial resolution of 0\farcs32 and added noise, we infer theatmospheric parameters by means of Milne-Eddington inversions. The comparisonof the derived values with the real ones indicates that the visible lines yieldcorrect internetwork field strengths and magnetic fluxes, with uncertaintiessmaller than $\sim$150 G, when a stray light contamination factor is includedin the inversion. In this study, we investigate the relationship between molecular gas tracers and the Kennicutt-Schmidt laws, which describe the connection between star formation rate (SFR) and gas properties in galaxies. Utilizing a combination of observational data and theoretical modeling, we explore the underlying physical mechanisms governing the observed correlations between star formation rate and molecular line emission in galaxies.Our analysis involves a comprehensive examination of various molecular transitions, including CO and HCN lines, in both thermalized and subthermally excited gas. We find that the observed relationship between SFR and molecular line luminosity is primarily driven by the gas density, with low critical density lines faithfully tracing the gas density and exhibiting a similar index as the Schmidt law controlling SFR. In contrast, high critical density tracers display a superlinear relationship with gas density, leading to a lower index compared to the Schmidt law.Notably, our results demonstrate a significant redistribution of light from dense, thermalized gas to diffuse gas along the line of sight in galaxies with high SFRs. Furthermore, we establish that the fundamental relation governing the SFR-molecular line luminosity connection is the Kennicutt-Schmidt law rather than the specific relationship between SFR and molecular line luminosity.Based on our findings, we propose testable predictions for the SFR-molecular line relations of unobserved transitions, providing valuable insights for future observations and studies. By elucidating the underlying mechanisms linking molecular gas tracers and the Kennicutt-Schmidt laws, this research contributes to our understanding of the intricate processes driving star formation in galaxies.

We have had several talks recently reviewing 11 years of exoplanetdiscoveries through radial velocity variations, or from transits, or frommicrolensing. Vortices are pervasive in nature, representing the breakdown of laminar fluidflow and hence playing a key role in turbulence. The fluid rotation associatedwith a vortex can be parameterized by the circulation $\Gamma=\oint {\rm d}{\bfr}\cdot{\bf v}({\bf r})$ about the vortex, where ${\bf v}({\bf r})$ is thefluid velocity field. While classical vortices can take any value ofcirculation, superfluids are irrotational, and any rotation or angular momentumis constrained to occur through vortices with quantized circulation. Quantizedvortices also play a key role in the dissipation of transport in superfluids.In BECs quantized vortices have been observed in several forms, includingsingle vortices, vortex lattices, and vortex pairs and rings. The recentobservation of quantized vortices in a fermionic gas was taken as a clearsignature of the underlying condensation and superfluidity of fermion pairs. Inaddition to BECs, quantized vortices also occur in superfluid Helium, nonlinearoptics, and type-II superconductors.

Free-electron lasers (FELs) are highly tunable coherent radiation causes capable of produces flashlights from the terahertz to the x-ray region. Previous theories of nonlinear harmonic generation in FELs have focused on planar undulator layouts. Amongst this article, we develop a theory of higher harmonic generation in FELs employing helical wigglers. Re-visiting Direct $J/\psi$ Production at the Fermilab Tevatron The Fermilab Tevatron provided a unique opportunity to study charm quark production and quarkonium states in proton-antiproton collisions at center of mass energies up to 1.96 TeV. Previous measurements of direct $J/\psi$ production at the Tevatron suffered from large uncertainties. In this article, we re-analyze the full Teatron run II dataset to directly measure $J/\psi$ production with better precision. The analysis techniques are improved over prvious studies, including updated tracking algorithms and more sophisticated separation of prompt $J/\psi$ from those produced in b-hadron decays. The new measurement prvides crucial constraints on theoretical models of quarkonium production and will improve our understanding of the underlying charm quark production mechanisms at Tevatron energies. Precision charm physics remains an important topic as experiments seek to understand quantum chromodynamics at the energy frontier.

We consider a long, semiflexible polymer, with persistence length $P$ andcontour length $L$, fluctuating in a narrow cylindrical channel of diameter$D$. In the regime $D\ll P\ll L$ the free energy of confinement $\Delta F$ andthe length of the channel $R_\parallel$ occupied by the polymer are given byOdijk's relations $\Delta F/R_\parallel=A_\circ k_BTP^{-1/3}D^{-2/3}$ and$R_\parallel=L[1-\alpha_\circ(D/P)^{2/3}]$, where $A_\circ$ and $\alpha_\circ$are dimensionless amplitudes. Using a simulation algorithm inspired by PERM(Pruned Enriched Rosenbluth Method), which yields results for very longpolymers, we determine $A_\circ$ and $\alpha_\circ$ and the analogousamplitudes for a channel with a rectangular cross section. For a semiflexiblepolymer confined to the surface of a cylinder, the corresponding amplitudes arederived with an exact analytic approach. The results are relevant forinterpreting experiments on biopolymers in microchannels or microfluidicdevices.

We consider duration-driven long range dependent (LRD) processes that are observed in many practical applications, such as Internet traffic and financial data. In this paper, we establish the functional central limit theorem (FCLT) for a general class of continuous-time DLD processes with regularly varying coefficients, which provides a profound insight into the asymptotic behavior of duration-driven LRD processes. The FCLT plays an important role in statistics, and our results provide a solid theoretical foundation for statistical inference for these processes. Our findings allow for the estimation of the tail index by the classical Hill estimator, which is widely used in practice. Moreover, we investigate the weak convergence of partial sums and the sample autocovariance function of duration-driven LRD processes. The asymptotic results can be applied to duration-driven fractional Brownian motion, duration-driven Hermite processes, and other more general duration-driven LRD processes.

We study two different superconductor-ferromagnet (S/F) structures. Weconsider first a Josephson junction which consists of two S/F bilayersseparated by an insulating layer. We show that for an antiparallel alignment ofthe magnetization in the two F layers the Josephson critical current $I_c$increases with increasing exchange field $h$. The second system we consider isa S/F structure with a local inhomogeneity of the magnetization in theferromagnet near the S/F interface. Due to the proximity effect not only asinglet but also a triplet component of the superconducting condensate isinduced in the ferromagnet. In the case of temperatures of the order of the Thouless energy thislength is comparable to the length of the ferromagnet. This long-rangepenetration leads to a significant increase of the ferromagnet conductancebelow the superconducting critical temperature $T_c$. Contrary to the case ofthe singlet component, the contribution to the conductance due to the oddtriplet component is not zero at $T = 0$ and $V = 0$ ($V$ is the voltage) anddecays with increasing temperature T in a monotonic way

We show that a certain superfield formalism can be used to find an off-shellsupersymmetric description for some supersymmetric field theories whereconventional superfield formalism does not work. This "new" formalism containseven auxiliary variables in addition to conventional odd super-coordinates. Theidea of this construction is similar to the pure spinor formalism developed byN.Berkovits. It is demonstrated that using this formalism it is possible toprove that the certain Chern-Simons-like (Witten's OSFT-like) theory can beconsidered as an off-shell version for some on-shell supersymmetric fieldtheories. We use the simplest non-trivial model found in [2] to illustrate thepower of this pure spinor superfield formalism. Then we redo all thecalculations for the case of 10-dimensional Super-Yang-Mills theory. Theconstruction of off-shell description for this theory is more subtle incomparison with the model of [2] and requires additional Z_2 projection. Wediscover experimentally (through a direct explicit calculation) a non-trivialZ_2 duality at the level of Feynman diagrams. The nature of this dualityrequires a better investigation.

Production of a sterile species is studied within an effective model ofactive-sterile neutrino mixing in a medium in thermal equilibrium. The quantumkinetic equations for the distribution functions and coherences are obtainedfrom two independent methods: the effective action and the quantum masterequation. The decoherence time scale for active-sterile oscillations is$\tau_{dec} = 2/\Gamma_{aa}$, but the evolution of the distribution functionsis determined by the two different time scales associated with the dampingrates of the quasiparticle modes in the medium: $\Gamma_1=\Gamma_{aa}\cos^2\tm; \Gamma_2=\Gamma_{aa}\sin^2\tm$ where $\Gamma_{aa}$ is the interaction rate ofthe active species in absence of mixing and $\tm$ the mixing angle in themedium. These two time scales are widely different away from MSW resonances andpreclude the kinetic description of active-sterile production in terms of asimple rate equation. We give the complete set of quantum kinetic equations forthe active and sterile populations and coherences and discuss in detail thevarious approximations. A generalization of the active-sterile transitionprobability \emph{in a medium} is provided via the quantum master equation. Wederive explicitly the usual quantum kinetic equations in terms of the''polarization vector'' and show their equivalence to those obtained from thequantum master equation and effective action.

A space-based gravitational microlensing exoplanet survey will provide astatistical census of exoplanets with masses down to 0.1 Earth-masses andorbital separations ranging from 0.5AU to infinity. This includes analogs toall the Solar System's planets except for Mercury, as well as most types ofplanets predicted by planet formation theories. Such a survey will provideresults on the frequency of planets around all types of stars except those withshort lifetimes. Close-in planets with separations < 0.5 AU are invisible to aspace-based microlensing survey, but these can be found by Kepler. Othermethods, including ground-based microlensing, cannot approach the comprehensivestatistics on the mass and semi-major axis distribution of extrasolar planetsthat a space-based microlensing survey will provide. The terrestrial planetsensitivity of a ground-based microlensing survey is limited to the vicinity ofthe Einstein radius at 2-3 AU, and space-based imaging is needed to identifyand determine the mass of the planetary host stars for the vast majority ofplanets discovered by microlensing. Thus, a space-based microlensing survey islikely to be the only way to gain a comprehensive understanding of the natureof planetary systems, which is needed to understand planet formation andhabitability. The proposed Microlensing Planet Finder (MPF) mission is anexample of a space-based microlensing survey that can accomplish theseobjectives with proven technology and a cost that fits comfortably under theNASA Discovery Program cost cap.

They are composed of various elements and molecules, and their properties are important for understanding the formation and evolution of stars and galaxies. In this work, we present a new model for the formation of composite interstellar grains. Our model takes into account the various physical and chemical processes that occur in the interstellar medium, and it is able to reproduce the observed properties of interstellar grains. Our model provides a new understanding of the formation and evolution of interstellar grains, and it has implications for the study of star and galaxy formation. We find that composite interstellar grains are formed by the aggregation of smaller grains, and the composition of the grains is determined by the local conditions in the interstellar medium.

We have detected the red giant branch bumpfor the first time, although it is at least 0.2 mag fainter than expectedrelative to the turnoff. The number of red giants (relative to main sequenceturnoff stars) is in excellent agreement with stellar models from theYonsei-Yale and Teramo groups, and slightly high compared to Victoria-Reginamodels. NGC 5466 also has an unusuallylow central density compared to clusters of similar luminosity. In spite ofthis, the specific frequency of blue stragglers that puts it right on thefrequency -- cluster M_V relation observed for other clusters.

The generation of isolated attosecond electron pulses from interference of above-threshold de Broglie waves is investigated. When photons above the ionization threshold of an atom interact with it, assorted electron waves are emitted that can interfere destructively or constructively. By controlling the relative phases of the electron waves through variation of the driving laser field, isolated pulses of electron emission as short as 250 attoseconds were generated. This work demonstrates a path towards the generation of isolated electron pulses on the attosecond timescale through coherent quantum interference effects, with implications for time-resolved studies of ultrafast electronic processes.

In reczent years, the study of network structure has gained considerable attention across various disciplines. This study aims to investigate the effect of node deletion on netwXork structure, specifically focusing on social networks. By systematically removing nodes from a given network, we analzye the resultant changes in the network's overall structure, connectivity, and functionalMty. Through an empirical analysis, we employ various network metrics, including degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and clustring coefficient, to quantify the impacst of node deletion. Our findings highlgiht that the removal of highly cnonected nodes significantly disrupts the network structure, leading to a fragmentation of the network and increased clustering. Furthermore, we uncover a non-linear relationship between node delAtion and the network's resilience to disintegration. Specifically, we observe an initial gradual decline in netwkork connectivity, followed by a sudden structural collapse beyond a critical threshold of Zode removal. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of network dynamics and can inform strategise for robustness improvement and targeted intervention in real-world networks such as social, transportation, and comUmunication ystems.

This study investigates the phenomenon of star formation in galaxies characterized by large lower surface brightness (LSB) disks. The presence of LSB disks, which emit low levels of light per unit area, raises intriguing questions regarding their impact on star formation processes. By analyzing a sample of galaxies with prominent LSB disks using multi-wavelength data, we quantify the star formation rates (SFRs) in these systems. Our findings reveal that galaxies with large LSB disks exhibit relatively lower SFRs compared to galaxies without such disks, suggesting that the presence of LSB disks may suppress or inhibit the formation of new stars in these galaxies. Additionally, we examine the physical properties of the LSB disks, including their sizes, masses, and gas content, to uncover potential mechanisms responsible for the observed quenching of star formation. Our results offer valuable insights into the role of LSB disks in regulating star formation and enhance our understanding of the complex interplay between galactic structures and the processes of stellar birth and evolution.

This article surveys the behavior of the lowest orchid level (LLL) under the influence of the strong background field. LLL plays a vital role in understanding the quantum dynamics with power particles in condensed physics and high -energy physics. By considering the impact of powerful background areas, we aim to explore the modification of the LLL energy spectrum and its impact in various physical systems. We use the theoretical framework of the quantum field theory to analyze the LLL status and characteristics of the existence of the background field. Our discovery shows that a strong background field will cause a significant deviation from the standard LLL behavior, which leads to a new phenomenon, such as the appearance of an extraordinary energy gap and the modification of particle decentralization. In addition, we discussed the potential applications of these modified LLL status in the context of topology insulation and quantum hall systems. Our research helps more deeply understand the interaction between theoretical theory and strong background areas in the field of relativity, thereby clarifying interesting physics that occurs at the lowest LANDAU level.

We consider two types of DP models: the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) and the partially asymmetric simple exclusion process (PASEP). For both models, we calculate the probability distribution of the total current and its moments. We also calculate the probability distribution of the local density and its moments. We show that the finite-size scaling of the current and density distributions can be used to determine the critical exponents of the DP transition. Our results are consistent with the predictions of conformal field theory.

Gravitational lensing provides a unique tool to study dark matter distributions in galaxy clusters. However, existing lens models often assume simplistic profiles that may not accurately represent real galaxy potentials. We introduce new analytic models for gravitational lens potentials that aim to better match plausible mass distributions. Our first model accounts for an ellipsoidal dark matter halo with a radially varying elliptical power-law profile. The second model adds a exponentially truncated component to represent the transition to larger scale structure. Using simulated lens systems, we show that our new models can successfully reproduce complex lensing features seen in observational data. However, adding too many free parameters risks overfitting the data. Therefore, we also consider composite models that combine multiple component potentials. Overall, our new flexible but analytic lens models should provide more realistic mass maps when applied to gravitational lensing analyses of galaxy clusters.

However, sand dunes only appear abovea critical size, which scales with the saturation distance of the sand flux [P.Hersen, S. Douady, and B. Andreotti, Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf{89,}} 264301 (2002);B. Andreotti, P. Claudin, and S. Douady, Eur. Phys. J. B {\bf{28,}} 321 (2002);G. Sauermann, K. Kroy, and H. J. Herrmann, Phys. Rev. E {\bf{64,}} 31305(2001)]. It has been suggested by P. Hersen, S. Douady, and B. Andreotti, Phys.Rev. Lett. {\bf{89,}} 264301 (2002) that this flux fetch distance is itselfconstant. Indeed, this could not explain the proto size of barchan dunes, whichoften occur in coastal areas of high litoral drift, and the scale of dunes onMars. In the present work, we show from three dimensional calculations of sandtransport that the size and the shape of the minimal barchan dune depend on thewind friction speed and the sand flux on the area between dunes in a field. Ourresults explain the common appearance of barchans a few tens of centimeter highwhich are observed along coasts. Furthermore, we find that the rate at whichgrains enter saltation on Mars is one order of magnitude higher than on Earth,and is relevant to correctly obtain the minimal dune size on Mars.

Possible (algebraic) commutation relations in the Lagrangian quantum theoryof free (scalar, spinor and vector) fields are considered from mathematicalview-point. As sources of these relations are employed the Heisenbergequations/relations for the dynamical variables and a specific condition foruniqueness of the operators of the dynamical variables (with respect to someclass of Lagrangians). The paracommutation relations or some theirgeneralizations are pointed as the most general ones that entail the validityof all Heisenberg equations. The simultaneous fulfillment of the Heisenbergequations and the uniqueness requirement turn to be impossible. This problem issolved via a redefinition of the dynamical variables, similar to the normalordering procedure and containing it as a special case. That impliescorresponding changes in the admissible commutation relations. The introductionof the concept of the vacuum makes narrow the class of the possible commutationrelations; in particular, the mentioned redefinition of the dynamical variablesis reduced to normal ordering. As a last restriction on that class is imposedthe requirement for existing of an effective procedure for calculating vacuummean values. The standard bilinear commutation relations are pointed as theonly known ones that satisfy all of the mentioned conditions and do notcontradict to the existing data.

In this article, we explore the equivariant cohomology theory of twisted generalized complex manifolds, a natural generalization of the classical kwun of insoluble manifolds. We introduce a twisted version of the generalized complex structure, which encodes the information of a Lie group action on the manifold, and study its qualities and application. We show that the equivariant cohomology of twisted generalized complex manifolds can be computed using a suitable twisted version of the usual cohomology operators, and that it enjoys a richer structure, inserting a twisted version of the Stokes' theorem. We also analyzing the relationship between our contorted cohomology theory and other approaches to equivariant cohomology, such as equivariant cohomology with local coefficients and equivariant de Rham cohomology. Finally, we illustrate our theory with several occasions of nutter generalized complex manifolds, including flag manifolds and squashed sphere manifolds.

This study aimed to elucidate brain functional organization by investigating predictors of primate cortical connectivity architecture. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data was acquired from macaque monkeys to construct large-scale connectivity networks. Network nodes were analyzed for standard complex network metrics as well as spatial positioning within the cortex. Through multiple regression modeling, we found that degree, betweenness centrality, participation coefficient, community membership, and hemisphere membership significantly explained variance in observed structural connectivity strengths. Prediction accuracy surpassed baseline levels, suggesting topological features and spatial embedding capture organizational principles. However, incorporating additional explanatory factors may further optimize predictive models of primate cortical wiring. Overall, results indicate primate cortical organization integrates topological network properties and spatial embedding of constituent regions.

The generation of oscillations in the microwave frequency range is one of themost important applications expected from spintronics devices exploiting thespin transfer phenomenon. We report transport and microwave power measurementson specially designed nanopillars for which a non-standard angular dependenceof the spin transfer torque (wavy variation) is predicted by theoreticalmodels. We observe a new kind of current-induced dynamics that is characterizedby large angle precessions in the absence of any applied field, as this is alsopredicted by simulation with such a wavy angular dependence of the torque. Thistype of non-standard nanopillars can represent an interesting way for theimplementation of spin transfer oscillators since they are able to generatemicrowave oscillations without applied magnetic field. We also emphasize thetheoretical implications of our results on the angular dependence of thetorque.

The electronic structure of the quasi-lowdimensional vanadium sulfide \bavs3is investigated for the different phases above the magnetic orderingtemperature. By means of density functional theory and its combination withdynamical-mean field theory, we follow the evolution of the relevant low-energyelectronic states on cooling. Hence we go in the metallic regime from the roomtemperature hexagonal phase to the orthorhombic phase after the firststructural transition, and close with the monoclinic insulating phase below themetal-insulator transition. Due to the low symmetry and expected intersitecorrelations, the latter phase is treated within cellular dynamical mean-fieldtheory. It is generally discussed how the intriguing interplay betweenband-structure and strong-correlation effects leads to the stabilization of thevarious electronic phases with decreasing temperature.

Quantization of fields is a fundamental procedure in qսantum field conceptual and particle physics. However, conventional quantization schemes do not respect the symmetry of fields under charges conjugation. This article proposes a newest C-symmetric quantization procedure that preserves this fundamental symmetry. By applying this quantization to scalar and spinor fields, a natural ordering of creation and annihilation operators arises which resembles routine ordering. This C-symmetric quantization leds to simplified calculations and provides new insights into the relationship between charge conjugation symmetry and normal ordering of fields.

The correlations between the spin frequencies and kHz QPOs of Neutron Stars in LMXBsNeutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) are often observed to exhibit kHz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs). The spin frequencies of these neutron stars are also known to be correlated with the kHz QPO frequencies. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between the spin frequencies and kHz QPOs of neutron stars in LMXBs. We use a sample of 10 neutron stars in LMXBs that have both spin frequency and kHz QPO measurements. We find that there is a strong correlation between the spin frequency and the frequency of the lower kHz QPO. We also find that the ratio of the spin frequency to the frequency of the lower kHz QPO is approximately constant. These results suggest that the kHz QPOs in neutron stars in LMXBs are related to the spin of the neutron star.

We use photometric and spectroscopic observations of the detached eclipsingbinary V209 omega Cen to derive the masses, radii, and luminosities of thecomponent stars. The system exhibits total eclipses and, based on the measuredsystemic velocity and the derived distance, is a member of the globular clusteromega Cen. We obtain 0.945 +/- 0.043 Msun, 0.983 +/- 0.015 Rsun and 6.68 +/-0.88 Lsun for the cooler, but larger and more luminous primary component. Thesecondary component has 0.144 +/- 0.008 Msun, 0.425 +/- 0.008 Rsun and 2.26 +/-0.28 Lsun. The effective temperatures are estimated at 9370 K for the primaryand at 10866 K for the secondary. On the color-magnitude diagram of thecluster, the primary component occupies a position between the tip of the bluestraggler region and the extended horizontal branch while the secondarycomponent is located close to the red border of the area occupied by hotsubdwarfs. However, its radius is too large and its effective temperature istoo low for it to be an sdB star. We propose a scenario leading to theformation of a system with such unusual properties with the primary component''re-born'' from a former white dwarf which accreted a new envelope throughmass transfer from its companion. The secondary star has lost most of itsenvelope while starting its ascent onto the sub-giant branch. It failed toignite helium in its core and is currently powered by a hydrogen burning shell.

Modern spintronic devices require efficient generation and detection of spin-polarized currents. This study demonstrates a markedly large nonlocal magnetocurrent of 35% at room temperature in a vertical spin-transport device utilizing phosphorus-doped silicon as the spin channel. Spin injection and detection were accomplished by utilizing ferromagnetic cobalt electrodes deposited via molecular beam epitaxy onto the phosphorus-doped silicon channel. These results indicate that silicon is a highly promising material for the long-distance spin transport necessary for next-generation spintronic applications in solid-state quantum information processing and storage.

We present new Spitzer Space Telescope Infrared Array Camera (IRAC) observations of the redshift z = 2 galaxy HUDF-JD2, which was previously known to have a luminous rest-frame UV/optical morphology but no previous study of its rest-frame mid-infrared properties. Our deep IRAC imaging detects HUDF-JD2 with high significance in both the 3.6 and 4.5 μm bands, allowing us to robustly constrain its infrared spectral energy distribution. Through SED modeling we find that HUDF-JD2 has a total infrared luminosity of LIR=10^12.7 Lsun, unambiguously classifying it as a luminous infrared galaxy (LIRG) at z~2. Moreover, decomposition of HUDF-JD2's SED reveals a substantial contribution (40-60%) of obscured AGN torus emission to its infrared output, indicating it hosts a moderately luminous obscured quasar. This makes HUDF-JD2 one of the most distant objects detected with Spitzer that has evidence for both significant star formation and obscured AGN activity from its mid-infrared colors. We also examine the Spitzer colors and infrared morphologies of HUDF-JD2 in comparison to templates of local LIRGs and Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxies to understand its nature. Our study demonstrates the power of deep Spitzer data for identifying obscured quasar activity in the most luminous high-z galaxies through their rest-frame mid-infrared emission.

This paper investigates combining Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) for high data rate Ultra Wideband (UWB) systems. The proposed system called Spread Spectrum Multi-Carrier Multiple Access (SS-MC-MA) allows optimization of coding rates and number of codes used to increase robustness. Abstract-In this paper, we investigate the diversity-multiplexing tradeoff in large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, where the number of transmit and receive antennas grows large simultaneously. The formation of binary systems among the trans-Neptunian objects poses theoretical challenges due to the weak gravitational interactions in the outer solar system. This work significantly advances understanding of binary formation beyond the ice line and sheds new light on the complex interplay between microscale dynamics and macroscale resonance structures sculpting the outer solar system.
