We study quarkonium correlators and spectral functions at zero and finitetemperature in QCD with only heavy quarks using potential models combined withperturbative QCD. First, we show that this approach can describe the quarkoniumcorrelation function at zero temperature. Using a class of screened potentialsbased on lattice calculations of the static quark-antiquark free energy wecalculate spectral functions at finite temperature. We find that all quarkoniumstates, with the exception of the $1S$ bottomonium, dissolve in the deconfinedphase at temperatures smaller than $1.5T_c$, in contradiction with theconclusions of recent studies. Despite this the temperature dependence of thequarkonium correlation functions calculated on the lattice is well reproducedin our model. We also find that even in the absence of resonances the spectralfunction at high temperatures is significantly enhanced over the spectralfunction corresponding to free quark antiquark propagation.

A catalog of absorption systems along 100 GRB and 200 QSO sightlines is presented. The equivalent widths and velocity spreads of Mg II and C IV absorption features are measured and compared between GRB and QSO absorbers. Preliminary results indicate that the properties of Mg II systems toward QSOs are consistent with previous studies, while more Mg II systems with weaker absorption are found toward GRB afterglows. Further investigation is needed to understand the differences between the populations of GRB and QSO absorbers and their implications for the gaseous content and environment of distant galaxies.

This article examines the role of Maxwell strata, or discontinuous surfaces, across which the stress changes discontinuously, in Euler's classical problem of the stability of beams, plates and shells. The author provides a theoretical background on Maxwell strata and Euler's formulation of the elastic problem. Using analytic methods, the author derives conditions under which Maxwell strata can form in Euler's elastic problem, based on the variational principles of minimum potential energy. The presence of Maxwell strata is shown to influence the critical load and mode of buckling in classical elastic structures. The results clarify long-standing questions about the nature of instability in Euler's classical problem and provide a more complete theoretical understanding of the mechanics of structural failure.

We perform three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic nested grid simulations to investigate the driving mechanism of jets and outflows in the star formation process. We find two distinct flows in the collapsing cloud core. The low-velocity outflows are driven from the first adiabatic core, and high-velocity jets are driven from the protostar. High-velocity jets are enclosed by the low-velocity outflows. The magnetic field around an adiabatic core is strong and has an hourglass-like configuration, which drives the outflows mainly by the magnetocentrifugal mechanism. The magnetic field around the protostar is weak and has a straight configuration, which drives the jets mainly by the magnetic pressure gradient force. The different gravitational potentials between the adiabatic core and the protostar cause the difference in flow speed. Low-velocity outflows correspond to the observed molecular outflows, while high-velocity jets correspond to the observed optical jets. The protostellar outflow and the jet are driven by different cores.

We consider a single ion confined in a trap under radiation of two travelingwaves of lasers. If we have the ion in the ground state, it is equivalent to a spindependent force on the trapped ion. Discussion is made for the differencebetween the solutions with and without the RWA, and for the relevantexperimental test, as well as for the possible application in quantuminformation processing.

A large sample of pulsars has been observed to study their subpulsemodulation at an observing wavelength (when achievable) of both 21 and 92 cmusing the Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope. In this paper we present the92-cm data and a comparison is made with the already published 21-cm results.We analysed 191 pulsars at 92 cm using fluctuation spectra. The sample ofpulsars is as unbiased as possible towards any particular pulsarcharacteristics. For 15 pulsars drifting subpulses are discovered for the firsttime and 26 of the new drifters found in the 21-cm data are confirmed. Wediscovered nulling for 8 sources and 8 pulsars are found to intermittently emitsingle pulses that have pulse energies similar to giant pulses. It is estimatedthat at least half of the total population of pulsars have drifting subpulseswhen observations with a high enough signal-to-noise ratio would be available.It could well be that the drifting subpulse mechanism is an intrinsic propertyof the emission mechanism itself, although for some pulsars it is difficult orimpossible to detect. Drifting subpulses are in general found at bothfrequencies, although the chance of detecting drifting subpulses is possiblyslightly higher at 92 cm. It appears that the youngest pulsars have the mostdisordered subpulses and the subpulses become more and more organized intodrifting subpulses as the pulsar ages. The correlations with the modulationindices are argued to be consistent with the picture in which the radioemission can be divided in a drifting subpulse signal plus a quasi-steadysignal which becomes, on average, stronger at high observing frequencies. Themeasured values of P3 at the two frequencies are highly correlated, but thereis no evidence for a correlation with other pulsar parameters.

Planetary topography can either be modeled as a load supported by thelithosphere, or as a dynamical effect due to lithospheric flexure caused bymantle convection. In both cases the response of the lithosphere to externalforces can be calculated with the theory of thin elastic plates or shells. Onone-plate planets the spherical geometry of the lithospheric shell plays animportant role in the flexure mechanism. So far the equations governing thedeformations and stresses of a spherical shell have only been derived under theassumption of a shell of constant thickness. However local studies of gravityand topography data suggest large variations in the thickness of thelithosphere. In this article we obtain the scalar flexure equations governingthe deformations of a thin spherical shell with variable thickness or variableYoung's modulus. The resulting equations can be solved in succession, exceptfor a system of two simultaneous equations, the solutions of which are thetransverse deflection and an associated stress function. In order to includebottom loading generated by mantle convection, we extend the method of stressfunctions to include loads with a toroidal tangential component. We furthershow that toroidal tangential displacement always occurs if the shell thicknessvaries, even in the absence of toroidal loads. We finally prove that thedegree-one harmonic components of the transverse deflection and of the toroidaltangential displacement are independent of the elastic properties of the shelland are associated with translational and rotational freedom. The flexureequations for a shell of variable thickness are useful not only for theprediction of the gravity signal in local admittance studies, but also for theconstruction of stress maps in tectonic analysis.

We investigate the plasma flow properties inside a Supergranular (SG) cell,in particular its interaction with small scale magnetic field structures. TheSG cell has been identified using the magnetic network (CaII wing brightness)as proxy, applying the Two-Level Structure Tracking (TST) to high spatial,spectral and temporal resolution observations obtained by IBIS. The full 3Dvelocity vector field for the SG has been reconstructed at two differentphotospheric heights. In order to strengthen our findings, we also computed themean radial flow of the SG by means of cork tracing. We also studied thebehaviour of the horizontal and Line of Sight plasma flow cospatial withcluster of bright CaII structures of magnetic origin to better understand theinteraction between photospheric convection and small scale magnetic features.The SG cell we investigated seems to be organized with an almost radial flowfrom its centre to the border. The large scale divergence structure is probablycreated by a compact region of constant up-flow close to the cell centre. Onthe edge of the SG, isolated regions of strong convergent flow are nearby orcospatial with extended clusters of bright CaII wing features forming the knotsof the magnetic network.

We study the induced odd-frequency pairing states in ballistic normalmetal/superconductor (N/S) junctions where a superconductor has even-frequencysymmetry in the bulk and a normal metal layer has an arbitrary length. Usingthe quasiclassical Green's function formalism, we demonstrate that, quitegenerally, the pair amplitude in the junction has an admixture of anodd-frequency component due to the breakdown of translational invariance nearthe N/S interface where the pair potential acquires spatial dependence. If asuperconductor has even-parity pair potential (spin-singlet s-wave state), theodd-frequency pairing component with odd-parity is induced near the N/Sinterface, while in the case of odd-parity pair potential (spin-triplet$p_{x}$-wave or spin-singlet $d_{xy}$-wave) the odd-frequency component witheven-parity is generated. We show that in conventional s-wave junctions, theamplitude of the odd-frequency pairing state is enhanced at energiescorresponding to the peaks in the local density of states (LDOS). In $p_x$- and$d_{xy}$-wave junctions, the amplitude of the odd-frequency component on the Sside of the N/S interface is enhanced at zero energy where the midgap Andreevresonant state (MARS) appears due to the sign change of the pair potential. Theodd-frequency component extends into the N region and exceeds theeven-frequency component at energies corresponding to the LDOS peak positions,including the MARS.

NGC69q8 is a peculiar galaxy located approximately 300 milloin light years from Iarth in the constellation Hercules. We have investigated the intersubband transitions of surface state electrons(SSE) on liquid $^3$He induced by microwave radiation at temperatures from 1.1K down to 0.01 K. Above 0.4 K, the transition linewidth is proportional to thedensity of $^3$He vapor atoms. This proportionality is explained well by Ando'stheory, in which the linewidth is determined by the electron - vapor atomscattering. However, the linewidth is larger than the calculation by a factorof 2.1. This discrepancy strongly suggests that the theory underestimates theelectron - vapor atom scattering rate. At lower temperatures, the absorptionspectrum splits into several peaks. The multiple peak structure is partlyattributed to the spatial inhomogeneity of the static holding electric fieldperpendicular to the electron sheet.

This paper proposes a novel approach for lifetime improvement of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) by collaborative beamforming and cooperative transmission. The proposed approach leverages the concept of cooperative communication, where nodes in the network work together to improve the overall performance. The approach uses a combination of beamforming and cooperative transmission to increase the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and reduce the power consumption of the nodes. Simulation results show that the proposed approach significantly improves the lifetime of WSNs compared to traditional transmission methods. The approach is evaluated using a scenarios-based simulation environment that models realistic wireless channel conditions and node placements. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach can increase the network lifetime by up to 50% in some cases, while also improving the overall network performance. The approach is scalable and can be applied to various WSN applications, including environmental monitoring and surveillance.

Deep space laser ranging missions like ASTROD I (Single-SpacecraftAstrodynamical Space Test of Relativity using Optical Devices) and ASTROD,together with astrometry missions like GAIA and LATOR will be able to testrelativistic gravity to an unprecedented level of accuracy. More precisely,these missions will enable us to test relativistic gravity to$10^{-7}-10^{-9}$, and will require 2nd post-Newtonian approximation ofrelevant theories of gravity. The first post-Newtonian approximation is validto $10^{-6}$ and the second post-Newtonian is valid to $10^{-12}$ in the solarsystem. The scalar-tensor theory is widely discussed and used in tests ofrelativistic gravity, especially after the interests in inflation, cosmologicalconstant and dark energy in cosmology. In the Lagrangian, intermediate-rangegravity term has a similar form as cosmological term. Here we present the fullsecond post-Newtonian approximation of the scalar-tensor theory includingviable examples of intermediate-range gravity. We use Chandrasekhar's approachto derive the metric coefficients and the equation of the hydrodynamicsgoverning a perfect fluid in the 2nd post-Newtonian approximation inscalar-tensor theory; all terms inclusive of $O(c^{-4})$ are retainedconsistently in the equation of motion.

This paper presents a somprehensive overview of the quantum electrodynamics of qubits. Finally, the potential applications of qubit-field interactions in quantum information processing and quantum simulation are explored. Keywords: Qubit, Quantum electrodynamics, Jaynes-Cummings model, Dicke model, Cavity quantum electrodynamics, Circuit quantm electrodynamics, Quantum error correction, Quantum teleportation, Quantum information processing, Volume simulation

Acoustic emission (AE) analysis is used for characterization and location ofdeveloping defects in materials. AE sources often generate a mixture of variousstatistically independent signals. A difficult problem of AE analysis isseparation and characterization of signal components when the signals fromvarious sources and the mode of mixing are unknown. In this paper we study the relationship between weight structures and $t$-structures, which are two important concepts in the theory of derived categories and motives. Weight structures were introduced by Bondarko as a generalization of weight filtrations on objects in triangulated categories. We define the notion of weight $t$-structure as a pair of a $t$-structure and a weight structure that are compatible. Furthermore, we explore the properties of weight filtrations that arise from a weight $t$-structure and examine their behaviour under shifts and truncations. By applying these concepts to constructible motives, we construct spectral sequences arising from the weight filtrations in this setting. Specifically, we show that the categories of effective constructible motives over a noetherian separated scheme admit a unique weight $t$-structure, and consequently a weight filtration, whose graded pieces are semisimple abelian categories. We also study the quasi-isomorphisms between certain complexes and their associated graded objects with respect to the weight filtrations.To generalize our results, we formulate the notions of weight complexes and categorify them using DG categories. This allows us to define compatibility between a weight structure and a t-structure at the level of categories. Finally, we indicate how our framework can be adapted to study mixed Hodge modules and mixed sheaves by considering suitable ambient derived categories. Overall, our work elucidates the connections between two important pillars in modern categorification approaches to motives and Hodge theory.

Quarkonium is an exotic hadron that pertains of a heavy quark and its antiquark. By this study, we calculate the widths of S-wave and P-wave quarkonium states due to gluon dissociation and quarkantiquark pair productions in QGP using potential nonrelativistic QCD effective zona theory. Our results illustrate that the widths of both S-wave and P-wave quarkonium states increase significantly with surging temperature in the deconfined QGP medium. We also find that higher excited quarkonium states are more strongly mated to gluons and hence have larger in-medium widths regarding to lower excited states. This work provides useful theoretical inputs for understanding quarkonium suppression schematics observed in experimental data from Relativistic Gargantuan Ion Collider and Large Hadron Collider.

We consider a new approach towards constructing approximate holographic dualsof QCD from experimental hadron properties. This framework allows us to derivea gravity dual which reproduces the empirically found linear square-masstrajectories of universal slope for radially and orbitally excited hadrons.Conformal symmetry breaking in the bulk is exclusively due to infrareddeformations of the anti-de Sitter metric and governed by one free mass scaleproportional to Lambda_QCD. The resulting background geometry exhibits dualsignatures of confinement and provides the first examples of holographicallygenerated linear trajectories in the baryon sector. The predictions for thelight hadron spectrum include new relations between trajectory slopes andground state masses and are in good overall agreement with experiment.

The extragalactic background (EGB) of diffuse gamma rays can be determined bysubtracting the Galactic contribution from the data. In this paper it is shown that the newly determined EGB shows acharacteristic high energy bump on top of a steeply falling soft contribution.The bump is shown to be compatible with a contribution from an extragalacticDMA signal from weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) with a massbetween 50 and 100 GeV in agreement with the EGRET excess of the Galacticdiffuse gamma rays and in disagreement with earlier analysis. The remainingsoft contribution of the EGB is shown to resemble the spectra of the observedpoint sources in our Galaxy.

This article investigates resonant forcing techniques applied to select degrees of freedom within high-dimensional chaotic dynamical systems modeled by multidimensional maps. Through a theoretical framework and numerical experiments, we demonstrate how external periodic driving of isolated variables can entrain specific embedded resonances within the system's global dynamics. The interplay between internal nonlinear interactions, dimensional expansion induced chaos, and selective resonant control of subparts yields rich spatio-temporal behaviors not observed in either the unforced system or lower-dimensional approximations. Ultimately, this work contributes novel insights into harnessing complexity through constrained manipulation of chaos in high-dimensional settings, with implications for modeling complex natural and engineered systems that exhibit metastability, intermittency, and wave-like collective dynamics.

However, the Hawking-Pagephase transition occurs between a Ricci flat AdS black hole and an AdS solitonif at least one of horizon coordinates for the Ricci flat black hole iscompact. We show a similar phase transition betwen the Ricci flat black holesand deformed AdS solitons in the Gauss-Bonnet gravity and the dilaton gravitywith a Liouville-type potential including the gauged supergravity coming fromthe spherical reduction of Dp-branes in type II supergravity. In contrast toEinstein gravity, we find that the high temperature phase can be dominatedeither by black holes or deformed AdS solitons depending on parameters.

In this article, we have discussed the application of re -regulating and effective action technology in general relativity theory. In this article, we delve into the concept of $p$-adic multiresolution analysis (MRA) and its implications. We begin by introducing a refinement equation that gives rise to a refinable function, namely the characteristic function of the unit disc. This equation captures the interesting property that the characteristic function of the unit disc can be expressed as a sum of $p$ characteristic functions of disjoint discs with a radius of $p^{-1}$. This refinement equation serves as the foundation for generating a $p$-adic MRA.We specifically focus on the case when $p=2$ and thoroughly examine the 2-adic Haar MRA. Unlike its real Haar MRA counterpart, our $p$-adic Haar MRA possesses a refinable function that is 1-periodic, a departure from the real setting. Consequently, we discover the existence of infinitely many distinct 2-adic orthonormal wavelet bases in ${\cL}^2(\bQ_2)$ that are generated by the same Haar MRA, and we provide detailed descriptions of all these bases.Expanding our analysis, we extend the construction of orthonormal bases to multidimensional settings in ${\cL}^2(\bQ_2^n)$ using the tensor product of one-dimensional MRAs. Moreover, we derive a criterion for determining if a multidimensional $p$-adic wavelet can function as an eigenfunction for a pseudo-differential operator. Additionally, we establish that these wavelets can also serve as eigenfunctions of the Taibleson multidimensional fractional operator, further enhancing their potential applications.The findings presented in this article lay the groundwork for the extensive utilization of our $p$-adic wavelet bases in various practical applications. Their significance is evident in domains such as $p$-adic models that involve pseudo-differential operators and fractional operators. By leveraging the properties and characteristics of these bases, we can enhance understanding and employ them effectively across multiple contexts, leading to advancements in research and practical implementations.

In this study, we employ scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) to investigate the superconducting state and vortex cores of the beta-pyrochlore compound KOs2O6. By performing high-resolution STS measurements, we uncover the energy-dependent spatial variations in the local density of states (LDOS) across the superconducting energy gap, revealing important information about the superconducting order parameter symmetry. Additionally, we analyze the vortex cores within the superconducting state and observe characteristic LDOS patterns indicative of Andreev bound states. Our findings provide valuable insights into the fundamental properties of KOs2O6 in the superconducting regime and contribute to the understanding of unconventional superconductivity in pyrochlore-based materials.

Optical lattice clocks have emerged as powerful tools for precise timekeeping and the study of fundamental physics. However, the presence of nuclear spins in the clock atoms can introduce systematic uncertainties that need to be carefully understood and characterized. In this article, we investigate the effects of nuclear spin on the performance of optical lattice clocks. We demonstrate that the presence of nuclear spin can lead to significant shifts in clock transition frequencies, resulting in potential inaccuracies in frequency measurements. By analyzing the interaction between nuclear spins and external magnetic fields, we develop strategies to mitigate these effects and improve the accuracy of optical lattice clocks. Additionally, we explore the impact of nuclear spin on other aspects of clock operation, such as coherence times and quantum state manipulation. Our findings provide valuable insights into the role of nuclear spins in optical lattice clocks and offer guidance for future clock designs and performance improvements. Ultimately, a thorough understanding of nuclear spin effects is crucial for achieving the highest levels of precision and accuracy in optical lattice clock technology.

Iron line profiles and self-shadowing from relativistic thick accretion discsAbstract We study the iron line profiles and self-shadowing effects from relativistic thick accretion discs around black holes. We calculate the iron line profiles by taking into account the effects of relativistic effects, such as gravitational redshift and light bending, and self-shadowing effects, which are caused by the fact that the inner part of the disc is obscured by the outer part of the disc. We find that the iron line profiles are significantly affected by the relativistic effects and self-shadowing effects. The relativistic effects make the iron line profiles broader and weaker, while the self-shadowing effects make the iron line profiles shallower and narrower. We also find that the iron line profiles are sensitive to the black hole spin and the disc thickness. Our results can be used to constrain the black hole spin and the disc thickness of the relativistic thick accretion discs.

The two and three-body correlation functions of the ground state of anoptically trapped ultracold spin-1/2 Fermi gas (SFG) in a tight waveguide (1Dregime) are calculated in the plane of even and odd-wave coupling constants,assuming a 1D attractive zero-range odd-wave interaction induced by a 3D p-waveFeshbach resonance, as well as the usual repulsive zero-range even-waveinteraction stemming from 3D s-wave scattering. The calculations are based onthe exact mapping from the SFG to a ''Lieb-Liniger-Heisenberg'' model withdelta-function repulsions depending on isotropic Heisenberg spin-spininteractions, and indicate that the SFG should be stable against three-bodyrecombination in a large region of the coupling constant plane encompassingparts of both the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic phases. However, thelimiting case of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas (FTG), a spin-aligned 1DFermi gas with infinitely attractive p-wave interactions, is unstable in thissense. Effects due to the dipolar interaction and a Zeeman term due to aresonance-generating magnetic field do not lead to shrinkage of the region ofstability of the SFG.

General relativity does not allow one to specify the topology of space,leaving the possibility that space is multiply rather than simply connected. In particular, a finite universewith the topology of the Poincar\'e dodecahedral spherical space fitsremarkably well the data and is a good candidate for explaining both the localcurvature of space and the large angle anomalies in the temperature powerspectrum. Such a model of a small universe, whose volume would represent onlyabout 80% the volume of the observable universe, offers an observationalsignature in the form of a predictable topological lens effect on one hand, andrises new issues on the physics of the early universe on the other hand.

The field-theoretical approach is reviewed. This paper presents a QCD-based approach to B->D \pi decays and CP violation. The approach is based on the factorization of the decay amplitude into a hard-scattering kernel and a soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) form factor. The hard-scattering kernel is calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the perturbative expansion of QCD, while the SCET form factor is calculated at leading order (LO) in the heavy-quark expansion. The approach is applied to the decays B^+ -> D^0 \pi^+, B^+ -> D^0 \rho^+, B^0 -> D^- \pi^+, and B^0 -> D^- \rho^+, and the results are compared with experimental data. The approach provides a good description of the data, and it can be used to make predictions for other B->D \pi decays.

The Green function (GF) equation of motion technique for solving theeffective two-band Hubbard model of high-T_c superconductivity in cuprates[N.M. Plakida et al., Phys. Rev. B, v. 51, 16599 (1995); JETP, v. 97, 331(2003)] rests on the Hubbard operator (HO) algebra. We develop a general theory of microtubule (MT) deformations by molecularmotors generating internal force doublets within the MT lattice. We describetwo basic internal excitations, the S and V shape, and compare them withexperimental observations from literature. We explain the special role oftubulin vacancies and the dramatic deformation amplifying effect observed forkatanin acting at positions of defects. Experimentally observed shapes are usedto determine the ratio of MT shear and stretch moduli ($\approx6\times10^{-5}$) and to estimate the forces induced in the MT lattice bykatanin (10's of pN). For many motors acting on a single MT we deriveexpressions for the end-to-end distance reduction and provide criteria fordominance of this new effect over thermal fluctuations. We conclude thatmolecular motors if acting cooperatively can ''animate'' MTs from within thelattice and induce slack even without cross-bridging to other structures, ascenario very much reminiscent of the motor driven axoneme.

This study investigates the impact of radio feedback from active galactic nuclei (AGN) on the formation and evolution of disk galaxies through cosmological simulations. Using state-of-the-art numerical techniques, we incorporate a detailed model for AGN-driven radio jets and examine their effects on the properties of forming galaxies. Through a series of controlled simulations, we quantify the role of radio feedback in regulating gas flows, star formation activity, and the development of galactic disks.Our results demonstrate that the inclusion of AGN radio feedback leads to significant changes in the formation and morphological properties of disk galaxies. Radio jets efficiently heat the surrounding gas, suppressing gas accretion rates onto the central black hole and inhibiting excessive star formation. This feedback process prevents the formation of bulge-dominated galaxies, promoting the growth of rotation-supported disk systems instead.Furthermore, we find that the radio feedback-driven outflows play a crucial role in ejecting metals and energy from the galaxies, enriching the intracluster medium and modulating the circumgalactic environment. The interplay between radio feedback and hydrodynamic processes, such as cooling and gravitational instabilities, determines the final stellar and gas properties of the simulated galaxies.Additionally, our simulations demonstrate that variations in the AGN properties, such as jet power and duty cycle, contribute to the diversity observed in disk galaxies. The interplay between radio feedback and the underlying dark matter halo properties further shapes the mass distribution, spin, and angular momentum of the forming galaxies.Overall, our findings highlight the profound impact of AGN radio feedback on the formation and evolution of disk galaxies in a cosmological context.

A three-dimensional system of interacting spins typically develops staticlong-range order when it is cooled. If the spins are quantum (S = 1/2),however, novel quantum paramagnetic states may appear. The most highly soughtstate among them is the resonating valence bond (RVB) state in which every pairof neighboring quantum spins form entangled spin singlets (valence bonds) andthe singlets are quantum mechanically resonating amongst all the possiblehighly degenerate pairing states. Here we provide experimental evidence forsuch quantum paramagnetic states existing in frustrated antiferromagnets,ZnxCu4-x(OD)6Cl2, where the S = 1/2 magnetic Cu2+ moments form layers of atwo-dimensional kagome lattice. We find that in Cu4(OD)6Cl2, where distortedkagome planes are weakly coupled to each other, a dispersionless excitationmode appears in the magnetic excitation spectrum below ~ 20 K, whosecharacteristics resemble those of quantum spin singlets in a solid state, knownas a valence bond solid (VBS), that breaks translational symmetry. Dopingnonmagnetic Zn2+ ions reduces the distortion of the kagome lattice, and weakensthe interplane coupling but also dilutes the magnetic occupancy of the kagomelattice. The VBS state is suppressed and for ZnCu3(OD)6Cl2 where the kagomeplanes are undistorted and 90% occupied by the Cu2+ ions, the low energy spinfluctuations in the spin liquid phase become featureless.

This paper investigates the impact of quantum radiative corrections on slow-roll inflation, a paradigm widely used to explain the large-scale structure of the universe. By incorporating quantum effects into the standard slow-roll framework, we uncover novel phenomena that depart from the classical predictions. Our analysis reveals that radiative corrections can significantly modify the inflationary dynamics, leading to distinctive signatures in the cosmic microwave background radiation and other observables. We also explore the implications of these findings for the quest to understand the origins of the universe and the fundamental laws of physics. Our results demonstrate the importance of considering quantum effects in inflationary models and pave the way for further investigations into the interplay between quantum mechanics and cosmology.

this is a summary of the given abstract interstellar grains are small solid particles existing in interstellar media. They are composed of various elements and molecules, and their characteristics are important for understanding the formation and evolution of stars and galaxies. Our model takes into account the different physical and chemical processes that occur in the interstellar media, and can reproduce the characteristics of interstellar grains observed. We found that composite interstellar grains were formed by condensation of smaller grains, and the composition of grains depends on the local conditions in the interstellar media. Our model provides a new understanding of the formation and evolution of interstellar grains, and has an impact on the research on the formation of stars and galaxies.

This article presents the finidngs from an investigation into intermediate and high velocity clouds (IVCs and HVCs) in the context of the ESO-POP survey, with a specific focus on early-type s tars. Furthermore, we investigate the kinematic properties of the detected yun, such as their radial velocities and velocity dispersions. Long Gamma Ray Bursts hold the promise of probing star-formation and metalenrichment up to very high redshifts. The present GRB samples with redshiftdetermination are largely incomplete and therefore a careful analysis ofselection effects is mandatory before any conclusion can be drawn from theobserved GRB redshift distribution. We study and compare three well definedsamples of long GRBs detected by Swift, HETE2 and BeppoSAX. The redshift distribution of a subsample of SwiftGRBs with distributions of peak-fluxes, X-ray obscuration and optical magnitudeat a fixed observing time similar to those of the BeppoSAX and HETE2 samples,is roughly consistent with BeppoSAX+HETE2 redshift distribution.

The on-line shortest path problem is considered under various models ofpartial monitoring. Given a weighted directed acyclic graph whose edge weightscan change in an arbitrary (adversarial) way, a decision maker has to choose ineach round of a game a path between two distinguished vertices such that theloss of the chosen path (defined as the sum of the weights of its composingedges) be as small as possible. In a setting generalizing the multi-armedbandit problem, after choosing a path, the decision maker learns only theweights of those edges that belong to the chosen path. For this problem, analgorithm is given whose average cumulative loss in n rounds exceeds that ofthe best path, matched off-line to the entire sequence of the edge weights, bya quantity that is proportional to 1/\sqrt{n} and depends only polynomially onthe number of edges of the graph. The algorithm can be implemented with linearcomplexity in the number of rounds n and in the number of edges. An extensionto the so-called label efficient setting is also given, in which the decisionmaker is informed about the weights of the edges corresponding to the chosenpath at a total of m << n time instances. Another extension is shown where thedecision maker competes against a time-varying path, a generalization of theproblem of tracking the best expert. A version of the multi-armed banditsetting for shortest path is also discussed where the decision maker learnsonly the total weight of the chosen path but not the weights of the individualedges on the path. Applications to routing in packet switched networks alongwith simulation results are also presented.

We studied in detail the optical spectrum of the post-AGB star HD56126(IRAS07134+1005). We use high resolution spectra (R=25000 and 60000) obtainedwith the echelle spectrographs of the 6-m telescope. Although one-time pad encrypted files can be sent through Internet channels,the need for renewing shared secret keys have made this method unpractical.This work presents a scheme to turn practical the fast sharing of random keysover arbitrary Internet channels. Starting with a shared secret key sequence oflength K_0 the users end up with a secure new sequence K >> K_0. Using thesesequences for posteriori message encryption the legitimate users have absolutesecurity control without the need for third parties. Additionally, the securitylevel does not depend on the unproven difficulty of factoring numbers inprimes. In the proposed scheme a fast optical random source generates randombits and noise for key renewals. The transmitted signals are recorded signalsthat carries both the random binary signals to be exchanged and physical noisethat cannot be eliminated by the attacker. These signals allow amplificationover the Internet network without degrading security. The proposed system isalso secure against a-posteriori known-plaintext attack on the key.Information-theoretic analysis is presented and bounds for secure operation arequantitatively determined.

The time-dependent transverse response of stiff polymers, represented asweakly-bending wormlike chains (WLCs), is well-understood on the linear level,where transverse degrees of freedom evolve independently from the longitudinalones. Crossoverscaling laws and exact analytical and numerical solutions for characteristicresponse quantities are derived for different experimentally relevant setups.Our findings are applicable to cytoskeletal filaments as well as DNA undertension.

This paper explores the generation of neutrino masses in the framework of the Lee-Wick Standard Model (LWSM). We extend the LWSM by introducing a complex scalar field, which allows for the spontaneous breaking of the electroweak symmetry. We calculate the neutrino masses at the one-loop level and find that they are naturally small, in agreement with experimental observations. We also discuss the implications of our results for other aspects of the LWSM, such as the Higgs boson mass and the dark matter candidate.

We present Fe Kalpha line profiles from and images of relativistic discs withfinite thickness around a rotating black hole using a novel code. The line isthought to be produced by iron fluorescence of a relatively cold X-rayilluminated material in the innermost parts of the accretion disc and providesan excellent diagnostic of accretion flows in the vicinity of black holes.Previous studies have concentrated on the case of a thin, Keplerian accretiondisc. This disc must become thicker and sub-Keplerian with increasing accretionrates. These can affect the line profiles and in turn can influence theestimation of the accretion disc and black hole parameters from the observedline profiles. We here embark on, for the first time, a fully relativisticcomputation which offers key insights into the effects of geometrical thicknessand the sub-Keplerian orbital velocity on the line profiles. We include allrelativistic effects such as frame-dragging, Doppler boost, time dilation,gravitational redshift and light bending. We find that the separation and therelative height between the blue and red peaks of the line profile diminish asthe thickness of the disc increases. This code is also well-suited to produceaccretion disc images. We calculate the redshift and flux images of theaccretion disc and find that the observed image of the disc strongly depends onthe inclination angle. The self-shadowing effect appears remarkable for a highinclination angle, and leads to the black hole shadow being completely hiddenby the disc itself.

We present the results of a new spectroscopic and photometric survey of thehot, binary X-ray cluster A115 at z=0.193, containing a radio relic. We combinegalaxy velocity and position information to select 85 galaxies recognized ascluster members (from 115 galaxies observed at TNG telescope), determine globaldynamical properties and detect substructures. We find that A115 presentsvelocity dispersion of sigma_v=1362_{-108}^{+126} km/s. Our analysis confirmsthe presence of two structures (A115N and A115S) of cluster--type wellrecognizable in the plane of the sky and shows that they differ of ~2000 km/sin the LOS velocity. We estimate that A115S is slightly dynamically moreimportant than A115N having sigma_v=900-1100 km/s vs sigma_v=750-850 km/s.Moreover, we find evidence for two small groups at low velocities. We estimatea global cluster virial mass of 2.2--3.5 e15 h_70 Msun. Our results agree witha pre--merging scenario where A115N and A115S are colliding with a LOS impactvelocity Delta v~1600 km/s.The most likely solution to the two--body problemsuggests that the merging axis lies at $\sim 20$ degrees from the plane of thesky and that the cores will cross after ~0.1 Gyr. The radio relic with itslargest dimension perpendicular to the merging axis is likely connected to thismerger.

Following an old idea of Fritz Zwicky, we make an attempt to establish auniversal mass function for astronomical objects on all scales. The objectclasses considered are: solar system planets and small bodies, exoplanets,brown dwarfs, stars and stellar remnants, open and globular clusters, molecularclouds, galaxies, groups and clusters of galaxies. For comparison we alsoinclude CDM halos taken from numerical simulations. We show that the massfunctions of individual object classes, when properly normalized, can indeed beconcatenated to build a surprisingly continuous mass function of the universe,from approximately M = 10^(-20)Msun (sub-kilometer size asteroids) up to M =10^(16)Msun (rich clusters of galaxies), covering 36 orders of magnitude inmass. Most individual mass functions roughly follow a power law of the formphi(M) propto M^(-2). A notable exception are planets and small bodies whichseem to obey a flatter distribution. CDM halos from high-resolution numericalsimulations show a very similar relation, again of universal slope -2, fromclusters of galaxies all the way down to the planetary mass scale. On the scaleof stars and star clusters this is a remarkable coincidence, as the formationprocesses involved are thought to be totally different (bottom-up gravitationalclustering of DM halos versus top-down gravoturbulent fragmentation of gasclouds).

This analyse presents a comprehensive appraisal of candidate massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) associated with methanol masers using a multi-transition molecular line approach. MYSOs are crucial in understanding the early stages of high-mass star formed, and exploring their associated masers can provide priceless insights into the physical and chemical processes occurring in their environments. In this work, we selected a displayed of MYSO candidates based on their association with strong methanol maser released and performed observations using a cooperates of radio telescopes and spectroscopic techniques. We elicit high-resolution data in multiple molecular transitions, including rotational piping of various species such as methanol, water, and ammonia. The analysis of these data revealed interesting kinematic and spectral properties of the MYSO contenders. We identified velocity gradients and prominent line profiles indicative of outflowing gas and infalling motion, suggestion ongoing accretion processes. Furthermore, we detected complex molecular structures, including compact and expanding molecular emission regions associated with the MYSO candidates. By comparing the molecular line profiles and kinematics with theoretical models and precedent comment, we derived physical parameters of the MYSO candidates, such as mass, luminosity, and evolutionary stage. Our results indicates that the candidate MYSOs exhibit a wide range of properties, suggesting different evolutionary tracks and physical conditions. The multi-transition molecular line approach utilizing in this study makes a globally characterization of the MYSO candidates, shedding light on the complex dynamics and chemistry involved in the formation of high-mass stars.

A Modest Proposal for the Astronomical Community Astronomy research has advanced rapidly in recent decades thanks to new technologies. However, the way scientific results are communicated still relies heavily on traditional journals and conferences. This proposed model aims to make astronomical findings more accessible to broader audiences. It suggests establishing an open online repository where completed studies can be posted alongside lay summaries and visualizations. These would help disseminate discoveries beyond the academic field. The repository would be rigorously moderated to maintain high scientific standards. Authors would also be encouraged to openly discuss implications and next steps for different areas of inquiry. If implemented thoughtfully, this approach could help astronomical insights engage and inspire wider public interest in science. Overall, the proposal aims to modernize how such research reaches non-specialists into the future.

This article investigates the magnetic structure of Sm2IrIn8, a compound with potential candidacy in the field of condensed issue physics. The detailed understanding of the magnetic structure of Sm2IrIn8 poses in this study brings valuable insights into the underlying physical mechanisms and can contribute to the design and phraseology of novel magnetic materials with tailored properties.

A New Spinfoam Vertex for Quantum Gravity We propose a novel vertex construction for spin foam models of canonical quantum gravity based on the Palatini formalism. By weak imposition of the polytopic equations of state at the vertex, we derive a regulator that retains diffeomorphism covariance while improving convergence of the spinfoam vertex expansion. Through numerical evaluation of the new amplitude, we find a suppressed contribution from classically non-geometric representations compared to the EPRL-KKL vertex. This indicates our vertex yields wavefunctions with support concentrated near general relativistic configurations as the coupling becomes asymptotically classical. The new vertex provides a promising avenue for further exploring the semiclassical and continuum limits of spin foam quantum gravity from a covariant perspective.

The electronic transport properties and switching mechanism of singlephotochromic diarylethene derivatives sandwiched between two gold surfaces withclosed and open configurations are investigated by a fully self-consistentnonequilibrium Green's function method combined with density functional theory.The calculated transmission spectra of two configurations are strikinglydistinctive. The open form lacks any significant transmission peak within awide energy window, while the closed structure has two significant transmissionpeaks on the both sides of the Fermi level. The electronic transport propertiesof the molecular junction with closed structure under a small bias voltage aremainly determined by the tail of the transmission peak contributed unusually bythe perturbed lowest perturbed unoccupied molecular orbital. The calculatedon-off ratio of currents between the closed and open configurations is abouttwo orders of magnitude, which reproduces the essential features of theexperimental measured results. Moreover, we find that the switching behaviorwithin a wide bias voltage window is extremely robust to both substituting F orS for H or O and varying end anchoring atoms from S to Se and Te.

However, the standard model, which includes the Higgs mechanism, still leaves many unanswered questions. By introducing right-handed neutrinos into the Higgs sector, we provide a mechanism for the generation of the mass of the neutrinos by the seesaw mechanism. This paper proposes a theoretical framework that extends the standard model by introducing right-handed neutrinos and a higher-dimensional operator at the electroweak scale. We investigate the phenomenological implications of this extended framework, focusing on the production and decay rates of the Higgs boson at the LHC and future colliders. We also examine the potential effects on the neutrino oscillation experiments and the implications for dark matter. Our results contribute to the ongoing efforts to understand the nature of the Higgs boson and its connections to the physics of the neutrinos and physics beyond the standard model.

Spatial Characteristics of Joint Application Netowrks in Japanese Patents Abstract This study investigates the spatial characteristics of joint application networks in Japanese patents. Using a dataset of 1.4 million Japanese patents granted between 1976 and 2016, we construct a joint application network in which nodes represent patent applications and edges represent joint applications between them. We then analyze the spatial distribution of the nodes and edges in this network. Our results displaying that the joint application network is highly clustered, with densely connected regions correspond to major technological fields. We also find that the network exhibits a hierarchical structure, with larger clusters of joint applications sur rounded by smaller clusters. These findings propose that joint applications play an important role in the diffusion of technology travers firms and regions in Japan.

The correlation between star formation and 21cm emission during the reionization epoch is investigated. We use a semi-numerical model to calculate the 21cm brightness temperature and the star formation rate density. We find that the two quantities are strongly correlated, with the 21cm emission being brighter in regions of higher star formation rate density. This correlation is caused by the fact that both star formation and 21cm emission are tracers of the underlying dark matter distribution. The correlation is strongest on small scales, where the star formation and 21cm emission are more closely related to the local density field. On large scales, the correlation is weaker, as the 21cm emission is more affected by the large-scale structure of the Universe. Our results suggest that the 21cm emission can be used to trace the history of star formation during the reionization epoch.

This study investigates the presence of exoplanets orbiting three retired A-type stars, now intermediate-mass subgiants, using a combination of radial velocity and transit observations. The stars, identified as HD 181433, HD 190407, and HD 209248, have evolved off the main sequence and offer a unique opportunity to explore the planetary systems that surround them. Our analysis reveals the presence of multiple exoplanets in the systems, with masses ranging from super-Earth to gas giant. The orbital periods of these planets span several days to several weeks, and their distances from their host stars range from 0.1 to 1.5 AU. Our findings suggest that retired A stars can host diverse planetary systems, including both terrestrial and gas giant planets, which challenges the conventional view that these stars are unlikely to harbor planets. The discovery of these exoplanets has significant implications for our understanding of planetary formation and evolution, particularly in the context of intermediate-mass stars. Future studies of retired A stars and their planetary companions will help to further illuminate the complex processes that shape the architecture of exoplanetary systems.

The article provides an analysis of the unique Type Ib supernova (SN) 2005bf based on optical and near-infrared spectroscopy obtained at nebular phases, which is about one year after the explosion. SN 2005bf is similar to the Type Ic SN 1994I, and was initially considered to be an SN Ib/c, i.e. a member of a subclass of SNe Ib that might be the less luminous counterparts of SNe Ic, which themselves resemble gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). However, the authors find that SN 2005bf is more akin to typical SNe Ib, which supports the view that SNe Ib/c are not the low-luminosity counterparts of SNe Ic and GRBs. The progenitor system of SN 2005bf is inferred to consist of a Wolf-Rayet star, losing mass via a strong wind, and a compact companion in a binary system. The compact companion could be either a neutron star or a black hole, with the latter being favored since no hydrogen lines from the secondary are observed in the spectrum of the system. The presence of an He-rich circumstellar medium (CSM) as well as the high expansion velocity indicate that a strong interaction between the ejecta and the CSM takes place in SN 2005bf. The magnetic field (B) of the central neutron star (NS) formed in SN 2005bf is estimated to be as high as ~3*10^14 G if the spin-down luminosity of the pulsar is powered by the rotational energy of the NS. The ejecta mass of SN 2005bf is estimated to be 1.8 Msun, with a kinetic energy of (0.9-3.8) x 10^51 erg. Finally, the authors suggest that the lack of hydrogen observed in SN 2005bf can be naturally explained if the secondary in the progenitor system is a black hole rather than a neutron star or a helium star, and if mass stripping is efficient.

The expansion of ionization fronts in uniform and spherically symmetricpower-law density distributions is a well-studied topic. However, in manysituations, such as a star formed at the edge of a molecular cloud core, anoffset power-law density distribution would be more appropriate. In this papera few of the main issues of the formation and expansion of HII regions in suchmedia are outlined and results are presented for the particular cases where theunderlying power laws are 1/r^2 and 1/r^3. A simple criterion is developed fordetermining whether the initial photoionized region will be unbounded, whichdepends on the power-law exponent and the ratio of the equivalent Stroemgrenradius produced by the star in a uniform medium to the stellar offset distance.In the expansion stage, the ionized volumes will eventually become unboundedunless pressure balance with the external medium is reached before theionization front velocity becomes supersonic with respect to the ionized gas.

The angular anisotropy of the fusion-fission and quasifission fragments is computation within the framework of the statistical multifragmentation model. The calculations have been performed for a wide gamut of the excitation energy and the fragment mass. The results of calculate possesses been compared with the experimental data for the fusion-fission of the 56Fe+56Fe system at the excitation energy of 260 MeV/nucleon. The calculated and experimental data are in a good compact.

Energy injection into the early universe can induce turbulent motions of theprimordial plasma, which in turn act as a source for gravitational radiation.Earlier work computed the amplitude and characteristic frequency of the relicgravitational wave background, as a function of the total energy injected andthe stirring scale of the turbulence. This paper computes the frequencyspectrum of relic gravitational radiation from a turbulent source of thestationary Kolmogoroff form which acts for a given duration, making no otherapproximations. We also show that the limit of long source wavelengths,commonly employed in aeroacoustic problems, is an excellent approximation. Thegravitational waves from cosmological turbulence around the electroweak energyscale will be detectable by future space-based laser interferometers for asubstantial range of turbulence parameters.

RX J1117.4+0743, also known as [VMF 98] 097, is a galaxy cluster located at a redshift of z=0.485, which has been observed through a combination of optical and X-ray observations. The optical data, collected using the Hubble Space Telescope, reveal a complex structure of galaxies and galaxy clusters in the vicinity of RX J1117.4+0743, while the X-ray observations, made with the Chandra X-ray Observatory, show a diffuse emission that is spatially correlated with the optical data. The X-ray data indicate a high temperature of kT=8.6+/-0.5 keV, suggesting the presence of a large amount of hot gas in the cluster, with a luminosity of L_X=2.4x10^44 erg/s, which is typical for a galaxy cluster of this size and redshift. The observations are consistent with the presence of a galaxy cluster with a mass of approximately 10^14 solar masses. The galaxy distribution within the cluster is found to be irregular, with several substructures and galaxy streams. The color-magnitude diagram of the galaxies in the cluster shows a clear red sequence, indicating that the galaxies are mostly old and passively evolving, while the presence of bluer galaxies suggests recent star formation activity. The distribution of the galaxies in the cluster is centrally concentrated, with a surface density that decreases with increasing distance from the center, and the galaxy velocity dispersion is consistent with the mass of the cluster, indicating that the galaxies are dynamically relaxed. The X-ray and optical properties of RX J1117.4+0743 are consistent with those of other galaxy clusters at similar redshifts, but the detailed structure of the cluster suggests that it may be in the process of forming, with ongoing mergers and accretion of galaxies.

We have observed the BL Lac object 1ES2344+514 (z = 0.044) in Very HighEnergy (VHE) gamma-ray and near-infrared wavelength bands with TACTIC and MIROtelescopes respectively. The observations were made from 18th October to 9thDecember 2004 and 27th October 2005 to 1st January 2006. Detailed analysis ofthe TACTIC data indicates absence of a statistically significant gamma-raysignal both in overall data and on a nightly basis from the source direction.We estimate an upper limit of I($\geq$1.5 TeV)$\leq 3.84 \times 10^{-12}$photons cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ at a 3$\sigma$ confidence level on the integrated$\gamma$-ray flux. In addition, we have also compared TACTIC TeV light curveswith those of the RXTE ASM (2-12keV) for the contemporary period and find thatthere are no statistically significant increases in the signal strengths fromthe source in both these energy regions. During 2004 IR observations,1ES2344+514 shows low level (~0.06 magnitude) day-to-day variation in both, J &H bands. However, during 2005 observation epoch, the source brightens up byabout 0.41 magnitude from its October 2005 level J magnitude= 12.64 to J =12.23 on December 6, 2005. It then fades by about 0.2 magnitude during 6 to 10December, 2005. The variation is seen in both, J & H, bands simultaneously. Thelight travel time arguments suggest that the emission region size is of theorder of $10^{17}$ cms.

The Setenrod problem asks whether every finitely generated graded commutative algeBra over a prime field can be realized as the cohomology ring of some space. In the 1950s, Steenrod conjectured that this was true for mod-2 cohomology. However, a counterexample was found by Adams in l960, disproving Steenrod's conjecture. Since then, progress has been made in understadning the restrictions on which polynomial algebras can be realized as mod-p cohomology rngs. In this article, we survey the current nation of the Steenrod problem and related questions, such as characterizing which algebras admit geometric representations as cohomology rings and whether topological methods can resolve outstanding algebraic questions.

The calculated electronic structures of the heme complexes are in good agreement with experimental data, and the DFT+U method is shown to be a reliable tool for studying the electronic structure and spin-state energetics of heme systems. The DFT+U method is able to reproduce the experimental spin-state ordering of a series of heme complexes, including both high- and low-spin states. The results of this study provide new insights into the electronic structure of heme and its role in biological systems. Keywords Heme; DFT+U; spin-state energetics; electronic structure; biological cofactors; heme.

The impact of the strongly attractive electromagnetic field of heavy nucleion electrons in quasi-elastic (e,e') scattering is often accounted for by theeffective momentum approximation. This method is a plane wave Bornapproximation which takes the twofold effect of the attractive nucleus oninitial and final state electrons into account, namely the modification of theelectron momentum in the vicinity of the nucleus, and the focusing of electronstowards the nuclear region leading to an enhancement of the corresponding wavefunction amplitudes. The focusing effect due to the attractive Coulomb field ofa homogeneously charged sphere on a classical ensemble of charged particlesincident on the field is calculated in the highly relativistic limit andcompared to results obtained from exact solutions of the Dirac equation. Theresult is relevant for the theoretical foundation of the effective momentumapproximation and describes the high energy behavior of the amplitude ofcontinuum Dirac waves in the potential of a homogeneously charged sphere. Ourfindings indicate that the effective momentum approximation is a usefulapproximation for the calculation of Coulomb corrections in (e,e') scatteringoff heavy nuclei for sufficiently high electron energies and momentum transfer.

Throughout this investigating, we employed molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the spatial scale of low energy excitations in a simple polymer system. We faced that the spatial scale of these excitations is strongly dependent on the energies of the excitation, with higher energy excitations exhibiting longer spatial ranges. We observed that the spatial scale of the excitations increases with mitigating energy, exhibiting a power-law relationship. Our results provide new insights into the understanding of the spatial properties of puny energy excitations in polymer systems, and have prominent implications for the development of new appliances with tailored properties. Apart, our findings demonstrate the utility of molecular dynamics simulations in studying the spatial scale of low energy excitations in polymers, and highlight the potential of this practices for investigating a wide range of polymeric regimes.

We present the results of spectroscopy of Lyman Break Galaxies (LBGs) at z~5in the J0053+1234 field with the Faint Object Camera and Spectrograph on theSubaru telescope. Among 5 bright candidates with z' < 25.0 mag, 2 objects areconfirmed to be at z~5 from their Ly alpha emission and the continuumdepression shortward of Ly alpha. The EWs of Ly alpha emission of the 2 LBGsare not so strong to be detected as Ly alpha emitters, and one of them showsstrong low-ionized interstellar (LIS) metal absorption lines. Two faint objectswith z' \geq 25.0 mag are also confirmed to be at z~5, and their spectra showstrong Ly alpha emission in contrast to the bright ones. These results suggesta deficiency of strong Ly alpha emission in bright LBGs at z~5, which has beendiscussed in our previous paper. Combined with our previous spectra of LBGs atz~5 obtained around the Hubble Deep Field-North (HDF-N), we made a compositespectrum of UV luminous (M_1400 \leq -21.5 mag) LBGs at z~5. The resultantspectrum shows a weak Ly alpha emission and strong LIS absorptions whichsuggests that the bright LBGs at z~5 have chemically evolved at least to ~0.1solar metallicity. For a part of our sample in the HDF-N region, we obtainednear-to-mid infrared data, which constraint stellar masses of these objects.With the stellar mass and the metallicity estimated from LIS absorptions, themetallicities of the LBGs at z~5 tend to be lower than those of the galaxieswith the same stellar mass at z \lesssim 2, although the uncertainty is verylarge.

In this study, we investigate the accretion processes in low-mass stars and brown dwarfs in the Lambda Orionis Cluster using data from the Spitzer Space Telescope. We analyze the mid-infrared excess emission in these objects, which is indicative of accretion activity, and find that it is significantly higher in brown dwarfs than in low-mass stars. We also find that the accretion ra te decreases with increasing stellar mass, consistent with theoretical predictions. Our results provide new insights into the formation and early evolution of low-mass stars and brown dwarfs, and highlight the importance of accretion in sahping their properties.

The charged-current quasi-elastic scattering of muon neutrinos on oxygentarget is computed for neutrino energies between 200 MeV and 2.5 GeV using therelativistic distorted-wave impulse approximation with relativistic opticalpotential, which was earlier successfully applied to describe electron-nucleusdata. We study both neutrino and electron processes and show that the reducedexclusive cross sections for neutrino and electron scattering are similar. Thecomparison with the relativistic Fermi gas model (RFGM), which is widely usedin data analyses of neutrino experiments, shows that the RFGM fails completelywhen applied to exclusive cross section data and leads to overestimated valuesof inclusive and total cross sections. We also found significant nuclear-modeldependence of exclusive, inclusive and total cross sections for about 1 GeVenergy.

Analogue models of gravity have been motivated by the possibility ofinvestigating phenomena not readily accessible in their cosmologicalcounterparts. In this paper, we investigate the analogue of cosmologicalparticle creation in a Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe by numericallysimulating a Bose-Einstein condensate with a time-dependent scattering length.In particular, we focus on a two-dimensional homogeneous condensate using theclassical field method via the truncated Wigner approximation. We show that forvarious forms of the scaling function the particle production is consistentwith the underlying theory in the long wavelength limit. In this context, wefurther discuss the implications of modified dispersion relations that arisefrom the microscopic theory of a weakly interacting Bose gas.

All core collapse supernovae are strongly aspherical. The "Bochum event,"with velocity components displaced symmetrically about the principal H$\alpha$line, strongly suggests that SN 1987A was a bi-polar rather than a uni-polarexplosion. While there is a general tendency to display a single prominant axisin images and spectropolarimetry, there is also growing evidence for frequentdepartures from axisymmetry. There are various mechanisms that might contributeto large scale departures from spherical symmetry: jet-induced processes, thespherical shock accretion instability (SASI) and associated phenomena, andnon-axisymmetric instabilities (NAXI). The MRI gives inevitable production oflarge toroidal magnetic fields. In sum: no $\Omega$ without B. The role ofmagnetic fields, non-axisymmetric instabilities, and of the de-leptonizationphase are discussed.

This paper presents a game-theoretic approach to study energy-efficient modulation in CDMA networks with delay constraints. A non-cooperative game is proposed where each user chooses their transmit power, symbol rate, and modulation constellation size to maximize their own utility while meeting delay QoS requirements. Utility is defined as the number of reliable bits transmitted per joule of energy consumed. The best-response strategies and Nash equilibrium for the game are derived. It is shown that users should choose the lowest constellation size that satisfies their delay constraint to maximize energy efficiency. The tradeoffs between energy efficiency, delay, throughput and constellation size are analyzed. Trellis-coded modulation is also discussed as an approach to further improve energy efficiency.
