We investigate the impact of the surrounding hot environment on the cool star's effective temperature and surface features, as well as the turnout of any possible deviations from typical stellar developments. By comprehensively studying the behavior of cool strs in hot places, this research unveils valuable insights into the intricate interplay between stellar atmospheres and their encircling environments, shedding light on the adaptability and resilience of these celestial objects.

This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the circumstellar Silicon Monoxide (SiO) maser emission in the star R Leo. R Leo is an extensively studied asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star situated at a distance of 120 parsecs from Earth. Employing high-resolution interferometric observations acquired from the Very Large Array (VLA), we have achieved an unprecedented level of detail in mapping the spatial distribution of SiO maser emission around R Leo.Our study reveals a complex and intricate morphology of the SiO maser emission, characterized by numerous distinct clumps and filaments surrounding the central star. We ascertain that the maser emission primarily originates from regions located at a radial distance of approximately 10-30 astronomical units from the central star, which aligns with previous observations.Furthermore, we examine the velocity structure of the maser emission and identify indications of radial expansion motions. The presence of these kinematic features suggests the existence of outflowing material and provides insight into the mass-loss processes taking place in the circumstellar environment of R Leo.Moreover, we investigate the polarization properties of the SiO maser emission and find that the majority of maser spots exhibit linear polarization. These polarizations align with the direction of the local magnetic field, indicating a significant influence of magnetic fields in the maser generation mechanism.We compare the observed SiO maser features with hydrodynamic models of AGB stellar atmospheres and circumstellar envelopes, enabling us to constrain the physical properties of the surrounding gas and dust. These findings provide valuable insights into the role of SiO molecules as tracers of the mass-loss phenomena occurring in evolved stars like R Leo.In conclusion, our meticulous mapping and analysis of the circumstellar SiO maser emission in R Leo unveil the intricate structure and kinematics of the maser regions.

Precise measurements of radio-frequency magnetic susceptibility are important for understanding magnetic properties in a wide range of materials. This study demonstrates a new technique for measuring radio-frequency magnetic susceptibility in (anti)ferromagnetic materials with high accuracy. The technique employs a precision coil setup capable of generating radio-frequency magnetic fields between 1 Hz to 1 MHz while also carefully measuring the magnetic response of a sample material. Tests on known (anti)ferromagnetic samples, including various nickel, cobalt and iron alloys, show the new technique can determine magnetic susceptibility to within 1% accuracy. The response is also measured as a function of both frequency and temperature to identify resonant phenomena and phase transitions in the materials. Possible applications include more precise characterization of materials for sensors, data recording media and related technologies requiring control and detection of magnetic signals. Furthermore, the frequency dependence provides insights into the dynamics of magnetization processes on short timescales. The high sensitivity also enables susceptibility measurements of very small sample volumes down to the microgram range. In summary, this novel and precise technique extends our ability to probe magnetic properties and holds promise for advancing the understanding and development of (anti)ferromagnetic materials.

The increasing interest in the Mueller density-matrix-functional theory hasled us to a systematic mathematical investigation of its properties. Thisfunctional is similar to the Hartree-Fock functional, but with a modifiedexchange term in which the square of the density matrix \gamma(X, X') isreplaced by the square of \gamma^{1/2}(X, X'). After an extensive introductorydiscussion of density-matrix-functional theory we show, among other things,that this functional is convex (unlike the HF functional) and that energyminimizing \gamma's have unique densities \rho(x), which is a physicallydesirable property often absent in HF theory. We show that minimizers exist ifN \leq Z, and derive various properties of the minimal energy and thecorresponding minimizers. We also give a precise statement about the equationfor the orbitals of \gamma, which is more complex than for HF theory. We statesome open mathematical questions about the theory together with conjecturedsolutions.

We study the spectral and energetics properties of 47 long-duration gamma-raybursts (GRBs) with known redshift, all of them detected by the Swift satellite.Due to the narrow energy range (15-150 keV) of the Swift-BAT detector, thespectral fitting is reliable only for fitting models with 2 or 3 parameters. Ashigh uncertainty and correlation among the errors is expected, a carefulanalysis of the errors is necessary. We fit both the power law (PL, 2parameters) and cut--off power law (CPL, 3 parameters) models to thetime-integrated spectra of the 47 bursts, and present the correspondingparameters, their uncertainties, and the correlations among the uncertainties.The CPL model is reliable only for 29 bursts for which we estimate the nuf_nupeak energy Epk. For these GRBs, we calculate the energy fluence and the rest-frame isotropic-equivalent radiated energy, Eiso, as well as the propagateduncertainties and correlations among them. We explore the distribution of ourhomogeneous sample of GRBs on the rest-frame diagram E'pk vs Eiso. We confirm asignificant correlation between these two quantities (the "Amati" relation) andwe verify that, within the uncertainty limits, no outliers are present. We alsofit the spectra to a Band model with the high energy power law index frozen to-2.3, obtaining a rather good agreement with the "Amati" relation of non-SwiftGRBs.

Transforming nonlocality into frequency dependence: a shortcut to spectroscopyThis paper presents a shortcut to spectroscopy by transforming nonlocality into frequency dependence. The key idea is to use a frequency-dependent kernel to represent the nonlocal interaction, which allows us to directly calculate the frequency-dependent response of the system. This approach is much more efficient than conventional methods, which require explicitly solving the nonlocal equation. We demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of our method by applying it to several model systems. Our results show that our method can achieve comparable accuracy to conventional methods, but with a much lower computational cost. This work provides a new tool for studying nonlocal systems and opens up the possibility of using spectroscopy to probe nonlocal interactions.

Resent works of Hawking and Susskind suggested that information is conservedin the universe. We extend this thesis and propose that dynamics of information- computations can conserve in Anti-de-Sitter cosmological model. Informationgeometry formalism is proposed to analyze information in dynamical systems. Weconsider entropy flow as a geometrical flow on statistical manifold and developa Dynamic Cores model to analyze migration of information in dynamical systems.Geometrical flow on the statistical manifold was considered as a transition oflocal dynamical systems in original d+1-dim AdS space to their delocalizedholographic representation in d-dim Conformal Field Theory (CFT). It was notedthat geometrical flow related to renormalization group flow and providesemi-conservation of informational invariants. Those invariants interpreted astypes of computations.

This study surveyed the universal concept of PP waves, and PP waves are a specific type of gravity wave solution. By analyzing the mathematical characteristics and physical characteristics of PP waves, we found a significant universality that should be expressed in different time and space dimensions and various conditions. Our analysis shows that some key features of PP waves, such as its invalid measurement, and curvatures, and the specific details of the solution will show consistent patterns. This versatility allows summary and prediction, which exceeds specific solutions that have so far studied. To establish this universality, we adopt a combination of analytical technology and numerical simulation. We first come to the general form of the measurement of PP waves and check its meaning. Subsequently, we explored our behavior under different disturbances and modifications to test universal robustness. Our discovery shows that despite being disturbed, the basic characteristics of PP waves are still stable, providing further evidence for observed universality. In addition, we have studied the connection between PP waves and other wave solutions, including plane gravity waves and vacuum solutions. Through comparative analysis, we have determined the common attributes between these wave solutions and established a unified framework to cover their similarity. This framework enables us to understand basic physics and predict the behavior of PP waves in various cases. Finally, we discussed our discovery of the meaning of a wider range of gravitational waves. The universality observed in PP waves shows that the mathematical infrastructure of managing these solutions is deeper, providing potential ways for future research.

The matrix product ansatz (MPA) is a powerful tool for investigating quantum many-body systems. Here, we apply the MPA to the six-vertex model, a fundamental model in statistical mechanics, and demonstrate its ability to capture ground-state properties accurately. Furthermore, the MPA provides insights into the excitations of the model. These findings highlight the potential of the MPA for studying a broad range of quantum many-body systems.

We consider gauge theories in a strong external magnetic like field. Thissituation can appear either in conventional four-dimensional theories, but alsonaturally in extra-dimensional theories and especially in brane world models.We show that in the lowest Landau level approximation, some of the coordinatesbecome non-commutative. We find physical reasons to formal problems withnon-commutative gauge theories such as the issue with SU(N) gauge symmetries.Our construction is applied to a minimal extension of the standard model. It isshown that the Higgs sector might be non-commutative whereas the remainingsectors of the standard model remain commutative. Signatures of this model atthe LHC are discussed. We then discuss an application to a dark matter sectorcoupled to the Higgs sector of the standard model and show that here again,dark matter could be non-commutative, the standard model fields remainingcommutative.

ZnO: Co nanoparticles were synthesized by a simple solution-based method. X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy confirm the formation of the ZnO:Co nanoparticles with a Wurtzite structure. The electrical transport measurements exhibit a metal-insulator transition (MIT) behavior for 5% Co-doped ZnO nanoparticles. The temperature dependence of resistivity suggests that the MIT is caused by the Mott's variable-range hopping conduction mechanism. The optical properties of the ZnO:Co nanoparticles were investigated by UV-vis absorption and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy. The UV-vis diffuse reflectance spectra exhibit a red shift of the absorption edge with increasing Co doping concentration, indicating the narrowing of the band gap. The PL spectra of the ZnO:Co nanoparticles show a strong emission peak in the visible region, which is attributed to the defect states introduced by Co doping. The results suggest that Co doping can induce ferromagnetism and a MIT in ZnO nanoparticles, making them promising candidates for spintronic and optoelectronic applications.

A critique of the singularity theorems of Penrose, Hawking, and Geroch isgiven. It is pointed out that a gravitationally collapsing black hole acts asan ultrahigh energy particle accelerator that can accelerate particles toenergies inconceivable in any terrestrial particle accelerator, and that whenthe energy $E$ of the particles comprising matter in a black hole is $\sim10^{2} GeV$ or more, or equivalently, the temperature $T$ is $\sim 10^{15} K$or more, the entire matter in the black hole is converted into quark-gluonplasma permeated by leptons. As quarks and leptons are fermions, it isemphasized that the collapse of a black-hole to a space-time singularity isinhibited by Pauli's exclusion principle. It is also suggested that ultimatelya black hole may end up either as a stable quark star, or as a pulsating quarkstar which may be a source of gravitational radiation, or it may simply explodewith a mini bang of a sort.

This article presents the discovery of a point-like very-high-energy (VHE) gamma-ray source located in the constellation of Monoceros. The observations were conducted using the High Energy Stereoscopic System (H.E.S.S.), a ground-based gamma-ray observatory. The source, designated as Monoceros VHE-1, exhibits a spatial extent of less than 0.05 degrees and displays a power-law spectrum with a photon index of Γ = 2.6 ± 0.2.The detection of Monoceros VHE-1 was made possible by employing a combination of data from multiple observational campaigns conducted between 2018 and 2021. The total exposure time accumulated amounts to approximately 150 hours, yielding a statistical significance of more than 10 standard deviations for the source detection. A comprehensive multi-wavelength analysis was performed, combining the VHE gamma-ray data with archival data from X-ray and radio telescopes. The counterparts at other wavelengths were identified, comprising a point-like X-ray source and an extended radio emission region surrounding Monoceros VHE-1. Detailed spectral and morphological studies were carried out, revealing intriguing features and potential connections with known astrophysical objects.Based on the observational results and theoretical considerations, several astrophysical scenarios are proposed to explain the nature and origin of Monoceros VHE-1. These scenarios encompass pulsar wind nebulae, binary systems containing a compact object, or shocks produced by the interaction of high-energy particles with the ambient medium.The discovery of Monoceros VHE-1 adds to the growing catalogue of VHE gamma-ray sources and provides valuable insights into the high-energy astrophysical processes taking place in the Monoceros region. Furthermore, it demonstrates the capability and scientific potential of ground-based gamma-ray observatories in advancing our understanding of the non-thermal universe.

The attractor mechanism implies that the supersymmetric black hole nearhorizon solution is defined only in terms of the conserved charges and istherefore independent of asymptotic moduli. Starting only with the near horizongeometry, Sen's entropy functional formalism computes the entropy of an extremeblack hole by means of a Legendre transformation where the electric fields aredefined as conjugated variables to the electric charges. However, traditionalEuclidean methods require the knowledge of the full geometry to compute theblack hole thermodynamic quantities. We establish the connection between theentropy functional formalism and the standard Euclidean formalism taken at zerotemperature. We find that Sen's entropy function 'f' (on-shell) matches thezero temperature limit of the Euclidean action. Moreover, Sen's near horizonangular and electric fields agree with the chemical potentials that are definedfrom the zero-temperature limit of the Euclidean formalism.

The stability of large-scale magnetic fields in rotating stars is explored,using 3D numerical hydrodynamics to follow the evolution of an initial poloidalfield. It is found that the field is subject to an instability, locatedinitially on the magnetic equator, whereby the gas is displaced in a directionparallel to the magnetic axis. If the magnetic axis is parallel to the rotationaxis, the rotation does not affect the initial linear growth of theinstability, but does restrict the growth of the instability outside of theequatorial zone. The magnetic energy decays on a timescale which is a functionof the Alfv\'en crossing time and the rotation speed, but short compared to anyevolutionary timescale. No evidence is found for a possible stable end state toevolve from an initial axisymmetric poloidal field. The field of an obliquerotator is similarly unstable, in both cases regardless of the rotation speed.

We consider a brane world in an arbitrary number of dimensions without Z_2symmetry and derive the effective Einstein equation on the brane, where itsright-hand side is given by the matter on the brane and the curvature in thebulk. This is achieved by first deriving the junction conditions for a non-Z_2symmetric brane and second solving the Gauss equation, which relates the meanextrinsic curvature of the brane to the curvature in the bulk, with respect tothe mean extrinsic curvature. The latter corresponds to formulating an explicitjunction condition on the mean of the extrinsic curvature, analogue to theIsrael junction condition for the jump of the extrinsic curvature. We find thatthere appears a new type of an effective anisotropic fluid on the right-handside of the effective Einstein equation due to the fact that there is no Z_2symmetry. The derived equation is a basic equation for the study ofKaluza-Klein brane worlds in which some dimensions on the brane arecompactified or for a regularization scheme for a higher codimension braneworld, where the Kaluza-Klein compactification on the brane is regarded as ameans to regularize the uncontrollable spacetime singularity caused by thehigher codimension brane.

In this article, we explore the concept of exact fzuzy sphere thermodynamics in the context of matrix quantum mechanics. We begin by introducing the fundamental pirnciples of matrix quantum mechanics and its connection to fuzzy spheres. We then delve into the thermodynamic properties of hazy spheres, specifisally examining the entropy and internal energy of these systems. Using rigorous mathematical techniques, we derive expressions for the thermodynamic properties of fuzzy spheres in terms of their matrix dimensions. Our results provide valuable insights into the behavior of fuzzy spheres at the quantum level, and have important implications for the examining of quantum thermodynamics. We conclude by discussing the potential applications of our findings in various fields, including quantum information theory and condensed matter physics.

We provide a new estimate of the local supermassive black hole mass functionusing (i) the empirical relation between supermassive black hole mass and theSersic index of the host spheroidal stellar system and (ii) the measured(spheroid) Sersic indices drawn from 10k galaxies in the Millennium GalaxyCatalogue. The observational simplicity of our approach, and the directmeasurements of the black hole predictor quantity, i.e. the Sersic index, forboth elliptical galaxies and the bulges of disc galaxies makes itstraightforward to estimate accurate black hole masses in early- and late-typegalaxies alike. We have parameterised the supermassive black hole mass functionwith a Schechter function and find, at the low-mass end, a logarithmic slope(1+alpha) of ~0.7 for the full galaxy sample and ~1.0 for the early-type galaxysample. Considering spheroidal stellar systems brighter than M_B = -18 mag, andintegrating down to black hole masses of 10^6 M_sun, we find that the localmass density of supermassive black holes in early-type galaxies rho_{bh,early-type} = (3.5+/-1.2) x 10^5 h^3_{70} M_sun Mpc^{-3}, and in late-typegalaxies rho_{bh, late-type} = (1.0+/-0.5) x 10^5 h^3_{70} M_sun Mpc^{-3}. Theuncertainties are derived from Monte Carlo simulations which includeuncertainties in the M_bh-n relation, the catalogue of Sersic indices, thegalaxy weights and Malmquist bias. The combined, cosmological, supermassiveblack hole mass density is thus Omega_{bh, total} = (3.2+/-1.2) x 10^{-6} h_70.That is, using a new and independent method, we conclude that (0.007+/-0.003)h^3_{70} per cent of the universe's baryons are presently locked up insupermassive black holes at the centres of galaxies.

This paper presents a new approach to clustering the co-occurrence of the most frequent patterns in a stream. The co-occurrence relationship between the patterns is represented as a graph structure. Then a graph clustering algorithm is adapted to group similar patterns based on their co-occurrence links. The clustering is fully incremental and can dynamically update the clustering as new windows of data arrive. This allows the patterns in the stream to be grouped according to their common attributes and their temporal behavior. The memory and time complexity of the clustering is analyzed, and several parameter sensitivity tests are performed to understand the impact of the clustering quality. An experimental evaluation shows that the clustering can effectively discover meaningful groups of patterns in both synthetic and real data streams. The proposed approach provides an effective way to analyze and monitor the evolving patterns in high-speed streams. Finally, the potential applications of the clustered patterns in ranking, classification, and anomaly detection are discussed.

In the context of brane-world cosmology, assisted chaotic inflation is a novel paradigm that reconciles the divergent observations of the cosmic microwave background radiation and the large-scale structure of the universe. By invoking a braneworld scenario, where our universe is a four-dimensional brane embedded in a higher-dimensional bulk, we demonstrate that the observed accelerated expansion of the universe can be attributed to the interaction between the brane and the bulk. Through a series of numerical simulations, we show that the assisted chaotic inflation model can produce a viable cosmology that is consistent with current observational data. Our findings offer a fresh perspective on the origins of the universe and highlight the potential of brane-world cosmology as a promising avenue for understanding the early universe.

In this study, we investigate the spin-orbit scattering length in narrow Al_xGa_{1-x}N/GaN wires using a recursively Green's function approach. We find that the spin-orbit scattering length is significantly enhanced in these wires compared to bulk AlGaN. The enhancement is attributed to the increased spin-orbit coupling in the narrow wires, which arises from the confinement of electrons in the transverse direction. We observe that the spin-orbit scattering length increases as the wire width decreases, and reaches a maximum value at a wire width of approximately 100 nm. Further reduction of the wire width leads to a decrease in the spin-orbit scattering length. The enhanced spin-orbit scattering length in these narrow wires has important implications for the development of spintronic devices, as it can improve the efficiency of spin-based phenomena such as weak antilocalization.

This article investigates the Al'tshuler-Aronov remedial to the conductivity of a large metallic square network. The Al'tshuler-Aronov correction is a phenomenon in mesoscopic physics that puts due to electron-electron interactions in disordered systems. The inquiry focuses on a large metallic square network, which consists of an array of metallic squares interconnected by generates. Using theoretical calculations and numerical simulations, the backers evaluation the impact of the Al'tshuler-Aronov correction on the overall conductivity of the network. They analyze various parameters such as the system stature, disorder strength, and electron-electron interaction strength to understand their influence on the hone. The results showed that the Al'tshuler-Aronov correction very affects the conductivity of the large metallic square network, leading to deviations from the classical conductivity predictions. This research contributes to the understanding of mesoscopic systems and provides beneficial insights into the behavior of electron-electron interactions in large metallic webs. The findings possessed potential implications in the design and optimization of electronic devices based on mesoscopic structures.

The crossover between an impurity band (IB) and a valence band (VB) regime asa function of the magnetic impurity concentration in models for dilutedmagnetic semiconductors (DMS) is studied systematically by taking intoconsideration the Coulomb attraction between the carriers and the magneticimpurities. The density of states and the ferromagnetic transition temperatureof a Spin-Fermion model applied to DMS are evaluated using Dynamical Mean-FieldTheory (DMFT) and Monte Carlo (MC) calculations. It is shown that the additionof a square-well-like attractive potential can generate an IB at small enoughMn doping $x$ for values of the $p-d$ exchange $J$ that are not strong enoughto generate one by themselves. We observe that the IB merges with the VB when$x >= x_c$ where $x_c$ is a function of $J$ and the Coulomb attraction strength$V$. Using MC calculations, we demonstrate that the range of the Coulombattraction plays an important role. While the on-site attraction, that has beenused in previous numerical simulations, effectively renormalizes $J$ for allvalues of $x$, an unphysical result, a nearest-neighbor range attractionrenormalizes $J$ only at very low dopings, i.e., until the bound holes wavefunctions start to overlap. Thus, our results indicate that the Coulombattraction can be neglected to study Mn doped GaSb, GaAs, and GaP in therelevant doping regimes, but it should be included in the case of Mn doped GaNthat is expected to be in the IB regime.

This paper presents the analysis and design of an organic high-speed digital electro-optic switch. The switch is based on a novel electro-optic polymer material with a high refractive index and low absorption loss. The device has a simple structure and is easily integrated with other optical devices. The switch exhibits a high extinction ratio, low insertion loss, and a sub-nanosecond switching speed. It also has low power consumption, making it suitable for high-speed optical networks. Experimental results demonstrate the switch's good performance, suggesting its potential for future high-speed optical networks.

The quantum Zeno effect arises due to frequent observation. That implies theexistence of some experimenter and its interaction with the system. In thiscontribution, we examine what happens for a closed system if one considers aquantum Zeno type of question, namely: "what is the probability of a system,remaining always in a particular subspace". This has implications to thearrival time problem that is also discussed. We employ the decoherent historiesapproach to quantum theory, as this is the better developed formulation ofclosed system quantum mechanics, and in particular, dealing with questions thatinvolve time in a non-trivial way. We get a very restrictive decoherencecondition, that implies that even if we do introduce an environment, there willbe very few cases that we can assign probabilities to these histories, but inthose cases, the quantum Zeno effect is still present.

We present measurements of the masses of 20 X-ray luminous clusters ofgalaxies at intermediate redshifts, determined from a weak lensing analysis ofdeep archival R-band data obtained using the Canada-France-Hawaii-Telescope.Compared to previous work, our analysis accounts for a number of effects thatare typically ignored, but can lead to small biases, or incorrect errorestimates. We derive masses that are essentially model independent and findthat they agree well with measurements of the velocity dispersion of clustergalaxies and with the results of X-ray studies. Assuming a power law betweenthe lensing mass and the X-ray temperature, M_2500 T^alpha, we find a best fitslope of alpha=1.34^{+0.30}_{-0.28}. This slope agrees with self-similarcluster models and studies based on X-ray data alone. For a cluster with atemperature of kT=5keV we obtain a mass M_{2500}=(1.4+-0.2)\times10^{14}h^{-1}Msun in fair agreement with recent Chandra and XMM studies.

This study presents near and mid-infrared photometry of the Pleiades star cluster, obtained using the IRAC and MIPS instruments on board the Sptizer Sapce Telescope. The data reveal a waelth of new information about the cluster's stellar population, including the identification of several nouveau substellar candidate members. The photometry is used to construct color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, which are then used to identify objects with masses below the hydrogen-burning limit. The resulting list of substellar candidate members includes several objects that were not previously known to be members of the Pleiades. The study demonstrates the power of Hubble photometry for studying the low-mass stellar population in open clusters, and provides a valuable resource for future studies of the Pleiades and other nearby clusters.

Using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and Z-contrast imaging we havedemonstrated elongated nanostructure formation of fullerene derivative[6,6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) within an organic hostthrough annealing. The annealing provides an enhanced mobility of the PCBMmolecules and, with good initial dispersion, allows for the formation ofexaggerated grain growth within the polymer host. Spinfoam theories are hoped to provide the dynamics of non-perturbative loopquantum gravity. But a number of their features remain elusive. The beststudied one -the euclidean Barrett-Crane model- does not have the boundarystate space needed for this, and there are recent indications that,consequently, it may fail to yield the correct low-energy $n$-point functions.These difficulties can be traced to the SO(4) -> SU(2) gauge fixing and the waycertain second class constraints are imposed, arguably incorrectly, strongly.We present an alternative model, that can be derived as a bona fidequantization of a Regge discretization of euclidean general relativity, andwhere the constraints are imposed weakly. Its state space is a natural subspaceof the SO(4) spin-network space and matches the SO(3) hamiltonian spin networkspace. In this article, we explore the concept of algebraic cycles on the relative symmetric powers and the relating Jacobian of a family of curves. We presents a novel approach to studying these cycles, which allows us to gain new insights into the structure and properties of the underlying algebraic varieties. Ours results have important implications for the study of algebraic geometry and the geometry of algebraic curves, and we provide examples to illustrate the practical applications of our findings. Fruthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by applying it to several explicit families of curves, providing newest examples of algebraic cycles and shedidng light on the rich geometric structure of these varieties.

The compound LiHoF_4 exhibits a paramagnetic to ferromagnetic phase transition at low temperatures that can be tuned with an applied magnetic field. In this study, we investigate the phase diagram of the diluted magnetic system LiHo_xY_{1-x}F_4 for varying concentrations of magnetic Ho^{3+} ions. Using susceptibility and specific heat measurements, we map out the phase boundaries between the paramagnetic, spin glass, and ferromagnetic phases as a function of temperature and Ho concentration. We observe a spin glass phase emerging at low temperatures and Ho concentrations below x=0.167. Above this concentration, a ferromagnetic phase is stabilized with a critical temperature that decreases with decreasing x. The results are compared to theoretical predictions for diluted magnetic systems. Our measurements provide a comprehensive experimental phase diagram that elucidates the effect of dilution on the magnetic ordering in LiHoF_4.

We present the results of a Gemini Near-Infrared Integral Field Spectroscopic survey of young star clusters in the merging galaxy NGC 3256. The survey aimed to study the star formation history of the galaxy and to investigate the role of galaxy interactions in triggering starbursts. We observed a total of 20 clusters in the galaxy, including 7 newly discovered clusters, using the Gemini North telescope with the Near-Infrared Integral Field Spectrograph (NIFS). The clusters were selected based on their optical and near-infrared colors, which indicate youth and high masses. We derived the ages, masses, and extinctions of the clusters using population evolution models fitted to their spectra. Our results show that the clusters in NGC 3256 have ages ranging from 10^5 to 10^7 years, with the youngest clusters being located in the tidal tails of the galaxy. The masses of the clusters range from 10^5 to 10^6 Msun, with the most massive clusters being located in the central region of the galaxy. We found that the clusters have a high level of extinction, with A_V ranging from 1 to 4 magnitudes. Our findings suggest that the star formation in NGC 3256 has been triggered by the galaxy interaction, with the youngest clusters forming in the tidal tails. The extinction observed in the clusters suggests that the star formation is taking place in a dust-rich environment. Overall, our results provide new insights into the star formation history of NGC 3256 and highlight the importance of galaxy interactions in shaping the evolution of galaxies.

Context. Gas within a galaxy is forced to establish pressure balance againstgravitational forces. The shape of an unperturbed gaseous disk can be used toconstrain dark matter models. Aims. We derive the 3-D HI volume densitydistribution for the Milky Way out to a galactocentric radius of 40 kpc and aheight of 20 kpc to constrain the Galactic mass distribution. Methods. We usedthe Leiden/Argentine/Bonn all sky 21-cm line survey. The transformation frombrightness temperatures to densities depends on the rotation curve. We exploredseveral models, reflecting different dark matter distributions. Each of thesemodels was set up to solve the combined Poisson-Boltzmann equation in aself-consistent way and optimized to reproduce the observed flaring. Results.Besides a massive extended halo of M ~ 1.8 10^{12} Msun, we find aself-gravitating dark matter disk with M=2 to 3 10^{11} Msun, including a darkmatter ring at 13 < R < 18.5 kpc with M = 2.2 to 2.8 10^{10} Msun. Theexistence of the ring was previously postulated from EGRET data and coincideswith a giant stellar structure that surrounds the Galaxy. The resulting MilkyWay rotation curve is flat up to R~27 kpc and slowly decreases outwards. The\hi gas layer is strongly flaring. The HWHM scale height is 60 pc at R = 4 kpcand increases to ~2700$ pc at R=40 kpc. Spiral arms cause a noticeable imprinton the gravitational field, at least out to R = 30 kpc. Conclusions. Our massmodel supports previous proposals that the giant stellar ring structure is dueto a merging dwarf galaxy. The fact that the majority of the dark matter in theMilky Way for $R \la 40$ kpc can be successfully modeled by a self-gravitatingisothermal disk raises the question of whether this massive disk may have beencaused by similar merger events in the past.

We prove that the Neumann, Dirichlet and regularity problems for divergenceform elliptic equations in the half space are well posed in $L_2$ for smallcomplex $L_\infty$ perturbations of a coefficient matrix which is either realsymmetric, of block form or constant. All matrices are assumed to beindependent of the transversal coordinate. We solve the Neumann, Dirichlet andregularity problems through a new boundary operator method which makes use ofoperators in the functional calculus of an underlaying first order Dirac typeoperator. We establish quadratic estimates for this Dirac operator, whichimplies that the associated Hardy projection operators are bounded and dependcontinuously on the coefficient matrix. We also prove that certain transmissionproblems for $k$-forms are well posed for small perturbations of blockmatrices.

The results of quantitative analysis of word distribution in two fables inUkrainian by Ivan Franko: "Mykyta the Fox" and "Abu-Kasym's slippers" arereported. Our study consists of two parts: the analysis of frequency-rankdistributions and the application of complex networks theory. The analysis offrequency-rank distributions shows that the text sizes are enough to observestatistical properties. The power-law character of these distributions (Zipf'slaw) holds in the region of rank variable r=20 - 3000 with an exponent$\alpha\simeq 1$. This substantiates the choice of the above texts to analysetypical properties of the language complex network on their basis. Besides, anapplicability of the Simon model to describe non-asymptotic properties of worddistributions is evaluated. In describing language as a complex network, usually the words are associatedwith nodes, whereas one may give different meanings to the network links. Thisresults in different network representations. In the second part of the paper,we give different representations of the language network and performcomparative analysis of their characteristics. Our results demonstrate that thelanguage network of Ukrainian is a strongly correlated scale-free small world.Empirical data obtained may be useful for theoretical description of languageevolution.

Nonlinear kinetic theory of cosmic ray (CR) acceleration in supernovaremnants is employed to calculate CR spectra. The magnetic field in SNRs isassumed to be significantly amplified by the efficiently accelerating nuclearCR component. It is shown that the calculated CR spectra agree in asatisfactory way with the existing measurements up to the energy $10^{17}$ eV.The power law spectrum of protons extends up to the energy $3\times 10^{15}$ eVwith a subsequent exponential cutoff. It gives a natural explanation for theobserved knee in the Galactic CR spectrum. The maximum energy of theaccelerated nuclei is proportional to their charge number $Z$. Therefore thebreak in the Galactic CR spectrum is the result of the contribution ofprogressively heavier species in the overall CR spectrum so that at $10^{17}$eV the CR spectrum is dominated by iron group nuclei. It is shown that thiscomponent plus a suitably chosen extragalactic CR component can give aconsistent description for the entire Galactic CR spectrum.

Spinor quantum gases restrained in tightly focused laser beams exhibit novel collective phenomenon due to their confined quantum motion. This article investigates the stability of spinor Fermi gases confined in one-dimensional waveguides through theoretical mathematician and numerical simulations. It is reported that spin-exchange trauma between different atomic spin states can lead to phase separation of the atomic spin components. The derived stability diagram delineates stable and flimsy regimes reliance on the atom number, interaction strengths, and confinement geometry, providing useful directorate for experimental studies of spin dynamics in confined quantum gases.

This article explores the concepts of reduced phase space and toric variety coordinatizations in the context of Delzant spaces. Delzant spaces, characterized by symplectic toric manifolds, possess rich geometric and algebraic structures. The reduced phase space technique provides a powerful tool for simplifying the dynamics of these spaces by identifying key degrees of freedom and constructing a reduced symplectic structure. In addition, the toric variety coordinatizations offer an alternative approach to describing Delzant spaces, relating them to algebraic varieties defined by toric ideals. The article presents a comprehensive analysis of the reduced phase space method and toric variety coordinatizations, highlighting their respective advantages and applications in the study of Delzant spaces. The theoretical insights and practical implications provided herein contribute to a deeper understanding of the geometric and algebraic properties of symplectic toric manifolds.

This study introduces a novel approach for predicting the durations, amplitudes, and timings of future fifteen solar cycles through the utilization of historical solar activity data and advanced machine learning techniques. Accurately forecasting solar cycles is of utmost importance for numerous scientific, technological, and societal applications. To enhance predictive capabilities, our methodology combines the analysis of long-term solar cycle patterns with the application of deep learning algorithms. We gathered and preprocessed a comprehensive dataset encompassing centuries of solar activity observations, ensuring the mitigation of potential data gaps and inconsistencies.Training and validating our predictive model on this dataset yielded promising results, offering valuable insights for space weather forecasting, satellite operations, communication systems, and optimization of renewable energy production. These predictions enable stakeholders to make informed decisions and develop robust strategies in response to solar variability. Nonetheless, further research and refinement of the predictive model are necessary to improve the accuracy of long-term forecasts and delve into the underlying mechanisms governing solar cycle behavior.

I describe a Bayesian method to account for measurement errors in linearregression of astronomical data. The method allows for heteroscedastic andpossibly correlated measurement errors, and intrinsic scatter in the regressionrelationship. The method is based on deriving a likelihood function for themeasured data, and I focus on the case when the intrinsic distribution of theindependent variables can be approximated using a mixture of Gaussians. Igeneralize the method to incorporate multiple independent variables,non-detections, and selection effects (e.g., Malmquist bias). A Gibbs sampleris described for simulating random draws from the probability distribution ofthe parameters, given the observed data. I use simulation to compare the methodwith other common estimators. The simulations illustrate that the Gaussianmixture model outperforms other common estimators and can effectively giveconstraints on the regression parameters, even when the measurement errorsdominate the observed scatter, source detection fraction is low, or theintrinsic distribution of the independent variables is not a mixture ofGaussians. I conclude by using this method to fit the X-ray spectral slope as afunction of Eddington ratio using a sample of 39 z < 0.8 radio-quiet quasars. Iconfirm the correlation seen by other authors between the radio-quiet quasarX-ray spectral slope and the Eddington ratio, where the X-ray spectral slopesoftens as the Eddington ratio increases.

We present a novel comprehensive first-principles theoretical study of theelectronic properties and relative stabilities of edge-oxidized zigzag graphenenanoribbons. The oxidation schemes considered include hydroxyl, carboxyl,ether, and ketone groups. Using screened exchange density functional theory, weshow that these oxidized ribbons are more stable than hydrogen-terminatednanoribbons except for the case of the etheric groups. The stable oxidizedconfigurations maintain a spin-polarized ground state with antiferromagneticordering localized at the edges, similar to the fully hydrogenatedcounterparts. More important, edge oxidation is found to lower the onsetelectric field required to induce half-metallic behavior and extend the overallfield range at which the systems remain half-metallic. Once the half-metallicstate is reached, further increase of the external electric field intensityproduces a rapid decrease in the spin magnetization up to a point where themagnetization is quenched completely. Finally, we find that oxygen containingedge groups have a minor effect on the energy difference between theantiferromagnetic ground state and the above-lying ferromagnetic state.

This paper concerns the use of neural networks for predicting the residuallife of machines and components. In addition, the advantage of usingcondition-monitoring data to enhance the predictive capability of these neuralnetworks was also investigated. A number of neural network variations weretrained and tested with the data of two different reliability-related datasets.The first dataset represents the renewal case where the failed unit is repairedand restored to a good-as-new condition. Data was collected in the laboratoryby subjecting a series of similar test pieces to fatigue loading with ahydraulic actuator. The average prediction error of the various neural networksbeing compared varied from 431 to 841 seconds on this dataset, where testpieces had a characteristic life of 8,971 seconds. The second dataset wascollected from a group of pumps used to circulate a water and magnetitesolution within a plant. The data therefore originated from a repaired systemaffected by reliability degradation. When optimized, the multi-layer perceptronneural networks trained with the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm and the generalregression neural network produced a sum-of-squares error within 11.1% of eachother. The potential for using neural networks for residual life prediction andthe advantage of incorporating condition-based data into the model were provenfor both examples.

The question of a possible redshift-dependence of gamma-ray absorption due togamma-gamma pair production of jet photons in the accretion disk and BLRradiation field in strong-line quasars is investigated. For this relevantaspects of cosmological black hole and quasar evolution are applied to theexpected pair production opacity of GeV-photons in those sources. I demonstratethat for positively evolving and non-evolving accretion rates over cosmologicaltime, detectable gamma-ray optical depths originating within the AGN systemwill show a redshift-dependence in the LAT energy range with larger opacityfrom sources at higher redshifts. This introduces ambiguities in theinterpretation of spectral absorption features, and complicates approaches forestimating the evolution of the extragalactic background light by probing thegamma-ray horizon when using blazars whose external photon fields are involvedin gamma-ray production.

This paper presents a methodology for stabilizing discrete mechanical systems usign controlled Lagrangians. Fisrt, we introduce the discrete Lagrangian and Euler-Lagrange equations that govern the dynamics of mechWanical systems when modeled on a discrete time domain. We then propose a method to augmenu the Lagrangian with control input terms to influence the dynamics. The stabilization of the controlled Lagrangian system is investigated through Lyapunov ahalysis. sing this approach, we design control signals that guarantee asymptotic stability of the equilibrium for a simple Mass-Spring-Damper example. Finally, the results of numerical simulations validating the controlled Lagrangian stabolization method are provided.

OO Serpentis is a deeply embedded pre-main sequence star that went intooutburst in 1995 and gradually faded afterwards. Its eruption resembled thewell-known FU Orionis-type or EX Lupi-type outbursts. Since very few suchevents have ever been documented at infrared wavelengths, our aim is to studythe temporal evolution of OO Ser in the infrared. OO Ser was monitored with theInfrared Space Observatory starting 4 months after peak brightness and covering20 months. In 2004-2006 we again observed OO Ser from the ground andcomplemented this dataset with archival Spitzer obsevations also from 2004. Weanalysed these data with special attention to source confusion and constructedlight curves at 10 different wavelengths as well as spectral energydistributions. The outburst caused brightening in the whole infrared regime.According to the infrared light curves, OO Ser started a wavelength-independentfading after peak brightness. Later the flux decay became slower but stayedwavelength-independent. The fading is still ongoing, and current fading ratesindicate that OO Ser will not return to quiescent state before 2011. Theoutburst timescale of OO Ser seems to be shorter than that of FUors, but longerthan that of EXors. The outburst timescale and the moderate luminosity suggestthat OO Ser is different from both FUors and EXors, and shows similarities tothe recently erupted young star V1647 Ori. Based on its spectral energydistribution and bolometric temperature, OO Ser seems to be an early class Iobject, with an age of < 10^5 yr. The object is probably surrounded by anaccretion disc and a dense envelope. Due to the shorter outburst timescales,the viscosity in the circumstellar disc of OO Ser is probably an order ofmagnitude higher than usual for FUors.

This article investigates the prime spectrum of algebras of quadratic growth, shedding light on the intricate relationship between algebraic structures and prime numbers. The author's approach combines techniques from algebraic geometry and number theory, offering a unique perspective on the distribution of prime numbers. The article presents a detailed analysis of the prime spectrum, revealing novel patterns and properties that deepen our understanding of these fundamental mathematical objects. The results have far-reaching implications for various areas of mathematics, including algebraic K-theory and the study of elliptic curves. The author's work not only advances our knowledge of the prime spectrum but also opens up new avenues for research in arithmetic geometry. Ultimately, this article demonstrates the power of interdisciplinary methods in mathematics, fostering a deeper connection between seemingly disparate branches of the field.

This article presents a novel apprach to spin-independent dark matter searches using a CF3I-based SDD prototype. The prototype utilizes a combination of carbon fluoride (CF3I) and silicon driFft detectors (SDD) to detect and measure the energy deposited by aark matter particles. The CF3I acts as a converting material, converting the unclear recoils from the dark matter interactions into eletron signals that can be detected by the SDD. Thc prototype demonstrated improved sensitivity and resolution compared to traditional SDD-based detectors, makin it a promising approach for future dark matter searches.

We analyze a large trace dataset and identify the key characteristics of P2P IPTV traffic and examine its scaling properties using various techniques. Our results show that P2P IPTV traffic follows a power-law distribution in terms of session duration and a stretched-exponential distribution in terms of packet inter-arrival time. We also find that the traffic is highly localized in both time and space, with a significant fraction of packets belonging to a small number of popular streams. Our results have important implications for the design and optimization of P2P IPTV systems and highlight the need for further research into the underlying mechanisms and dynamics of this emerging technology. We also observe a strong correlation between the number of peers and the popularity of the stream, which suggests a hierarchical structure in the P2P overlay.

Globular clusters, dense stellar systems in our galaxy, have long been of interest for their unique properties and intriguing stellar populations. In this study, we investigate the possibility of the existence of exoplanets within globular clusters. By analyzing high-precision radial velocity data obtained from spectrograph observations, we aim to identify potential planets orbiting stars within these clusters. Considering the challenging environment of globular clusters, characterized by high stellar density and frequent stellar interactions, the presence of exoplanets poses interesting questions about their formation and survival mechanisms. Our analysis focuses on a sample of M dwarfs in globular clusters, as these low-mass stars are prime candidates for hosting exoplanets. We employ a combination of radial velocity techniques and statistical analysis to detect planetary signals and determine the occurrence rate of exoplanets in globular clusters. Preliminary results suggest that the observed M dwarfs in these clusters may indeed harbor planets, albeit with different characteristics compared to those observed in the galactic field. Furthermore, we discuss the implications of these findings for our understanding of planet formation and evolution in extreme environments. Further observations and detailed modeling will be needed to fully unravel the nature and properties of planets within globular clusters.

Gene duplication is an important mechanism for the evolution of regulatory networks. Previous models of gene doubling have provided insights but made limited assumptions about network structure and dynamics. We develop new computational layout of gene duplication that consider the topology and function of transcription factor regulatory networks. Our models begin with a core transcriptional regulation network and permissions for whole genome or single gene duplications. These duplication events are followed by evolutionary processes of loopholes through mutation of binding sites. We analyze how network structure and function changes in response to selective pressures on gene expression levels after duplications. Our results showed that gene duplications regularly lead to subfunctionalization or neofunctionalization of the encoded transcription factors and rewiring of regulatory interactions. Different topologies in the original network influence the amplitude and nature of rewiring following duplication. These new models provide a more realistic and detailed understanding of how gene duplication shapes the long-term modifying of regulatory buckets controlling development and physiology.

A basic question of protein structural studies is to which extent mutationsaffect the stability. This question may be addressed starting from sequenceand/or from structure. In proteomics and genomics studies prediction of proteinstability free energy change (DDG) upon single point mutation may also help theannotation process. The experimental SSG values are affected by uncertainty asmeasured by standard deviations. Most of the DDG values are nearly zero (about32% of the DDG data set ranges from -0.5 to 0.5 Kcal/mol) and both the valueand sign of DDG may be either positive or negative for the same mutationblurring the relationship among mutations and expected DDG value. In order toovercome this problem we describe a new predictor that discriminates between 3mutation classes: destabilizing mutations (DDG<-0.5 Kcal/mol), stabilizingmutations (DDG>0.5 Kcal/mol) and neutral mutations (-0.5<=DDG<=0.5 Kcal/mol).In this paper a support vector machine starting from the protein sequence orstructure discriminates between stabilizing, destabilizing and neutralmutations. We rank all the possible substitutions according to a three stateclassification system and show that the overall accuracy of our predictor is ashigh as 52% when performed starting from sequence information and 58% when theprotein structure is available, with a mean value correlation coefficient of0.30 and 0.39, respectively. These values are about 20 points per cent higherthan those of a random predictor.

This study uses the scratch density function theory (DFT) to calculate the electronic structure of Bafeo3. Due to its unique characteristics, such as huge magnetic and topological insulation, the electronic structure of the perovskite has attracted great attention. We use plane bases and projector enhanced wave methods to perform DFT calculations. Our results reveal the complex electronic structure with narrow band gaps and strong electronic correlations. We found that the electronic structure is highly sensitive to the choice of choosing related functions, which indicates accurately describing the importance of strong electrons in the system. Our research has a deeper understanding of the electronic characteristics of Bafeo3, which is essential for the design and optimization of advanced materials and equipment.

Study the state -symmetrical nucleus (IAN) state equation (EOS) in the framework of the relativity average field (RMF) model with hand -limited restrictions. Analysis of the influence of heterogeneous asymmetry and the density density of symmetrical energy on Ian's EOS. The calculated EOS is applied to the nature of the neutron star, such as symmetrical can be symmetrical when saturated density, non -compressed, and nuclear effective quality and pressure. Compare the results with the results of other theoretical models and experimental data.

Continuous Capillary Condensation: A Nozvel Method for Efficient Vapor-Liquid SeparationIn this study, we present a novel method for efficient vapor-liquiad separation, termed continuous capillary condensation (CCC). CCC utilizes a poroBs, continuous capillary structure to continuously condense vapor into liquid, resulting in enhanced separation efficiency and meduced energy consumption. The CCC method was tested using a variety of vapor-liqui systems, and renults showed a significant improvement in separation efficiency compared to traditional methods. The continuous capillary structure was found to be particularly effective in separating vapor-liquid mixtuers with low condensation rates, where traditional methods often struggel. Furthermore, the CCC method was found to be easily scalable, making it a promising solution for largeMscale industrial applications. Overall, our findings demonstrate the potential of CCC as a game-changNer in the field of vapor-liquid separation, with significant implications for energ efficiency, cost savings, and environmental sustainability.

Gravitational waves (GWs) from the inspiral of a neutron star (NS) orstellar-mass black hole (BH) into an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) withmass between ~50 and ~350 solar masses may be detectable by the plannedadvanced generation of ground-based GW interferometers. Such intermediate massratio inspirals (IMRIs) are most likely to be found in globular clusters. Weanalyze four possible IMRI formation mechanisms: (1) hardening of an NS-IMBH orBH-IMBH binary via three-body interactions, (2) hardening via Kozai resonancein a hierarchical triple system, (3) direct capture, and (4) inspiral of acompact object from a tidally captured main-sequence star; we also discusstidal effects when the inspiraling object is an NS. For each mechanism wepredict the typical eccentricities of the resulting IMRIs. We find that IMRIswill have largely circularized by the time they enter the sensitivity band ofground-based detectors. Hardening of a binary via three-body interactions,which is likely to be the dominant mechanism for IMRI formation, yieldseccentricities under 10^-4 when the GW frequency reaches 10 Hz. Even amongIMRIs formed via direct captures, which can have the highest eccentricities,around 90% will circularize to eccentricities under 0.1 before the GW frequencyreaches 10 Hz. We estimate the rate of IMRI coalescences in globular clustersand the sensitivity of a network of three Advanced LIGO detectors to theresulting GWs. We show that this detector network may see up to tens of IMRIsper year, although rates of one to a few per year may be more plausible. Wealso estimate the loss in signal-to-noise ratio that will result from usingcircular IMRI templates for data analysis and find that, for the eccentricitieswe expect, this loss is negligible.

We demonstrate gamut upshifting of laser pulses through relativistic ideals from a flying mirror. Two colliding laser pulses were used to create a thin foil that behaving as a relativistically boosted mirror. As the mirror airlifted towards an incoming infrared laser pulse at just under the tempo of light, its relativistic Radar shift caused the reflected light to be upshifted into the visible frequency range. Precision timing and geographic overlap of the colliding pulses allowed reflection to occur effectively from the accelerating mirror. Spectral analysis reassured the upshifted output reached frequencies almost double that of the input light. This technique shows potential for applications such as generating high harmonic light melt from tabletop laser systems. More experimentation are planned to refine the process and better characterize the interactions behind this relativistic photonic tennis demonstration.

This study presents Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) evidence that highlights a pronounced modulation effect on the Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) in BaCuSi$_2$O$_6$. Through the utilization of high-resolution NMR techniques in combination with theoretical analysis, strong spatial variations in the BEC order parameter across the crystal lattice of BaCuSi$_2$O$_6$ are demonstrated. The results uncover a complex interplay between the spin degrees of freedom and the lattice structure in this material, manifested by a distinct anisotropy and periodicity in the modulation pattern. Additionally, a correlation is observed between the modulation amplitude and the temperature, suggesting the significant influence of thermal fluctuations in the BEC modulation mechanism. These findings not only shed light on intriguing quantum phenomena in low-dimensional magnetic materials but also provide valuable insights for the future development of quantum devices involving BEC manipulation.

This article presents an investigation into the bounds that can be placed on the elements of quark mass matrices using measured properties of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) mixing matrix and current values of quark masses. The CKM matrix is a fundamental component in the Standard Model of particle physics, describing the mixing between quarks and their respective mass eigenstates. By exploiting the known properties of the CKM matrix and the current estimates of quark masses, we derive bounds on the elements of the quark mass matrices. Our results provide valuable insights into the structure of the quark sector and may have implications for the search for new physics beyond the Standard Model. Specifically, we find that the bounds on the quark mass matrix elements are strongest for the uppermost quark generation, and they are weakest for the lowermost generation. Our findings are in good agreement with previous studies and provide further support for the Standard Model framework.

This study employs the Zakharov simulation to investigate the spectral features of on-demand Langmuir turbulence in an inhomogeneous plasma. The investigation focuses on the behavior of the turbulence in the presence of an appreciable density gradient and its impact on the spectral properties of the waves. The study reveals that the density gradient induces a dependence of the wave properties on the wave number, leading to a breakdown of the usual assumptions of homogeneity. The simulations demonstrate that the turbulence exhibits a range of spectral features, including a blue shift of the spectral peak and an increase in the spectral bandwidth with increasing density gradient. The findings have important implications for the understanding of Langmuir turbulence in inhomogeneous plasmas, such as those encountered in tokamak edges and stellar atmospheres. The results suggest that the density gradient plays a crucial role in determining the characteristics of the turbulence and its impact on plasma transport and confinement. The study contributes to the development of a predictive model for Langmuir turbulence in complex plasma environments, which is essential for advancing our understanding of plasma behavior and performance in fusion devices. The findings of this study have significant implications for the optimization of fusion experiments and the development of future fusion reactors.

Performance of object-oriented database systems (OODBs) is still an issue toboth designers and users nowadays. The aim of this paper is to propose ageneric discrete-event random simulation model, called VOODB, in order toevaluate the performances of OODBs in general, and the performances ofoptimization methods like clustering in particular. Such optimization methodsundoubtedly improve the performances of OODBs. Yet, they also always inducesome kind of overhead for the system. Therefore, it is important to evaluatetheir exact impact on the overall performances. VOODB has been designed as ageneric discrete-event random simulation model by putting to use a modellingapproach, and has been validated by simulating the behavior of the O2 OODB andthe Texas persistent object store. Since our final objective is to compareobject clustering algorithms, some experiments have also been conducted on theDSTC clustering technique, which is implemented in Texas. To validate VOODB,performance results obtained by simulation for a given experiment have beencompared to the results obtained by benchmarking the real systems in the sameconditions. Benchmarking and simulation performance evaluations have beenobserved to be consistent, so it appears that simulation can be a reliableapproach to evaluate the performances of OODBs.

Ordinal regression is a extensively studied problem in the realms of machine learning and statistical modeling. This article introduces a pioneering neural network methodology to address the complexities of ordinal regression. The proposed model harnesses the capabilities of deep learning to effectively capture the inherent ordinal nature of the target variable. By incorporating convolutional and recurrent layers, the neural network architecture adeptly captures both local and temporal dependencies in the input data. Furthermore, a novel loss function is introduced, which appropriately considers the ordinal relationship between the predicted and true labels. Through extensive experimentation on benchmark datasets, the proposed approach demonstrates significantly superior performance compared to existing methods. The neural network approach to ordinal regression presented in this article shows great promise for diverse applications, such as sentiment analysis, customer satisfaction prediction, and medical diagnosis, wherein accurate ordinal predictions play a pivotal role. This work concludes by discussing potential avenues for future research and suggesting plausible enhancements to encourage further advancements in this field.

Brownian motion is the random movement of particles halted in a fluid (liquid or gas) resulting from their clashes with the fast-moving molecules in the fluid. This circulation is named after the botanist Robert Brown, who first observed the phenomenon in 1827. The movement of pollen grains in water is a classic event of Brownian motion. Brownian motion is a rudimentary process in personage that plays a vital role in many physical, chemical, and biological systems. The understanding of Brownian motion has led to big developments in various fields of science and technology. This includes fields such as statistical mechanism, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and nanoscience. In this article, we will revisited the diverse and undulating nature of Brownian motion. We will discuss the theoretical foundations of Brownian motion and its historical changes. We wishing also examine various applications of Brownian motion in different fields of science and technology. Furthermore, we will investigate the significance of Brownian motion in understanding insoluble rallies such as the behavior of biological macromolecules and the transport of particles in fluids. Through this exploration, we ambition to deepen our understanding of Brownian motion and its vital rolle in shaping our world. Finally, we aspiration reflect on the implications and potential future directions of research in the field of Brownian motion. We will analysis the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead for scientists and engineers working in this exciting and ever-evolving soil of study.

When ultrathin metal films are subjected to multiple cycles of rapid meltingand resolidification by a ns pulsed laser, spatially correlated interfacialnanostructures can result from a competition among several possible thin filmself-organizing processes. Here we investigate self-organization and theensuing length scales when Co films (1-8 nm thick) on SiO_{\text{2}} surfacesare repeatedly and rapidly melted by non-uniform (interference) laserirradiation. Pattern evolution produces nanowires, which eventually break-upinto nanoparticles exhibiting spatial order in the nearest neighbor spacing,\lambda_{NN2}.The scaling behavior is consistent with pattern formation bythermocapillary flow and a Rayleigh-like instability. For h_{0}\leq2 nm, ahydrodynamic instability of a spinodally unstable film leads to the formationof nanoparticles.

In this paper we examine the intertwining product and triangular action of Lie algebras. We define the intertwining product operation on the tensor product of two Lie algebras as the smallest Lie subalgebra containing the image of the canonical embeddings. Moreover, we establish that this intertwining product forms a cocartesian monoidal structure on the category of Lie algebras. We then prove that any triangular Lie algebra action induces a homomorphism from the intertwining product to the endomorphisms of the module along the action. Furthermore, we characterize when this homomorphism is an isomorphism and provide necessary and sufficient conditions. Applications of our results to representations of quantum groups are also discussed. Our work aims to further the mathematical understanding of the relationship between Lie algebras and their modules under triangular actions.

Relativistic X-ray emission lines from the inner accretion disk around blackholes are reviewed. Recent observations with the Chandra X-ray Observatory,X-ray Multi-Mirror Mission-Newton, and Suzaku are revealing these lines to begood probes of strong gravitational effects. A number of importantobservational and theoretical developments are highlighted, including evidenceof black hole spin and effects such as gravitational light bending, thedetection of relativistic lines in stellar-mass black holes, and evidence oforbital-timescale line flux variability. In addition, the robustness of therelativistic disk lines against absorption, scattering, and continuum effectsis discussed. Finally, prospects for improved measures of black hole spin andunderstanding the spin history of supermassive black holes in the context ofblack hole-galaxy co-evolution are presented. The best data and most rigorousresults strongly suggest that relativistic X-ray disk lines can drive futureexplorations of General Relativity and disk physics.

We clarify certain aspects and discuss extensions of the recently introducedstring D-instanton calculus (hep-th/0609191). The one-loop determinants arerelated to one-loop open string threshold corrections in intersecting D6-branemodels. Utilising a non-renormalisation theorem for the holomorphic Wilsoniangauge kinetic functions, we derive a number of constraints for the modulidependence of the matter field Kaehler potentials of intersecting D6-branemodels on the torus. Moreover, we compute string one-loop corrections to theFayet-Iliopoulos terms on the D6-branes finding that they are proportional tothe gauge threshold corrections. Employing these results, we discuss the issueof holomorphy for E2-instanton corrections to the superpotential. Eventually,we discuss E2-instanton corrections to the gauge kinetic functions and theFI-terms.

This study investigates the characteristic X-ray emission lines produced under the extreme conditions in the inner regions of accretion disks surrounding black holes. These lines offer a unique window into testing predictions of general relativity regarding relativistic effects in the realm of strong gravity. Using Chandra X-ray Observatory observations, we conduct X-ray spectroscopy of four stellar-mass black hole binary systems. Broad iron Kα lines are detected exhibiting asymmetric profiles consistent with an origin from the innermost stable circular orbit around the black holes. Detailed modeling of the line profiles reliably measures the spin of the black holes in these systems. Variations in the line shapes with source luminosity support the hypothesis that fluorescence in the inner accretion disk illuminated by a coronal source of hot electrons above the disk produces the observed lines.

In this article, we present the repercussions of a measurement of the rate of muon capture in hydrogen gas and the decide of the proton's pseudoscalar coupling $g_P$. The measurement was steered out using a beam of muons engender by the BBC/U70 accelerator at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory. The capture rate was assessing in a target of hydrogen gas at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. The data were analyzed using a likelihood-based pathways, elects into account the background from accidental coincidences and the signal efficiency. The resulting value of $g_P$ was shown to be (0.51 $\pm$ 0.17) GeV$^{-1}$, which is in good agreement with previous measurements and theorist predictions. The implications of this result for our understanding of the weak interaction and the structure of the protons are dealt.

We employ granular hydrodynamics to investigate a paradigmatic problem ofclustering of particles in a freely cooling dilute granular gas. We considerlarge-scale hydrodynamic motions where the viscosity and heat conduction can beneglected, and one arrives at the equations of ideal gas dynamics with anadditional term describing bulk energy losses due to inelastic collisions. Weemploy Lagrangian coordinates and derive a broad family of exact non-stationaryanalytical solutions that depend only on one spatial coordinate. Thesesolutions exhibit a new type of singularity, where the gas density blows up ina finite time when starting from smooth initial conditions. The density blowupssignal formation of close-packed clusters of particles. As the density blow-uptime $t_c$ is approached, the maximum density exhibits a power law $\sim(t_c-t)^{-2}$. The velocity gradient blows up as $\sim - (t_c-t)^{-1}$ whilethe velocity itself remains continuous and develops a cusp (rather than a shockdiscontinuity) at the singularity. The gas temperature vanishes at thesingularity, and the singularity follows the isobaric scenario: the gaspressure remains finite and approximately uniform in space and constant in timeclose to the singularity. An additional exact solution shows that the densityblowup, of the same type, may coexist with an "ordinary" shock, at which thehydrodynamic fields are discontinuous but finite. We confirm stability of theexact solutions with respect to small one-dimensional perturbations by solvingthe ideal hydrodynamic equations numerically. Furthermore, numerical solutionsshow that the local features of the density blowup hold universally,independently of details of the initial and boundary conditions.

This paper is concerned with embeddings of homogeneous spaces into Euclideanspaces. We show that any homogeneous metric space can be embedded into aHilbert space using an almost bi-Lipschitz mapping (bi-Lipschitz to withinlogarithmic corrections). The image of this set is no longer homogeneous, but'almost homogeneous'. We therefore study the problem of embedding an almosthomogeneous subset $X$ of a Hilbert space $H$ into a finite-dimensionalEuclidean space. In fact we show that if $X$ is a compact subset of a Banachspace and $X-X$ is almost homogeneous then, for $N$ sufficiently large, aprevalent set of linear maps from $X$ into $\Re^N$ are almost bi-Lipschitzbetween $X$ and its image. We are then able to use the Kuratowski embedding of$(X,d)$ into $L^\infty(X)$ to prove a similar result for compact metric spaces.

We re-analyze the direct $\jp$ production processes at the Fermilab Tevatronin view of the recent observation at the B-factories, where both $\jp$inclusive and exclusive production rates are found to be about an order ofmagnitude larger than the leading order estimates of non-relativistic QCD. Thecharm quark fragmentation to $\jp$, which is the dominant color-singlet processat high $p_T$, is normalized by the B-factory measurements. The processreceives further enhancement due to the charm sea contribution which has so farbeen ignored in most analyses. The Double Chooz near detector is a crucial component of the neutrino oscillation experiment, providing valuable information on neutrino interactions. In this study, we exploit the directional sensitivity of the near detector to enhance the precision of neutrino oscillation measurements. By analyzing the angular distribution of neutrino interactions within the detector, we demonstrate improved constraints on neutrino oscillation parameters, particularly in the case of non-standard neutrino interactions. Our results show that the directional sensitivity of the Double Chooz near detector offers a promising avenue for further advancing our understanding of neutrino physics. The observed patterns in the data provide valuable insights into the nature of neutrino interactions and their implications for the Standard Model. The analyses presented here demonstrate the potential of the Double Chooz experiment to shed light on the properties of neutrinos and their role in the universe. Our findings highlight the importance of continued research into the properties of neutrinos and their role in the universe, and underscore the value of the Double Chooz experiment in this pursuit.

This paper explores the connections between V-Langevin equations, continuous time random walks (CTRW), and fractional diffusion. We demonstrate that the stochastic processes generated by V-Langevin equations can be represented as CTRWs, which allows for a more straightforward computation of stochastic integrals. Our work bridges the gap between these seemingly unrelated concepts and facilitates the study of anomalous diffusion in various fields.

The AMANDA neutrino telescope at the geographic South Pole has been monitoring the Northern Hemisphere for muon neutrinos from gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) since 2000. During the period from 2000 to 2016, AMANDA did not observe any neutrinos in spatial and temporal coincidence with GRBs. We report on the results of this search and derive upper limits on the muon neutrino fluence from GRBs. We consider GRB models that predict a large flux of high-energy neutrinos. The resulting upper limits provide significant constraints on these models. The new upper limits are a significant improvement over the previously published limits from the AMANDA experiment.
